As, अयधत्, 'he sucked'. When it takes the alternative सिच्, then rule II. 4. 78. comes into operation, and we have अघात्, and अधासीत्, 'he sucked'. So also of ङि, we have अशिञिवयत्, 'he grew'. It also takes the अङ्, (III. 1. 58) and then its form is अश्वत्, or अश्वयीत्.

गुपेञ्छन्दसि ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ गुपेः, छन्दसि, (छ्लेः, चङ्, विभाषा, कर्तरि, लुङि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गुपेः परस्य छ्लेच्छन्दसि विषये विभाषा चङावेशो भवति ॥

50. After the verb गुप् 'to protect', चङ् is optionally the substitute of ङि in the Chhandas.

This rule applies where the root गुप् does not take the affix आय (II. 1. 28). As इमान् नो मिचावरुणो यत्, गुहान् अजुगुपतम् 'Mitra Varuna protected these our houses'. The other forms are अगोप्तम्, अगोपिष्टम् or अगोपाविष्टम्. In the secular literature, the latter three forms are used, but not the first.

नोनयतिध्वनयत्येलयत्यर्दयतिभ्यः ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, ऊनयति-ध्वनयति-एलयति-अर्दयतिभ्यः, (छ्लेः, चङि, छन्दसि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊन परिहाणे, ध्वन शब्बे, इल प्रेरणे, अर्व गतौ याचने च, एतेभ्यो धातुभ्यो ण्यन्तेभ्यः पूर्वेण छ्लेचङि प्राप्ते छन्दसि विषये न भवति ॥

51. After the causatives of the verbs ऊन 'to decrease', ध्वन 'to sound', इल 'to send', and अर्व 'to go or to beg', चङ् is not the substitute of ङि in the Chhandas.

Thus we have ऊनयाः in the Vedas; औनित् in the classical literature; so also ध्वनयीत्, ऐलयाः and अर्वयीत्; their classical forms being अधिध्वनत्, ऐलिलत्, and आर्वित्. See Rig Veda I. 53, 3, I. 162. 15. and Panini VII 2, 5.

अस्यतिवक्तिस्यातिभ्योऽङ् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्यति-वक्ति-स्यातिभ्यो, अङ्, (छ्लेः, कर्तरि, लुङि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ असु क्षेपणे, वच परिभाषणे, भूतावेशो वा, यथा प्रकृपने, चण्डिकावेशो वा, एभ्यः परस्य छ्लेचङावेशो भवति कर्णवाचिनि लुङि परतः ॥

52. After the verbs अस् 'to throw', वच् 'to speak', and यथा 'to speak', अङ् is the substitute of ङि, when लुङ् follows signifying the agent.

वच् may be either the root, or the substitute of भू (II. 4. 53) and so also यथा may be the root, or the substitute of चक्ष् (II. 4. 54). The root अस् belonging to the द्विष्वि or the Fourth conjugation, falls under the subdivision पुष्वि, and therefore it would have taken अङ् in the Parasmaipada

370

SUBSTITUTION OF CHLI.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 53-55]

by rule III. I. 55. The repetition is to indicate that it takes-अङ् in the Atmanepada also; as पश्चात (VII. 4. 17), अचोचत् and आख्यत्. In the Passive, we have पश्चात्तापम्.

लिपिसिचिह्वश्च ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ लिपि-सिचि-ह्वः, च, (च्लेः, अङ्, कर्तरि, लुङि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लिप उपदेह, सिच् चरयो, ह्वं स्वर्ग्याः एतेनयश्च परस्य, च्लेरङावेशो भवति ॥

53. After the verbs लिप् 'to paint', सिच् 'to sprinkle' and ह्वं 'to call', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि when लुङ् follows signifying the agent.

Thus अलिपत् 'he painted or wrote'; असिचत् 'he sprinkled'; and आहत् 'he called or challenged'.

आत्मनेपदेष्वन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्मनेपदेषु, अन्यतरस्याम्, ( च्लेः, अङ्, लिपि, सिचि, ह्वः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लिपिसिचिह्व आत्मनेपदेषु परतः च्लेरङावेशो भवति अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

54. After the verbs लिप्, सिच् and ह्वं, अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि, when the affixes of the Atmanepada follow.

Thus अलिपत् or अलिपत् 'he painted'; असिचत् or असिक्त 'he sprinkled'; आहत् or अह्वास्त 'he challenged'.

पुषादिद्युताद्युलुदितः परस्मैपदेषु ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुषादि-द्युतादि-लुद-इतः, परस्मैपदेषु, ( च्लेः, अङ् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुषादिन्यो द्युतादिभ्यः लादिभ्यश्च धातुभ्यः परस्य च्लेः परस्मैपदेषु परतो अङावेशो भवति ॥

55. अङ् is the substitute of च्लि, after the verbs पुष् 'to nourish', and the rest, द्युत् 'to shine', and the rest, and the verbs having an indicatory लु, when the affixes of the Parasmaipada follow.

The verbs classed as पुषादि, are a sub-division of the 4th conjugational verbs; and द्युतादि verbs belong to the 1st conjugation. As पुष्, अपुषत् 'he nourished'; द्युत्, अद्युतत् 'he shone'; गल्लु, अगमत् 'he went'. But not so in the Atmanepada; as व्यथोतिः, अलोतिः.

सर्तिशाशत्यर्तिभ्यश्च ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्ति-शास्ति-अर्तिभ्यः, च, ( च्लेः, अङ् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छ गतौ, शासु अनुशिष्टौ, क्र गतौ, इत्येतेभ्यः परस्य च्लेरङावेशो भवति ॥

BK. III. CH. I. § 56-58.]

SUBSTITUTION OF CHLI.

371

56. After the verbs स् 'to go', शात् 'to order', and क् 'to go', अङ् is the substitute of ण् in the Parasmaipada as well as in the Atmanepada.

Thus असत् 'he went'; अशिषत् 'he ordered'; आरत् 'he went'. This sutra has been separately enunciated in order to make the rule applicable to Atmanepada; as समरन्त (I. 3. 29). The च in the text is for the sake of drawing the anuvritti of the phrase 'in the Parasmaipada' of the last sutra, into the present and its anuvritti will extend to future sutras also.

इरितो वा ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इर्-इतः, वा, ( ण्, अङ् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इरितोभातोः परस्य ण् वेरडावेशो वा भवति ॥

57. अङ् is optionally the substitute of ण् after that root which has an indicatory इर्, when the Parasmaipada terminations are employed.

Thus from भिदिर् (भिव) 'to divide', we derive अभिदत् or अभैस्तीत्. But we have अभिन्न in the Atmanepada. So from छिदिर् — अचिच्चत् or अच्छैस्तीत्.

जुस्तम्भु मुचु ग्लुचु मुचु ग्लुचु ग्लुचु शिवभ्यः ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ जु-
स्तम्भु-मुचु-मुचु-मुचु-ग्लुचु-ग्लुचु-शिवभ्यः, ( ण्, अङ्, वा ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जु स्तम्भु मुचु ग्लुचु मुचु ग्लुचु ग्लुचु शिव, एतेभ्यो धातुभ्यः परस्य ण् वेरडावेशो भवति ॥

58. And, optionally अङ् is the substitute of ण् after the verbs ज् 'to grow old', स्तम्भ 'to stiffen' मुच् and ग्लुच् 'to go', मुच् and ग्लुच् 'to steal', ग्लुच् 'to go' and शिव 'to grow', when the terminations of the Parasmaipada are employed.

Thus अजरत् or अजारीत् 'he grew old'; अस्तम्भत् or अस्तम्भीत् 'he stiffened'; असुचत् or असोचीत् 'he went'; असुचत् or असोचीत् 'he went'; असुचत् or असोचीत् 'he stole'; असुचत् or असोचीत् 'he stole'; असुचत् or असुचीत् 'he went'; अश्वत्, अश्ववीत् or अशिश्ववीत् 'he grew'. The roots ग्लुच् and ग्लुच् both give rise to the same three forms, viz. असुचत्, असुच्यत् and असुचीत्. The use of one root would, therefore, have served the purpose. The employment of both indicates separateness of their meanings. Others say that the use of both roots indicates that in the case of ग्लुच्, the nasal is never elided. Thus the Aorist of ग्लुच् will be असुचत् and असुचीत्.

कुमुद्रुहिम्यश्छन्दसि ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ क-मु-दू-रुहिम्यः,
छन्दसि ( ण्, अङ् ) ॥

7

372

SUBSTITUTION OF CHLI.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 59-62.

वृत्तिः ॥ कृ मु इ रुहि इत्येतेभ्यः परस्य च्छोः छन्दसि विषये इङावेशो भवति ॥

59. After the verbs कृ 'to do', मु 'to die', इ 'to tear', and रुह 'to rise', अह is the substitute of च्छि when used in the Chhandas.

Thus अकरत् 'he did'; अमरत् 'he died'; अहरत् 'he tore'; आहहत् 'he rose'. See Rig Veda X. 85. 17, X. 44. 6. The classical Aorist of these verbs are अकार्पीत, अमृत, अहारीत, and अरुक्षत्.

चिण् ते पदः ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ चिण्, ते, पदः, ( श्लेः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पद गतो असाद्धातोः परस्य च्छोश्चिणावेशो भवति तद्वद्वे परतः ॥

60. चिण् is the substitute of च्छि after the verb पद 'to go', when the affix त follows.

The affix त here means the third person singular tense-affix of the Atmanepada; as अपादि 'he went'; but not so in the dual and plural; as अपसाताम् 'they two went'; अपसत् 'they went'; अद्+पद+चिण्+त=अ+पाद्+इ=अपादि (the affix त being elided by rule VI. 4. 104).

दीपजनबुधपूरितायिष्यायिभ्योऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥

दीप-जन-बुध-पूरि-तायि-प्यायिभ्यः, अन्यतरस्याम्, (श्लेः, चिण्, ते) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दीप जन बुध पूरि तायि प्यायि एतेभ्यः परस्य च्छोस्तद्वद्वे परतोऽन्यतरस्यां चिणा-वेशो भवति ॥

61. चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्छि, when त, the third person singular of the Atmanepada follows, after the verbs दीप 'to shine', जन् 'to be produced', बुध 'to teach or know', पूर 'to be full', ताय 'to extend or protect' and प्याय 'to smell'.

Thus अदीपि or अदीपिट 'he shone'; अजनि or अजनिट 'he was produced'; अदोधि or अबुद्ध 'he knew'; अपूरि or अपूरिट 'he was full'; अतायि or अतायिट 'he extended'; अप्यायि or अप्यायिट 'he grew'.

अचः कर्मकर्तरि ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अचः, कर्म-कर्तरि, (श्लेः, ते,

चिण् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अजन्ताद्धातोः परस्य च्छोः कर्मकर्तरि तद्वद्वे परतश्चिणावेशो भवति ॥

62. चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्छि when त, the third person singular of the Atmanepada follows, after a root which ends with a vowel, and when the object itself is spoken of as the agent.

A reflective verb is one in which the object is spoken of as the agent. In reflective verbs therefore, चिण् is employed after roots ending in

BK. III. CH. I. § 63-65.]

PROHIBITION OF CHLI.

373

vowels ; as अकारि कटः स्वयमेव 'the mat became made of itself. This is an optional rule (प्राप्तविभाषा). Therefore we have also अकृत कटः स्वयमेव ; similarly अज्ञाति or अज्ञादि केदारः स्वयमेव 'the embankment broke of itself.

But in verbs other than those that end in vowels, *i. e.* in those which end with a consonant, the चिण् is obligatory in the reflective voice, and not optional ; as अमेति कादम् स्वयमेव 'the wood split of itself'. So also in verbs other than reflexives ; as अकारि कटो देववत्तेन.

दुहश्च ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ दुहः, च, ( क्लेः, चिण्, अन्यतरस्यान्,

कर्म-कर्तरि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दुह प्रपूरणे, असात्परस्य च्छेशिणावेशो भवति अन्यतरस्यान् ॥

63. चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्छि after the verb दुह 'to milk', when it is used reflexively, and when it follows.

Thus अशेहि or अशुभ गोः स्वयमेव 'the cow milked of itself'. In verbs other than reflexive, the चिण् is compulsory, *e. g.* अशेहि गौर्गपालकेन 'the cow was milked by the cowherd'.

न रुधः ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, रुधः, ( क्लेः, चिण्, कर्म-कर्तरि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुधिर आवरणे, असात्परस्य च्छेः कर्मकर्तरि चिणावेशो न भवति ॥

64. चिण् is not the substitute of च्छि, after the verb रुध 'to obstruct', when used in the reflexive sense in the third person singular of the Atmanepada.

Thus अन्ववारुद्ध गो स्वयमेव 'the cow was obstructed of itself'. In verbs other than reflexive, चिण् is employed, *e. g.* अन्ववारोधि गौर्गपालकेन.

तपोऽनुतापे च ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तपः, अनुतापे, च, ( न, क्लेः,

चिण्, कर्म-कर्तरि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तप संतापे, असात्परस्य च्छेशिणावेशो न भवति कर्मकर्तरि अनुतापे च ॥

65. चिण् is not the substitute of च्छि after the verb तप 'to suffer', when used reflexively, and when the sense is that of experiencing remorse.

This prohibition applies even to the passive and impersonal voices of the verb तप् ; as अतप्त तपस्तापसः 'the ascetic performed austerity' ; अन्वतप्त पापेन कर्मणा 'he repented from evil deeds'.

चिण् भावकर्मणोः ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ चिण्, भाव-कर्मणोः, ( क्लेः,

चिण्, ते ) ॥

374

YAK, SAP AND SYAN.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 66-69.]

वृत्तिः ॥ धातोः परस्य चले भिक्षावेशो भवति भावे कर्मणि सश्च परतः ॥

66. चिण् is the substitute of चिण when न of the third person singular Atmanepada follows, denoting the action (भाव) or the object कर्म.

A verb is said to denote an action when it is used impersonally; and it is said to denote an object when used in the Passive sense. As अश्विनी भवता 'it was lain by you i. e. you lay'; अकारि कटी देववृत्तेन 'the mat was made by Devadatta'. The repetition of चिण् here is for the sake of distinctness.

सार्वधातुके यक् ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सार्वधातुके, यक्, (भाव-कर्मणोः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भावकर्मणो चिनि सार्वधातुके परतो धातो यक् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

67. The affix यक् comes after a root, when a सार्वधातुक (III. 4. 113) follows, denoting the action or the object.

In forming Impersonal and Passive verbs, this affix is employed in the conjugational tenses. Thus in Impersonal verbs आस्यते भवता 'you sit', राज्यते भवता 'you lie'. So in passive verbs; as क्रियते कटः and गभ्यते मानः. The क of यक् is servile, and prevents guna and vriddhi. This affix is also used in reflective voice (कर्मकर्षेरि); as क्रियते कटः स्वयमेव 'the mat becomes made of itself'.

कर्तेरि शप् ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तेरि, शप्, (सार्वधातुके, धातोः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तेवाचिनि सार्वधातुके परतो धातोः शप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

68. The affix शप् comes after a root, when a सार्वधातुक follows, signifying the agent.

In active voice, शप् is employed in the conjugational tenses. This affix, which is technically called a विकरण comes after roots of the भू class and after compound roots formed by सन् &c. (III. 1. 32). The indicatory श makes it a सार्वधातुक affix by III. 4. 113, the प indicates that the vowel has *anudatta* accent (III. 1. 4). As भू+शप्+तिप्=भू+अ+ति=भौ+अ+ति=भवति. (VII. 3. 84). So also पचति.

दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिव्-आदिभ्यः, श्यन्, (सार्व-धातुके, कर्तेरि, ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिव् इत्येवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः श्यन् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

69. The affix श्यन् comes after a root of the Divadi class, when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting the agent follows.

This debars शप्. The servile न of श्यन् is for the sake of accent (VI. 1. 197), showing that the *udatta* accent falls on the radical verb and not on the affix; and the indicatory श makes the affix sārvadhātuka; as दिव्+श्यन्+

BK. III. CH. I. § 70-73]

SYAN AND SNU.

375

तिप् = हीव्+व+ति (VII. 2. 77) = हीव्यति; so also सीव्यति. The *Divādi* verbs belong to the Fourth conjugation.

वा भाश-भ्लाश-भ्रमु-क्रमु-क्रमु-त्रसि-वुटि-लषः, (सार्वधातुके, कर्तरि, श्यन्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धारा-भ्लाश-धनु-क्रमु-क्रमु-त्रसि-वुटि-लषः, (सार्वधातुके, कर्तरि, श्यन्) ॥

70. The affix श्यन् is optionally employed in the active voice after the following verbs; धारा 'to shine', 'भ्लाश' 'to shine', 'धन' 'to whirl', 'क्रम' 'to walk', 'क्रम' 'to be sad', 'वस्' 'to fear', 'बुद' 'to cut', and 'लष' 'to desire'.

Thus धाराते or धारयते 'he shines'; भ्लाशाते or भ्लाशयते 'he shines'; धनति or धारयति 'he whirls'; क्रामति or क्राम्यति 'he walks'; क्रामति or क्राम्यति 'he is sad'. So also धरयति or धरयति; बुदयति or बुदति; लषयति or लषयति.

यसोऽनुपसर्गात् ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ यसः, अनुपसर्गात्, ( श्यन्, वा, सार्वधातुके, कर्तरि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यसोऽनुपसर्गाद्वा श्यन्-प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

71. The affix श्यन् is optionally employed after the verb यस् 'to strive', when it is employed, without a preposition, and when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

Thus धारयति or धरयति 'he strives'. But no option is allowed in आर्ययति, प्रथयति. The root यस् belongs to the *Divādi* class.

संयस्व ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सं-यसः, च, (श्यन्, वा) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संपूर्वाच्च यसेर्वा श्यन्-प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

72. The affix श्यन् is optionally employed after the root यस् 'to strive', when it is preceded by the preposition सन्, and when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

Thus संयस्वति or संयसति 'he strives'.

स्वादिभ्यः श्लुः ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सु-आदिभ्यः, श्लुः, (सार्वधातुके, कर्तरि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुन् अभिषवे इरवेवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः श्लुप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

73. The affix श्लु comes after the roots of Svādi class when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent follows.

8

376

SNU, SA AND SNAM.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 74-78]

This debars शप्. As सु+इनु+तिप्=सु+नु+ति=सुनोति 'he presses out'. These are roots of the Fifth class.

शुवः शू च ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शुवः, शू, च, (शुनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शुवः इनुप्रत्ययो भवति तत्सन्नियोगेन शुवः शू इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

74. And शू is the substitute of शू, and there is the affix इनु after it, when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

Thus शु+इनु+तिप्=शू+नु+ति=गुणोति 'he hears'; शृणुतः 'they two hear'.

अज्ञोऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अज्ञः, अन्यतरस्याम्, (शुनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अशू व्याप्तौ भौवादिकः अस्मादन्यतरस्यां इनुप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

75. The affix इनु is optionally employed after the root अश 'to pervade', when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

Thus अशणोति or अशति 'he pervades or obtains'.

तनूकरणे तज्ञः ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तनू-करणे-तज्ञः, (अन्यतरस्यां,

शुनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तक्षु त्वक्षु तनुकरणे, अस्मात्तनूकरणे वर्त्तमानादन्यतरस्यां इनु प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

76. The affix इनु is optionally employed after the root तज्ञ 'to bore or hew' when a sārvadhātuka affix denoting an agent, follows.

Thus तज्ञति or तक्षणोति काष्ठं 'he hews the wood'. But संतज्ञति वाग्भिः 'he cuts with speech'.

तुदादिभ्यः शः ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ तुद्-आदिभ्यः, शः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तुद् व्ययने, इत्येवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः शप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

77. The affix श is employed after the roots of the Tudādi class, in denoting the agent when a sārvadhātuka affix follows.

This debars शप्. The indicatory श makes this affix a sārvadhātuka affix. As तुद्+श+ति = तुद्+अ+ति = तुवति (I. 2. 4) 'he pains or torments'.

रुधादिभ्यः शनम् ॥ ७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ रुध-आदिभ्यः, शनम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुधिर् आवरणे, इत्येवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यो शनम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

78. The affix शनम् comes after the roots of the Rudhādi class, in denoting an agent when a sārvadhātuka affix follows.

BK. III. CH. I. § 79-81]

U, A AND SNA.

377

This debars शप्. The indicatory म् of the affix इनम् shows that the affix न is to be placed after the last vowel of the root; see Sūtra I. I. 47. As रध्+इनम्+ति=रध्+न+ति=रु+न+ध्+ति=रुणादि 'he obstructs'. So also मिनति 'he splits'. The indicatory श is for the sake of Sūtra VI. 4. 23.

तनादिकञ्च्य उ : ॥ ७९ ॥ पदानि ॥ तन-आदि-कञ्च्यः, उः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तनु विस्तारे, इत्येवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः कृपञ्च उपस्थयो भवति ॥

79. The affix उ comes after the roots of the Tanādi class and after the verb कृ 'to make' when a sārvadhātuka affix follows, signifying the agent.

This debars शप्. As तन्+उ+ति=तनोति 'he expands'; कृ+उ+ति=करोति 'he makes'. Though the root कृ is included in the list of the Tanādi verbs, for which see Dhātupātha, yet its separate enunciation in the present Sūtra is for the sake of making a restrictive rule with regard to this verb; that is to say, the root कृ is a Tanādi root only for the purposes of taking the affix उ; all the other operations of Tanādi verbs are not to be performed upon it. Thus the rule II. 4. 79. does not apply to कृ. Thus अकृत and अकृत्या; the सिन् elision being compulsory and not optional.

धिन्विकञ्च्योर च ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ धिन्वि-कञ्च्योः, अ, च,

(उः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हिनि धिनि जिनि प्रीणनाधोः कृति हिंसाकरणयोः इत्येतयोर्द्विरवोरुपस्थयो भवत्यकारशान्तादेशः ॥

80. The affix उ comes after the roots धिन्वि 'to please', and कृपिव 'to hurt', when a sarvadhātuka affix denoting the agent follows; and in these verbs अ is the substitute of the final इ.

The root धिन्व or धिन्व belongs to the Bhuādi class. Thus धिन्व + उ + ति = धिन् + अ + उ + ति = धिन् + उ + ति (VI. 4. 48) = धिनोति 'he pleases'. It might be asked, why there is no guna of the इ of धिन् by rule VII. 3. 86 which requires the base to be gunated before a sārvadhātuka or an ārdhadhātuka affix. The answer is to be found in Sūtra I. I. 57; the substitute of अ which is a blank, is like the former occupant (sthānivat), and thus prevents guna.

क्यादिभ्यः इना ॥ ८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रौ-आदिभ्यः, इना ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दुक्कीम् द्रव्यविनिमये इत्येवमादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः इनामस्थयो भवति ॥

81. The affix इना comes after the roots of the Kryādi class when a sārvadhātuka affix follows denoting the agent.

378

SNU, SNA AND SAYACH.

[BK. III. CH. I. 82-85]

This debars शप्. As क्री + इना + तिप् = क्रीणाति 'he buys'. So also घोणाति 'he pleases'.

स्तम्भुस्तम्भुस्कम्भुस्कम्भुस्कुम्भः श्लुञ्ज ॥ ८२ ॥ पदानि ॥

स्तम्भु-स्तम्भु-स्कम्भु-स्कुम्भु-स्कुम्भ्यः, श्लुः, च, (शना) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तम्भुस्तम्भुस्कम्भुस्कुम्भुस्कुम्भ्यस्तम्भ्यः श्लोयश्श्यो भवति श्लुञ्ज ॥

82 And there is the affix शना after स्तम्भ, स्तुम्भ, स्कुम्भ or स्कुम्भ 'to hinder', 'to be dull or insensible', 'to support', and स्कु 'to go by leaps', as well as the affix श्लु, when a sārvadhātuka affix follows, in denoting the agent.

As स्तम्भाति or स्तम्भोति, स्तुम्भाति or स्तुम्भोति, स्कम्भाति or स्कम्भोति, स्कुम्भाति or स्कुम्भोति, स्कुम्भाति or स्कुम्भोति. The first four of these roots are not found in the Dhātupātha and are to be found in the sūtras, and hence called Sāutra roots.

हलः श्नः शानज्भी ॥ ८३ ॥ पदानि ॥ हलः, श्नः, शानच्-है ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हल उत्तरस्य श्नामश्श्यस्य शानजादेशो भवति हौ परतः ॥

83. The affix शानच् is the substitute of शना after a root ending with a consonant, when हि follows.

The affix हि is the 2nd person singular of लोह or the Imperative mood. Thus पुष्य 'do thou nourish', गृहाण 'do thou take', from roots पुष्य and मह which end with consonants. But we have क्रीणीहि 'do thou buy'; here there is no substitution of शानच्, because the root ends with a vowel. The repetition of शना in the sūtra shows that शानच् is a mere substitute and not an independent affix.

छन्दसि शायजपि ॥ ८४ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, शायच्, अपि,

( हलः, श्नः, शानच्, है ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये श्नः शायजादेशो भवति शानजपि ॥

84. In the Chhandas, शायच् is also the substitute of शना after roots ending in consonants, when हि follows.

Thus गुभाय जिह्वा मधु, (Rig Veda VIII. 17. 5.) The affix शानच् is also employed; as बधान पशुन् 'kill the beasts'.

व्यत्ययो बहुलन् ॥ ८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ व्यत्ययः, बहुलन्, ( छन्दसि,

शवादयः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ व्यत्ययं विकरणाः शवादयो विहितास्तेषां छन्दसि विषये बहुलं व्यत्ययो भवति ॥

85. In the Chhandas there is diversely an interchange of the various vikaraṇas शप and the rest

BK. III. CH. I. § 86.]

AN.

379

which have been previously ordained under special circumstances.

The word व्याख्या means transgression of the fixed rule, or interchange, taking of two vikaraṇas at a time, and so on. Thus भेदति = भिद + शप् + ति instead of भिनत्ति from the root भिद 'to split', belonging to the Rudhādi class; e.g. शुभमस्य आण्डानि भेदति (Rig. VIII. 40. 11.) 'He (Indra) break the eggs (children) of Shushma; so also, जसा मरते पति: (Rig. X. 86. 11); here there is मरते = मु + शप् + ते) instead of भियते; the root मु belonging to the Tudādi class. So also there are two vikaraṇas at one and the same time, in the following. इन्द्रो वस्ते न नेषतु 'May Indra lead by this abode'; here there is नेषतु 3rd. per. sing. of the Imperative जोद् of the root नो 'to lead'; there are two vikaraṇas सिप् and शप् instead of नयतु = (नो + शप् + त्); इन्द्रेण युजा तद्वेषेण वृजम् (Rig. VII. 48. 1). The word तद्वेषेण (इ + उ + सिप् + शप् + अन) is the 1st. per. sing. of the Optative (जिह्) of the root इ, the classical form being तद्वेषेण or तोर्यस्म 'may we cross'.

In the Vedic literature we have many apparent irregularities with regard to the rules of declension of nouns, conjugation of verbs, application of Parasmaipada or Atmanepada affixes; rules of gender, person or tense, rules of interchange of consonants, or of vowels, rules of accent, rules relating to कृत् and तद्विष affixes and rules relating to the affixes included in the pratyāhāra यक् (III. 1. 22 to III. 1. 86).

लिङ्गशिष्यङ् ॥ ८६ ॥ पदानि ॥ लिङ्गि, आशिषि, अङ्, (छन्दसि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आशिषि विषये यो जिह् तस्मिन्परतरछन्दसि विषयेऽङ् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ दृगोरग्वक्तव्यः ॥

86. The affix अङ् is employed in the Chhandas when the affixes of the Benedictive (आशीर्विह) follow.

This debars शप्. The affixes of the Benedictive are ārdhadhā-tuka by III. 4. 116; but in the Vedas they are sārvadhāṭuka as well; see Rule III. 4. 117. The scope of the present rule is confined to the Benedictive of the verbs स्था, गा, गम्, वच्, वद्, शक् and रुह्; as उपस्थेयम्; सत्यमुपगेयम्; गमेन जानतो गृहान्, मन्त्र बोचेमापये; विषयेनो मनसि प्रवेष्टा; व्रतम् चरिष्यामि तच्छकेयम्; स्वर्गे लोकमारुहेयम्.

The affix अङ् is employed in the Chhandas after the verb दृग् in the Benedictive. Had there been अङ्, it would have caused *guṇa* by rule VII. 4. 16.; to prevent this, अङ् is ordained; as पितरंच दृगेयं मातरंच 'May I see the father and the mother'.

कर्मवत्कर्मेशा तुल्यक्रियः ॥ ८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्मवत्, कर्मशा, तुल्य-क्रियः ॥

9

380

REFLEXIVE AFFIX.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 87, 88.

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मणि क्रिया कर्म, कर्मस्थया क्रिया तुल्यक्रिया: कर्ता कर्मवद्वति ॥

87. The न denoting the agent, when the action affecting the agent is similar to the action which affects the object, is treated as if it were a न denoting the object.

This rule applies to reflexive verbs. "This direction implies the substitution for the operations incident to a tense-affix or न, denoting an agent, of all the operations, which fall to be performed when the tense-affix or न denotes the object. Hence there shall be the affixing of यक् (III. 1. 67) the employment of Atmanepada terminations (I. 3. 13), the substitution of चिण् for चिन् (III. 1. 66), and the treatment of the word as directed in sūtra VI. 4. 62." (Dr. Ballantyne). Thus भिद्यते काष्ठं स्वयमेव 'the wood splits of itself'; अमेहि काष्ठं स्वयमेव 'the wood splits of itself'.

When an action is participated by or affects the agent in the same way as is done by the object, the agent is treated like an object.

When in an object, though it stands as an agent, the action is perceived to take place as in an object, then that agent becomes like an object: and all grammatical rules applicable to the object apply to such an agent.

The word वत् 'like' in the sūtra signifies that the rules which apply to an agent also come into operation; thus भिद्यते कुसूजेन.

The word कर्मणा 'with the object' in the sūtra indicates that the tulya-kriya or similarity of action must be with the object, and not with the instrument or the location. Thus साध्वसिद्धिनन्ति 'the sword cuts well'; here 'sword' is not agent but instrument. So also साधु स्थाली पचति 'the pot cooks well'; here स्थाली is a location.

This 'karma-vad-bhāva, the passive-like-construction takes place only in cases of some verbs.

तपस्तपः कर्मकस्यैव ॥ ८८ ॥ पदानि ॥ तपः, तपः, कर्मकस्य, एव, (कर्मवत्, कर्तरि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तप सन्तापे, अस्य कर्ता कर्मवद्वति, स च तपः कर्मकस्यैव नान्य कर्मकस्य ॥

88. The agent of the verb तप 'to heat,' becomes similar to the object, only when the object is the word तपस् itself.

Thus तप्यते तपस्तपसः 'the devotee performs austere devotion'; but not so in उत्तपति सुवर्णं सुवर्णकारः 'the goldsmith heats the gold'.

न दुहस्तुनमां यक्चिशी ॥ ८९ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, दुह-स्तु-नमां, यक्-चिशी, (कर्मकर्तरि, कर्मवत्) ॥

BK. III. CH. I. § 89-91.] PROHIBITION OF YAK AND CHIN.

381

वृत्तिः ॥ वृह स्तु नम् इत्येतेषां कर्मकर्तरि यक्षिणो कर्मवद्भावापदिष्टौ न भवतः ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ यक्षिणोः प्रतिषेधे णिभ्रान्तिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रिमन्त्रि ॥

89. The affix यक्ष (III. 1. 67) and चिण (III. 1. 62) are not employed in the reflexive voice of the verbs वृह 'to milk', स्तु 'to fall in drops' and नम् 'to bow'.

The affixes यक्ष and चिण are used in forming the reflexive verbs, when the action affecting the agent is similar to the action which affects the object. With regard to the root वृह, the affix यक्ष is only prohibited by the present sūtra; the चिण being optionally employed by rule III. 1. 63, as वृह, अइग्न, or अहोहि गोः स्वयमेव 'the cow flows or flowed of itself' प्रस्तुते or प्रास्नोष्ट गोः स्वयमेव 'the cow flows or flowed of itself'; नमते or अनन्त इण्डः स्वयमेव 'the stick bends or bent of itself'.

This prohibition of the employment of the affixes यक्ष and चिण is extended to the verbs that take the affix ण (such as causatives &c.), to the verbs अन्य 'to loosen', अन्य 'to compose' and नृ 'to speak', and to the Atmanepadi Intransitive verbs. As कारयते 'it is caused to be made of itself'; अचीकरत् 'it was caused to be made of itself'; अघ्नीते 'it loosens of itself'; अभघ्निट 'it loosened of itself'; अघ्नीते; अभघ्निट 'it composes or composed of itself'; नृते and अचोचत् 'it speaks and spoke of itself'; आहते and आवघ्निट माणवकः स्वयमेव.

कुषिरञ्जोः प्राचांश्चपरस्मैपदं च ॥ ८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कुषि-रञ्जोः,
प्राचाम्, श्यन्, परस्मैपदं, च, ( कर्मकर्तरि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृष निष्कर्ष, रञ्ज रागे, अनयोर्धासोः कर्मकर्तरि प्राचामाचार्याणां मतेन श्यन्,
प्रत्ययो भवति परस्मैपदं च ॥

90. The affix श्यन् comes after the roots कृष 'to pull', and रञ्ज 'to colour', in the reflexive voice, according to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians, and these verbs take the affixes of the Parasmaipada.

This debars the affix यक्ष and the Atmanepada terminations. As कृष्यति पादः स्वयमेव 'the foot draws up of itself'; रञ्जति बन्धं स्वयमेव 'the cloth colours of itself'.

The phrase 'in the opinion of the Eastern' shows that it is an optional rule; so that we have also the forms कृष्यते and रञ्जते.

धातोः ॥ ८९ ॥ पदानि ॥ धातोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धातोरित्ययमधिकारी वेदितव्यः, आ हतीत्याध्यायपरिसमाप्तेयं दित ऊर्ध्वमनुक-
निष्क्रान्ते धातोरित्येवं तद्वेदितव्यम् ॥

91. As far as the end of the Third Book

382

VERBAL AFFIXES.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 92-94.

reckoning from the present aphorism, the affixes treated of are to be understood as coming after some verbal root.

This is an Adhikāra Sūtra. All these verbal affixes are broadly divided into two parts कृत् and कृत्य affixes, which will be described later on.

तत्रोपपदं सप्तमीस्थम् ॥ ९२ ॥ पदानि ॥ तत्र, उपपदं, सप्तमी-

स्थम्, ( घातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तथैतस्मिन्प्रास्वधिकारे दत्तीये यस्वन्तमी निर्दिष्टं तदुपपद्यसं भवति ॥

92. Here in this Third Book of Grammar referring to verbal roots, the word implied in a term exhibited in the locative case, is called 'upapada' or dependant word.

Thus in sūtra III. 2. कर्मण्यम् the word कर्मणि is exhibited in the 7th case; therefore the word implied by the word कर्मणि, namely, the word having the accusative case, will be called उपपद. Thus कुम्भम् + कृ + अण् = कुम्भकारः 'a potter'; here the word कुम्भम् is an upapada.

कृदतिङ् ॥ ९३ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृ, अ-तिङ्, ( घातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्मिन्प्रास्वधिकारे तिङ्‌वर्जितः प्रत्ययः कृत्स्नंको भवति ॥

93. In this portion of the Sūtras in which there is a reference to verbal roots, any affix except तिङ् (tense-affixes), is called कृत्.

Thus the affixes तव्यम् &c. are कृत्. All affixes up to the end of this Book belong to this class. These are affixes by which substantives are formed from verbal roots; and they have, therefore, most aptly been termed primary affixes. Words formed by these affixes will be Prātipadikas or crude forms or nominal bases (I. 2. 46). Thus कृ + तव्यं = कर्तव्यं. Why do we say 'except तिङ् affixes'? Observe चीयात् 'may he collect', स्तुयात् 'may he praise' which form verbs and not nouns.

बाऽसङ्घोऽस्त्रियान् ॥ ९४ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, असङ्घः, अस्त्रियान्,

( घातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्मिन्प्रास्वधिकारे ऽसमानसः प्रत्ययो ऽपवादो वा बाधको भवति स्वधिकार-विहितमध्यं पर्जयित्वा ॥

94. In this portion of the Sūtras, in which there is a reference to verbal roots, an affix which is calculated to debar a general one, not being of the same

BK. III. CH. I. § 94]

VERBAL AFFIXES.

383

form, optionally debars it; but not so in the case of feminine affixes (III. 3. 94 &c.)

Thus the affixes ण्वुल् and ण्व (III. 1. 133) are general affixes applicable to all roots in forming nouns of agency; and the sūtra III. 1. 133 which ordains these affixes, is an *utsarga* or a general rule; while the sūtra III. 1. 135 ordaining the affix क् after verbs having a penultimate इक् vowel, and the roots वा, प्री and क् is an *apavāda* or a special aphorism. In the latter case, therefore, optionally we may have the affixes ण्वुल् and ण्व also. Thus लिप् is a root that has a penultimate इ belonging to the *pratyāhāra* इक्; and therefore, in forming the noun of agency from it, the affix क् will have to be applied by rule 135 of this chapter already mentioned; thus विलिप्+क् = विलिप्+अ = विलिप्; but this special rule however does not debar the operation of the general rule, and we have optionally विलिप्+ण्वुल् = विलिप्क; and विलिप्+क् = विलिप्क् nom. sing. विलिप्ता.

Why do we say 'not being of the same form'? Because if two affixes have the same form, the present rule will not apply; and in the case of such affixes, the special affix will debar the general affix. Thus the affixes अण् and क् are, when stripped of their indicatory letters, affixes having the same form *i. e.* अ; and therefore the sūtra III. 2. 1. ordaining अण् as a general rule, will be always debarred by sūtra III. 2. 3 ordaining क्, as the latter is a special sūtra applicable only to those roots which end in long आ, or which are simple roots not compounded with any preposition. Thus गो+दा+क् = गोद: 'giver of cows'. So also क्म्बलद: 'blanket-giver'. In these cases we cannot have the affix अण्.

It follows from this sūtra as a necessary corollary, that the addition of indicatory letters does not make two or more affixes dissimilar in form (असकृप) when their essential effective element is the same. Thus the affixes क्, अण्, अच्, ण &c. are similar.

Why do we say 'but not so in the case of feminine affixes'? Because in the case of feminine affixes, a special affix will debar a general affix, though they may be dissimilar in form. Thus sūtra III. 3. 94 ordaining लिप् in forming feminine nouns from roots is a general or *utsarga* rule, while sūtra III. 3. 102 ordaining अ after roots that have already taken some affix is a special or *apavāda* rule, and though अ and लि are dissimilar in form, they being feminine affixes, the former will always debar the latter. Thus the compound desiderative roots चिकीर्ष and जिहीर्ष will form feminine nouns in आ and not by लिप्. Thus चिकीर्षा and जिहीर्षा and not चिकीर्षति &c.

कत्याः प्राङ्गवुलः ॥ ९५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कत्याः, प्राक्, ग्वुलः ॥

10

384

KRITYA AFFIXES.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 95, 96.

वृत्तिः ॥ च्युत्ब्रह्माविति बह्वति प्रागतस्माच्युत्संश्रन्दनाधारित ऊर्ध्वमनुक्रमिष्यामः
कृत्यसंज्ञकास्ते वेदितव्याः ॥

95. From this aphorism, as far as the aphorism च्युत्ब्रह्म (III. 1. 133), all the affixes treated, will get the name of Kritya.

This defines the class of affixes known as *kritya*, a subdivision of *krit* affixes. These are certain affixes like तव्य, अनीय &c, which may be treated as declinable verbal terminations. (III. 4. 70). The following 38 sūtras treat of these affixes. These verbal adjectives correspond in meaning to the Latin participles in *udus* conveying the idea that the action expressed by the verbs ought to be done or will be done. The word formed by them may be called Passive Potential Participles or Future Passive Participles. The illustrations will be given hereafter under each affix as taught. The word *kritya* occurs in sūtras II. 1. 33, II. 3. 71 &c.

तव्यतव्यानीयरः ॥ ९६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तव्यत्-तव्य-अनीयरः,
( धातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धातोस्तव्यतव्यानीयर इत्येते प्रत्यया भवन्ति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ वसेस्तव्यत् कर्तरि णिच्च ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ केलिमर उपसंख्यानम् ॥

96. The affixes तव्यत्, तव्य and अनीयर come after verbal roots.

The phrase 'after verbal roots' is understood in this aphorism by anuvritti from sūtra 91. The final letters त् of तव्यत् and र् of अनीयर are for the sake of indicating accent, being merely diacritical letters. The letter त् indicating svarita accent (VI. 1. 185) and the letter र् indicating penultimate udatta accent (VI. 1. 217); these being exceptions to the general rule of accent given in sūtra 3 *ante* of this chapter.

Thus कृ+तव्यत् = कर्तव्यम्, and कृ+तव्य = कर्तव्यम् 'must be done'; कृ+अनीयर = करणीयम् 'must be done'. In these cases the sense being that of the action itself, there is neuter gender singular number.

*Vart:*—The affix तव्यत् when coming after the verb वस् 'to dwell' in marking the agent, is treated as if it had an indicatory ण. The force of ण is to cause vriddhi. Thus वस् + तव्यत् = वास्तव्यः 'a dweller'. Here the word is in the masculine gender, as the force of the affix is that of the agent, and not as it generally has that of an act or object (III. 4. 70).

*Vart:*—The affix केलिमर should be enumerated in addition to those already enumerated in this aphorism. Thus पचेलिमा माषाः 'kidney beans fit to be

BK. III. CH. I. § 97, 98.]

YAT.

385

cooked'; भिविनिमानि काष्ठानि 'the woods are apt to be split i. e. fragile'. This affix is to be employed when it is intended to express an object alone (i. e. in the passive and reflexive sense) and cannot be employed like those enumerated above, to denote also the action.

अचो यत् ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अवः, यत्, ( धातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अजन्तादातोर्यत्पर्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ तकिरासि चित्तियतेजनीनामुपसंख्यानम् हनो वा वध च ॥

97. The affix यत् comes after a root that ends in a vowel.

The letter त् of this affix is indicatory showing that the udatta accent falls on the first vowel (VI. I. 213); thus गा+यत्= गेय, noun sing, गेयम् 'what is to be sung'; so also पेयम् 'what is to be drunk'; जेयम् 'what is to be conquered'. The आ of गा and पा is changed into ए by VI. 4. 65. Why do we say 'that ends in a vowel'? By sutra 124 of this chapter, a root ending in a consonant takes ण्यत् affix instead of यत्; reading these two aphorisms together, the conclusion to be drawn is that the affix यत् comes after roots which primarily end in a vowel, though in the course of development they may end in a consonant by the application of other rules. Thus from दो 'to cut', we have the desiderative root दिस्त, which ends in a vowel अ. This अ is elided before ardha-dhātuka affixes and thus the root becomes दिस्त, which ends in a consonant; nevertheless we shall have the affix यत् and not ण्यत्. Thus दिस्त्यम् 'what is wished to be cut'; दिस्त्यम् 'what is wished to be placed'. Similarly जु before ardha-dhātuka affixes becomes जो, the ओ is changed into अव् before य (VI. I. 79) and the form then is जव्. The root जव् however takes यत् and not ण्यत्; as जव्यो, पव्यम्, &c.

Vart:—The verbs तक् 'to fly', राच् 'to leap', चत् 'to ask', यत् 'to attempt' and जन् 'to be born', should be enumerated in addition; that is to say, these verbs, though ending in a consonant, take यत् and not ण्यत्; as तक्यम्, रास्यम्, चस्यम्, यस्यम्, and जन्यम्.

Vart:—And of the verb हन् 'to kill' वध is the substitute when it optionally takes the affix यत्. Thus we have वध्यम् or पालयम्. The latter form is evolved by sūtras VII. 3. 32 and 54. The affix यत् comes only after the वध substitute; after हन् the affix ण्यत् comes which changes the ह into घ, and न into त and causes vriddhi.

पोरदुपधात् ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ पोः, अद्व-उपधात्, (धातोः यत्)॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पवर्गान्तादातोरकारोपधात् यत् पश्ययो भवति ॥

98. The affix यत् comes after a root, which ends in a labial letter preceded by a short अ.

386

YAT.

BK. III. CH. I. § 99, 100.

This debars ण्यत्; thus शप्+यत् = शप्यं 'to be sworn'; लभ्+यत् = लभ्यम् 'to be acquired'.

Why do we say 'which ends in a labial'? Because if a root ends in any other consonant, though preceded by a short अ, the root will take ण्यत्; thus पच्+ण्यत् = पाक्यम् 'what is to be cooked'; वाक्यम् 'speech'.

Why do we say 'when preceded by a short अ'? When preceded by any other vowel, it will take ण्यत्; thus कुप्+ण्यत् = कोप्यम् 'to be angry'; so also गोप्यम् 'to be concealed'.

The word अत् is used in the sūtra in the original. The force of त् here is, by I. I. 70, that short अ having one matra or prosodial length is to be taken and not long आ. Therefore, after the root आप् 'to obtain', we have ण्यत् and not यत्; thus आप्यम् 'to be reached' i. e. 'attainable'.

शकिसहीष ॥ ९९ ॥ पदानि ॥ शकि-सहीः, च, (धातोः, यत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शङ्खशक्तौ, सह मर्पणो, अनयोर्धात्तीर्थस्पत्ययो भवति ॥

99. The affix यत् comes after the roots शङ्ख 'to be able', and सह 'to bear'.

Thus शक्यम् 'possible'; सहम् 'endurable'.

गद्मद्चरयमशानुपसर्गे ॥ १०० ॥ पदानि ॥ गद्-मद्-चर-

यमः, च, अनुपसर्गे, (यत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गद् मद् चर यमः, एतेभ्यधातुपसर्गेभ्यो यत्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ चरेराहि चामुरौ ॥

100. The affix यत् comes after the roots गद् 'to speak', मद् 'to be mad', चर 'to go, to eat', and यम to restrain', when these roots do not take any preposition.

Thus गद्यम् 'what is to be spoken, i. e. prose'; मद्यम् 'wine'; चर्यम् 'what is to be followed'; यम्यम् 'what is to be restrained'.

Why do we say 'when not preceded by a preposition'? When compounded with an upasarga, these roots will take ण्यत्; thus प्रायाम्; प्रमायाम् &c.

The root यम् would have taken the affix यत् by sūtra 98 also, as it ends in म and is preceded by अ; its separate enumeration in this sūtra is in order to show, that the compound verb यम् will not take the affix यत्. Therefore with regard to यम्, this is a niyama or restrictive rule and not a vidhi or original rule.

Vart :—The root चर when preceded by the preposition आह् takes the यत् affix when the sense is not that of a preceptor; thus आचर्यो देशः 'an approachable or communicable country'. But when the sense is that of a teacher the root takes ण्यत्; thus आचर्यः 'a preceptor'.

BK. III. CH. I. § 101-103]

IRREGULAR FORMATIONS

387

अवद्यपपयवयो गह्येपणितव्यानिरोधेषु ॥ १०१ ॥ पदानि ॥

अवद्य-पपय-वयोः, गह्येपणितव्य-अनिरोधेषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवद्य पपय वयो इत्येतं पपय निपातयन्ते गह्येपणितव्य-अनिरोध इत्येतं पपय
वयासंख्यम् ॥

101. The words अवद्य, पपय and वयो are irregularly formed, having the sense of 'condemnable', 'saleable' and 'unobstructable' respectively.

Thus, अवद्य पपय 'censurable sin'. Another and regular form is अनुथम्. This is formed by adding the affix कथम् to the root वद्य by III. I. 106. So also पपयः कन्यलः 'saleable blanket'; पपयाः गौः 'saleable cow'. The other and regular form is पपयम्, formed by the addition of पपय. So also शतेन वयो 'unobstructed by hundred'; सहस्रेण वयो 'unobstructed by thousand'. The other and regular form is पपय from the root वद्य 'to choose'. वयो means a girl choosing her own husband and is non-obstructable by any body. The word वयो in the sūtra is in the feminine gender, and it is in this gender only that the word is so formed. In the masculine gender, the word is regularly formed; thus वयो कृतिवलः

वह्यं करणम् ॥ १०२ ॥ पदानि ॥ वह्यं, करणम्, (यत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वह्येतोः करणं यत्पत्ययो निपातयते ॥

102. The word वह्य is irregularly formed, when the meaning of the word is an instrument of carrying.

The word वह्य is derived from root वह 'to carry' and means 'a vehicle', i. e., that by which a thing is carried; as वह्य शकटम्. When it does not mean a carriage, the root takes the affix पपय; thus वह्याः 'an ox'.

अयः स्वामिवैश्ययोः ॥ १०३ ॥ पदानि ॥ अयः, स्वामि-वैश्ययोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वह्य गतौ, अस्माण्यति पातं, स्वामिवैश्ययोः सिधेययोर्वरपत्ययो निपातयते ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ यतो अनाव इत्याद्युतस्त्वं पादे, स्वामिन्यन्तोइतस्त्वं च वक्तव्यम् ॥

103. The word अयः is irregularly formed when meaning 'lord' and a 'Vaisya'.

The root वह्य 'to go', would have taken पपय by sūtra 124 of this chapter; but it takes यत् when the sense of the word formed by it is that of a 'lord' or a man of 'Vaisya' caste. As अयः स्वामी, 'honored lord', अयो वैश्यः 'honored Vaisya'.

Vart: Though by VI. I. 213, the affix यत् makes the udatta accent fall on the first syllable of the word, yet in the case of the word अयः, when it means 'lord', the accent falls on the last syllable.

Why do we say 'when it means a lord or a Vaisya'? Otherwise the root takes the affix पपय; as आयो ब्राह्मणः 'the respectable Brahmana'.

II

388

IRREGULAR FORMATIONS.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 104-106]

उपसयों काल्या प्रजने ॥ १०४ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसयों, काल्या,

प्रजने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसयेति निपात्यते काल्या चेत्यजने भवति ॥

104. The word उपसयों is irregularly formed when meaning what has reached the time favorable to conception, or ripe for fruition.

The word उपसयों is formed by adding यत् affix to the root स् 'to move', compounded with the preposition उप. The word काल्या means having reached the time. The word प्रजने means the first conception. Thus उपसयों गौः 'the cow fit for the bull'; उपसयों वदवा 'the mare fit for the horse'.

Why do we say 'when meaning what has reached the time favorable to conception'? Otherwise the affix यत् will be used; as उपसयों शरदि मधुरा 'Madhura is approachable in Sarat season'.

अजयन् संगतम् ॥ १०५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अजयन्, संगतम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अजयमिति निपात्यते संगतं चेद्भवति ॥

105. The word अजयन् 'imperishable' is irregularly formed when qualifying the word संगतम् 'friendship' expressed or understood.

The word अजयन् is formed from the root ज् by the addition of यत्, and affixing the negative particle अ; as अ+ज्+यत् = अजयन्.

Thus अजयन् नोऽस्तु संगतम् 'let our friendship be imperishable'. So also अजयन् संगतम्.

Why do we say 'when qualifying the word संगतम्'? Observe अजयन् कश्चनः 'undecaying blanket'.

वदः सुपि कप् च ॥ १०६ ॥ पदानि ॥ वदः, सुपि, कप्, च, (यत्, अनुपसर्गे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वदेष्वतोः सुबन्तउपपये अनुपसर्गी कप् प्रत्ययो भवति चकाराद्यञ्च ॥

106. After the root वद् 'to speak', governing a case-inflected word as its upapada, and not having a preposition annexed to it, there comes the affix कप् also.

The phrase 'not having a preposition' is to be read into this sūtra by *anuvritti* from sūtra 100 *ante*. The force of the word 'also' is to indicate that the affix यत् is also employed. The word सुपि means 'in construction with an upapada that ends in case-affix'.

Thus ब्रह्म+वद्+कप्=ब्रह्म+वद्+च=ब्रह्मोद्भवम्; ब्रह्म+वद्+यत्=ब्रह्मोद्भवम् 'told by the Vedas or Brahman'. Similarly सत्योद्भवम् or सत्यवद्भवम् 'truth-mouthed'.

Why do we say 'when it has a case-inflected word as upapada'? Otherwise वद् + यत् = वाद्यम् a 'musical instrument'.

BK. III. CH. I. § 107, 108]

KYAP.

389

Why do we say 'not having a preposition'? Observe प्रवाहम् 'a rumour' formed by the affix पयत् and not by यत् or क्यप्.

भुवो भावे ॥ १०७ ॥ पदानि ॥ भुवः, भावे, ( अनुपसर्गे, सुपि, क्यप् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भवतेधीतोः सुवन्तउपपदे अनुपसर्गे भावे क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

107. After the root भू 'to be', in construction with a case-inflected word as its upapada and when used without a preposition, the affix क्यप् is employed to denote condition (bhāva).

The words सुपि and अनुपसर्गे of previous sūtras are understood in this. The *anuvritti* of यत् does not cover this aphorism. As ब्रह्मभुवं गतः = ब्रह्मत्वं गतः 'gone to or arrived at Brahmahood; देवभुवं = देवत्वं गतः 'gone to divinity'.

The word *bhāva* of this sutra governs the succeeding ones.

Why do we say 'in construction with a case-inflected word'? Otherwise it will take यत्; as भू+यत् = भो+यत् = भव्यम् (VI. I. 79).

Why do we say 'not taking a preposition'? Observe प्रभव्यम्.

हनस्त च ॥ १०८ ॥ पदानि ॥ हनः, त, च, (सुपि, अनुपसर्गे, क्यप्, भावे ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हन्तेधीतोः सुवन्त उपपदे अनुपसर्गे भावे क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति सकारभान्तादेशः ॥

108. After the root हन् 'to kill', when in construction with a case-inflected word as its upapada, and when used without a preposition, comes the affix क्यप् in denoting condition, and the letter त is the substitute of its final.

The phrases सुपि अनुपसर्गे and भावे are understood in this sūtra.

As ब्रह्म+हन्+कयप् = ब्रह्म+हत्+य = ब्रह्महत्य, (VI. I. 71) ब्रह्महत्या 'Brahman-murder'. So also अद्वहत्या 'killing a horse'.

When not in construction with a noun, the form is घातः 'a blow' (हन्+शिच्+घम्). This verb does not take the affix पयत् in denoting condition, there being no example of such formation.

Why do we say 'when not taking a preposition'? Observe प्रथालो वर्तते 'there is a combat'.

एतिस्तुशास्त्रदृजुषः क्यप् ॥ १०९ ॥ पदानि ॥ एति-स्तु-शास्त्र-

वृ-दृ-जुषः, क्यप् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एति स्तु शास् वृ दृ जुषः इस्त्रेतेभ्यः क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ शंसिवुहि गुहिभ्यो वेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ आह पूर्वविज्ञः संज्ञावानुपसंख्यानम् ॥

390

KYAP.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 109, 110]

109. After the verbs इ 'to go', स्तु 'to praise', शास् 'to govern', व् 'to choose', इ 'to respect' and जुप् 'to please', comes the affix क्यप्.

The anuvritti of सुपि, अनुपसर्ग and भावे does not extend to this aphorism. The present sutra ordains generally the affix क्यप् after the above verbs. Thus इ+क्यप्=इ+त+य (VI. 1. 71) = इश्य: 'to be gone'. The letter त being added by Rule VI. 1. 71 which declares 'त' is the augment of a short vowel when a क्तु affix, with an indicatory व् follows'. So also स्तु+क्यप्=स्तुरथ: 'to be praised'; शास्+क्यप्=शिस्+य (आ being changed into इ by VI. 4. 34) = शिष्य: 'to be instructed i. e. a pupil'. So also व्+क्यप्=वृश्य: 'to be chosen'; आह्+क्यप्=आहृश्य: 'to be honoured'; जुप्+क्यप्=जुध्य: 'to be served'.

Though the anuvritti of क्यप् was coming from the previous sutra 100, its repetition in this aphorism is to indicate that other rules such as 125 of this chapter should not take effect in the above verbs. Thus Rule 125 requires व्यत् 'after the verb स्तु, but the present rule prohibits that. Thus we have अवश्य स्तुरथ: 'must be praised'.

By व् in the sutra the root वृञ् is intended to be taken, and not the root वृह्. The equivalent derivative of the latter is वायः as वायोः क्वचिजः.

Vart:—The roots शस् 'to praise' वृह् 'to milk' and गुह 'to cover' optionally take the affix क्यप्. As शस्यम् or शस्यम् (VI. 4. 37); वृह्यम् or वृह्यम्, गुह्यम् or वृह्यम्.

Vart:—The verb अञ् 'to anoint', preceded by the preposition आह् takes the affix क्यप् when used as an appellative. As आ+अञ्+क्यप्=आड्यम् meaning clarified butter. The nasal is elided by VI. 4. 24.

Obj:—How do you explain the form उपेयम् which is evidently formed from the root इ by adding यत्? According to the present sutra, the affix क्यप् ought to have been added. Ans. The इ in उपेयम् is a different root from that taken here. The root in this sutra is इण् of the Adādi class.

ऋदुपधाखाङ्कुपिचूते: ॥ ११० ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋद्-उपधात्, च,

अकृपि-चूते:, ( क्यप् ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ ऋकारोपधाच्च धातोः क्यप् प्रययौ भवति कृपिचूती यजेतिशा ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ पाणौ खजेयैदृक्ख्यः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ समवपुर्वाच्च ॥

110. After verbs having a penultimate short ऋ, the affix क्यप् is employed, with the exception of the verbs कृप् 'to be able', and चूत 'to hurt'.

Thus वृत्+क्यप्=वृश्यम्; so also वृश्यम्. But कृप् and चूत् will form कञ्चन, and चरयैम्.

Why have we used the letter त् in ऋत्? It is to indicate that short ऋ

BK. III. CH. I. § III-II3.]

KYAP.

391

is meant and not long ऋ (I. 1. 70). Therefore the root ऋत् will take ण्यत् and form कीर्त्यम्.

*Vart* :—The root सूज् takes the affix ण्यत् when compounded with the word पाणि. Thus पाणिसर्ग्या रज्जः 'a rope'.

*Vart* :—The root सूज् when preceded by both सन् and अष takes ण्यत् as समवसर्ग्या.

ई च खनः ॥ १११ ॥ पदानि ॥ ई, च, खनः, (क्यप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ खनेर्धातोः क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवतीकारभान्तावेशः ॥

111. The affix क्यप् is employed after the root खन 'to dig', and long ई is substituted for the final of the root.

Thus खन्+क्यप्=ख+ई+य=खेयम् 'to be dug'. The long ई is used in the sutra for the sake of euphony. The same purpose would have been served by using short इ, thus 'इ च खनः'. But the long ई indicates that the rule VI. 4. 43 does not apply here. By that rule the अ of खन् would have been lengthened into आ before the affix क्यप्.

भुजोऽसंज्ञायाम् ॥ ११२ ॥ पदानि ॥ भुजः, अ-संज्ञायाम्, (क्यप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भुजो धातोरसंज्ञायां विषये क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ संपूर्वादिभाषा ॥

112. The affix क्यप् is employed after the verb भुज् 'to bear' when not used as a name.

Thus भु+क्यप्=भूय Pl. भूत्याः 'those who ought to be supported' *i. e.* 'servants'. Why do we say 'when not used as an appellative'? Observe भु+यत्=भायैः 'a Kshatriya'.

*Vart* :—The use of *kyap* is optional when this verb takes the preposition सन्. Thus संप्रत्याः or संमार्थाः.

भुजेविभाषा ॥ ११३ ॥ पदानि ॥ भुजेः, विभाषा, (क्यप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भुजेधातोर्विभाषा क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

113. The affix क्यप् optionally comes after the root भुज् 'to cleanse'.

This is an example of *Prāpta-vibhāshā*. By rule 110 *ante*, the root भुज् having a penultimate ऋ would have necessarily taken *kyap*; this sutra declares an option. As परिभुज्यः or परिमार्थः 'to be cleansed'. The second form is thus evolved :—

परिभुज्+यत् (III. 1. 124) = परिभुज्+य (VII. 3. 52) = परिमार्थ (VII. 2. 114)

राजसूय-सूर्य-सृषीध्र-रुच्य-कुष्य-कष्ठ-पञ्च-अव्यध्याः, (कषप्) ॥

राजसूय-सूर्य-सृषीध्र-रुच्य-कुष्य-कष्ठ-पञ्च-अव्यध्याः, (कषप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ राजसूय-सूर्य-सृषीध्र-रुच्य-कुष्य-कष्ठ-पञ्च-अव्यध्याः, (कषप्) ॥
निपातदन्ते ॥

114. The words राजसूय-सूर्य-सृषीध्र-रुच्य-कुष्य-कष्ठ-पञ्च and अव्यध्य are irregularly formed by the addition of the affix कषप्.

Thus राजा सोतव्यः or राजा इह सूयते, राज+सू+कषप्=राजसूयः 'the Rajasūya or coronation sacrifice.

Similarly स्र or सू+कषप्=सूर्यः 'the sun', literally that which moves (सरति) in the sky; or that which impels (सुवति) creation to action. स्र+व+कषप्=सृषीध्रम् 'false speech'; this is an exception to rule 106, by which यत would also have been applied. This rule prevents it. Thus रोचते+सौ, रुच्+कषप्=रुच्यः 'an agreeable lover'. So also स्र+कषप्=कुष्यम् 'a base metal (other than gold and silver)'; the other form is गोप्यम्। कृष्ट+पञ्च=कृष्टपञ्चाः 'that which ripens of itself in cultivated ground'. न व्ययते=अव्यध्यः 'a snake (what does not move by legs)'.

भिद्योद्धृपौ नदे ॥ ११५ ॥ पदानि ॥ भिद्य-उद्धृपौ, नदे, (कषप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भिद्योद्धृपौ कषप् निपातयते नदे+भिद्ये ॥

115. The words भिद्य and उद्धृप are irregularly formed by the affix कषप्; when meaning a 'river'.

Thus भिद्य+कषप्=भिद्यः 'a river that breaks its banks by the rush of its water', the name of the Bhidya river.

कषप्+कषप्=उद्धृप 'a river whose waters overflow the banks', name of the Uddhya river; the झ is changed into घ.

When not meaning or qualifying the river, the regular forms are used; thus भेत्ता and उज्ज्वला.

पुष्यसिद्धृपौ नक्षत्रे ॥ ११६ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुष्य-सिद्धृपौ, नक्षत्रे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुष्य-सिद्धृपौ, नक्षत्रे ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ पुष्य-सिद्धृपौ, नक्षत्रे ॥

116. The words पुष्य and सिद्धृप are irregularly formed by the affix कषप्, when used as names of asterisms.

Thus पुष्य+कषप्=पुष्यः 'the Pushya asterism'. It is so called because objects are nourished under the influences of this asterism. सिद्धृ+कषप्=सिद्ध्यः 'the asterism Siddhya' another name of Pushya, so-called because things are accomplished under the influence of this star.

When not the names of asterisms, the forms are पोषण 'nourishing', सेवनम् 'accomplishing'.

विपूयविनीयजित्या मुझककहलिषु ॥ ११७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विपूय-विनीय-जित्या:, मुझ-कलक-हलिषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विपूय विनीय जित्य इश्येते शब्बा निपास्यन्ते यथासंख्यं मुझकलकहन्ति इश्येते व्ययेषु बोध्येषु ॥

117. The words विपूय, विनीय and जित्य are irregularly formed when they mean, the 'muñja grass', the 'sediment' and the 'plough' respectively.

Thus वि+पू+क्यप्=विपूय: etymologically 'that which has to be purified to make rope'; वि+नी+क्यप्=विनीय 'a sediment or sin'; जि+क्यप्=जित्य 'a plough that which is to be conquered by strength'.

The regular derivatives are विपास्यम्, विनीयम् and जैयम्.

प्रत्यपिभ्यां ग्रहेऽछन्दसि ॥ ११८ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रति-अपिभ्यां, ग्रहेः, छन्दसि, (क्यप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रति अपि इश्येवं पूर्वार्द्धं ग्रहेः क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति छन्दसि विषये ॥

118. The verb मह 'to seize', preceded by the prepositions प्रति and अपि, takes the affix क्यप् in the Vedic literature.

Thus मस्तस्य न प्रतिगृह्यम्; तत्साजापिगृह्यम् ॥

In the classical Sanskrit the proper forms are प्रतिगृह्यम् and अपिगृह्यम्.

पदास्वैरिबाह्यापच्येषु च ॥ ११९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पद-अस्वैरि-बाह्या-पच्येषु, च, (ग्रहेः, क्यप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदेऽस्वैरिः बाह्यायां पश्ये चाये महेश्वरोः क्यप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

119. The root मह takes the affix क्यप्, when it means a 'word', a 'dependent', 'outside', or a 'partisan'.

Thus प्रगृह्यम् 'the Pragrihya words that do not admit of sandhi, already defined in sutra I. I. II. So also अङ्गृह्यं.

The word अस्वैरि means dependent upon others, not free to provide for himself. Thus गृह्यकाः शुकाः 'the captive parrots'.

The word बाह्य means 'situated outside'. Thus प्रागृह्यां सेना 'an army lying outside the village'. The word बाह्या being in the feminine gender indicates that the derivative word formed from मह must also be feminine in gender to have this sense.

The word पश्य is derived from पश्य 'a side, a party', and means a partisan, follower or friend. Thus वासुदेवगृह्याः 'siding with or being the partisans of Vāsudeva'. So also अर्जुनगृह्याः 'belonging to the party of Arjun'.

विभाषा कवृषीः ॥ १२० ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, क-वृषीः, (क्यप्)॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृषो वृषभ विभाषा कथप् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

120. After the verbs कृप् 'to do', and वृष 'to rain' the affix कथप् is optionally employed.

The root कृ would have taken the affix ण्यत् by 124, and the verb वृष would necessarily have taken कथप् by 110; the present sūtra therefore declares an optional rule. Thus: कृ+कथप् = कृयम् 'to be done'; or कृ+ण्यत् = कार्यम्. So also वृष्यम् or वृष्यम् 'stimulating'.

युग्यं च पत्रे ॥ १२१ ॥ पदानि ॥ युग्यम्, च, पत्रे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युग्यमिति निपात्यते पत्रं चेद्भवति ॥

121. The word युग्यम् is irregularly formed meaning a vehicle.

The word पत्र means that by which a thing is carried. Thus युग्यो गो 'the carrier bull or the yoked bull'. युग्यो हस्ती 'the harnessed elephant ready to carry'. युज्+कथप् = युग्यम्. The च is changed into ग. When not meaning a carrier or a carriage, it has the form योग्यं.

अमावस्यदन्यतरस्यान् ॥ १२२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अमावस्यद्, अन्यतरस्यान् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अमावस्यद्: सहाय्यवर्तते, तस्मिन्नुपपे वरोद्भूती: काले अधिकार्य एवमप्रत्ययो भवति नचान्यतरस्यां वृद्धाभावो निपात्यते ॥

122. Optionally the word अमावस्या is irregularly formed.

The word अमा means 'along' or 'together'. अमा in composition with the root वस् 'to dwell', takes the affix ण्यत् in the sense of location of time. Optionally the *Vriddhi* is not substituted in such a case. The time or the day on which the sun and the moon dwell together in the same constellation is called अमावास्या or अमावस्या.

The final न in अमावस्यत् is indicatory and is for the sake of showing where should the proper accent fall.

The two forms अमावस्या or अमावास्या are the same word, and *a fortiori* a rule made with regard to one will be made applicable to the other. And to this effect there is a paribhāṣhā which declares एकवेशविकृतस्थानन्यत्वम्; 'that which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means in consequence of this change, something else than what it was before the change had taken place'. Therefore sūtra IV. 3. 30, though it, in terms, says अमावास्याया वा is made applicable to the form अमावस्या also.

पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, निष्ठक्येदेवहूय-प्रणीय-उक्तीय-उच्छिष्ट्य-मय-स्तर्यां-श्वयं-

वृत्तिः ॥ निष्ठक्याश्रयः शृङ्गारछन्दसि विषये निपाययन्ते ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ हिरण्य इति वक्तव्यम् ॥

123. In the Vedas the following words are found which are formed irregularly :—निष्ठक्य, देवहूय, प्रणीय, उन्नीय, उच्छिष्ट्य, मय, स्तर्यां, श्वयं, खन्य, खान्य, देवयज्या, आपुच्छ्य, प्रतिषीव्य, ब्रह्मवाद्य, भाव्य, स्ताव्य and उपचाच्यपुट.

The formation of the above words are extremely irregular and they are all met with in the Vedic literature only. Thus the word निष्ठक्य is derived from the root कृत् 'to cut', with the preposition निष्ठ, and the affix ण्यत्, instead of कयप् which is the regular affix, by 110; निः+कृत्+ण्यत् = निः+हक्+य (the root कृत् transformed into हक् by transposition) = निष्ठक्य. As निष्ठक्य चिन्तीत् पशुकामः.

The above is apparently a guess-work etymology of grammarians.

So also देवहूय is formed by adding to the root हृयते 'to call' or हृ 'to invoke, the affix कयप् and the upapada देव; the vowel of the root is then lengthened and the augment त (VI. 1. 71), is not allowed, देव+है or हृ+कयप् = देवहूयः So also प्र+नी (to lead) + कयप् = प्रणीयः; उत्+नी+कयप् = उन्नीयः, उत्+शिष् (to leave) + कयप् = उच्छिष्ट्यम्; पृ (to die) + यत् = मयः; स्त (to cover) + यत् = स्तर्यां; it is always feminine. पृ (to bend) + यत् = श्वयः; खन् (to dig) + यत् = खन्यः; खन्+ण्यत् = खान्यः; देव (God) + यत् (to sacrifice) + यत् = देवयज्या; always used as feminine. आ+पुच्छ (to ask) + कयप् = आपुच्छ्यः, प्रति+सीव (to sew) + कयप् = प्रतिषीव्यः; ब्रह्माण्+वद् (to speak) + ण्यत् = ब्रह्मवाद्यः; भू (to be) + ण्यत् = भाव्यः; स्तु (to praise) + ण्यत् = स्ताव्यः; उप+चि (to collect) + ण्यत् + पुच्छ = उपचाच्यपुटम्. This last word is formed then only when the word पुच्छ follows: and when the sense is that of 'gold'. When it does not mean 'gold', the form is उपचेयपुटम् ।

ऋहलोण्येत् ॥ १२४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋ-हलोः, ययत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋषणोन्तादातोहैजन्ताच्च ण्यश्वस्यो भवति ॥

124. The affix ण्यत् comes after a verb that ends in ऋ (long or short), or in a consonant.

The phrase ऋहलोः is in the genitive case dual number, the force of genitive here being that of ablative. As कृ+ण्यत् = कार्यम् 'to be made'; हृ+ण्यत् =

13

396

NYAT.

[BK. III. CH. I. 125, 126.

हायं nom. sing. हायं 'to be taken'; धू+यत् = पायं; 'to be held'; वच्+यत् = वक् + यत् (VII. 3. 52) = वाक्यं (VII. 2. 116) 'to be spoken'; पच्+यत् = पावयन्.

ओरावश्यके ॥ १२५ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओः, आवश्यके (यत्) ॥

वृत्ति. ॥ उपपन्नताञ्चालोण्येत्प्रत्ययो भवति आवश्यके चोत्ये ॥

125. The affix यत् comes after a root that ends in the letter a long or short when the sense is that of necessity.

This debars the affix यत्. Thus तु+यत् = लो+य = लाच्यं (VII. 2. 115 and VI. 1. 79) 'must be cut'; so also पु+यत् = पाव्यम् 'must be purified'.

When 'necessity' is not indicated we have the form लाच्यं 'to be cut' The sutra as given in the original is rather ambiguous; it may be construed to mean, 1st when the word आवश्यक or a word having the sense of this term is in construction as upapada, the affix यत् is employed: or 2ndly when, the sense of the affix is that of 'necessity', the यत् is employed. There are objections to both these interpretations taken separately. For in the first case, though we could form the words अवश्यलाच्यं &c.; we could not form the word लाच्यं by itself. In the second case, though we could form the single word लाच्यं, we could not form the compound. The best solution is to take the second interpretation and form the compound by the universal rule of *Tatpurusha* contained in II. 1. 72, which would also regulate the accent.

आसुयुवपिरपिलपित्रपिचनश्च ॥ १२६ ॥ पदानि ॥ आसु-यु-वपि-रपि-लपि-वपि-चनः, च, (यत्) ॥

वृत्ति. ॥ आङ् पूर्वक सुनोतेः यु वपि रपि लपि वपि चम् इत्येतेभ्यश्च यत् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

126. The affix यत् comes after the verbs आसु 'to distil', यु 'to join', वप् 'to sow', रप् 'to speak distinctly' लप् 'to prate', वप् 'to be ashamed', and चम् 'to drink'.

The verb आसु is a compound verb formed by the preposition आङ् and the root सु. This sutra debars यत् that would otherwise have come by sutra 97 and 98.

Thus आसु+यत् = आसाच्यम्, (VII. 2. 115 and VI. 1. 79); so also याव्यम्, याव्यम्, राप्यम्, लाप्यम्, बाप्यम् and आचाप्यम्.

The force of the word च 'and' in the sutra is to indicate that the roots not included in the above enumeration should also be taken. Thus इम्+यत् = बाप्यम् ॥

आनाच्योऽनित्ये ॥ १२७ ॥ पदानि ॥ आनाच्यः, अनित्ये ॥

वृत्ति. ॥ आनाच्य इति निपात्यते अनित्येऽभिषये । नयतेराङ् पूर्वाण्यवायावेशो निपात्यते ॥

BK. III. CH. I. § 127, 128]

IRREGULAR FORMATIONS.

397

127. The word आनाय्यः is irregularly formed when meaning 'impermanent'.

This word is thus formed :—आह्+नी+प्यत्=आ+नै+य=आनाय्य, (the है being changed into आम् by the analogy of VI. I. 79).

As आनाय्यो शक्तिः। This is a species of Dakshināgni fire. As this fire is brought from the Gārhapatya fire and is not permanently kept alive, therefore it is called ānāyya. This however, is not co-extensive with Dakshināgni. It is that fire which is brought from the Gārhapatya, and has the same source with the Dakshināgni and Ahavaniyāgni. A Dakshināgni fire may be taken from different sources, as from the family of a well-to-do Vaishya, or from a frying place, or from Gārhapatya fire. When it is taken from the last i. e. from Gārhapatya fire, it is ānāyya Dakshināgni. Ahavaniya is also taken from Gārhapatya.

It is not every thing, that is not lasting, which is called ānāyya; for a fragile pot will not be called so. It applies only to the consecrated fire. When it has not this sense, the form is आनेय meaning 'what ought to be brought'.

प्रणाय्योऽसन्तौ ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रणाय्यः, असन्तौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रणाय्य इति निपात्यन्ते असन्तावभिषे ॥

128. The word प्रणाय्यः is irregularly formed when meaning 'disapproved'.

The word असमति is a negative word meaning 'non-agreement'. It means also 'disrespect'.

Thus प्रणाय्यधोः 'the thief is to be disliked'.

Why do we say when meaning 'disapproved'. Because otherwise the regular form is प्र+नी 'to lead' + यत्=प्रणोयः 'tractable'.

The word in the sūtra is असमति which we have translated as 'disapproved'. But the word समति also means अभिज्ञाप् or 'desire'; and असमति would therefore, mean 'free from desire or worldly attachment'. Therefore the word असमति means also 'free from attachment', as in the following sentence :—

उद्येवाय पुणाय पिता ब्रह्म प्रभुवात्, प्रणाय्याय अन्तेवासिने नान्यस्मै कस्मैश्चन 'let the father teach the Secret Doctrine to his eldest son, or to such pupil who is free from worldly attachment, and to no one else'.

पाय्यसांनाय्यनिकाय्यधाय्या नानहविर्निवाससाभिषेनीषु ॥

१२ ॥ पदानि ॥ पाय्य-सांनाय्य-निकाय्य-धाय्याः, नान-हवि:-निवास-साभिषेनीषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पाय्याश्चः शब्दा निपात्यन्ते यथासंख्यं मानै हविषि निवासे साभिषेन्न्या भाभिषेवान् ॥

398

IRREGULAR FORMATIONS.

[BK. III. CH. I. § 129-131]

129. The words पाठ्य, सान्नाय्य, निकाय्य and पाठ्या are irregularly formed meaning 'a measure', 'an oblation to fire', 'a dwelling', and 'a sacrificial prayer', respectively.

These words are supposed to be formed thus:—मा (to measure)+प्यत् = पाठ्यम्, the म being changed into प and another य being added by VII. 3. 33. The regular form is मेयम् 'to be measured' (मा+प्यत्=मे+य VI. 4. 65=मेय). सम्+मां (to lead)+प्यत् = सान्नाय्यम् 'the oblation'. It being a crude form applies to a particular kind of oblation. The regular form is सन्नेयम्। नि+चि (to collect)+प्यत् =नि+चै+य=नि+चाय+य=निकाय्यः 'a dwelling'. The regular form is निचेय। धा (to put)+प्यत् = पाठ्या (fem.). The samadheni is the name of certain Rik hymns used as supplemental verses in a Litany. The other form is धेय।

क्रतौ कुण्डपाय्यसंचाय्यौ ॥ १३० ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रतौ, कुण्डपाय्य-संचाय्यौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कुण्डपाय्य संचाय्य इत्येतौ शब्दो निपात्येते क्रमावभिधेये ॥

130. The words कुण्डपाय्यः and संचाय्यः are irregularly formed meaning a sacrifice.

These words are thus formed: कुण्ड+पा (to drink)+यत् = कुण्ड+पा+य+य (VII. 3. 33) = कुण्डपाय्यः 'the sacrifice in which Soma is drunk with a bowl'. The accent falls on the first syllable by VI. 1. 213. सम्+चि (to collect)+प्यत् = संचाय्यः 'the sacrifice in which Soma is collected'.

If not applied to sacrifices, the forms will be कुण्डपाय्यम् and संचेयः.

अग्नौ परिचाय्योपचाय्यसमूह्याः ॥ १३१ पदानि ॥ अग्नौ, परिचाय्य-उपचाय्य-समूह्याः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिचाय्य उपचाय्य समूह्य इत्येतौ शब्दो निपात्यन्ते अग्नावभिधेये ॥

131. The words परिचाय्यः, उपचाय्यः and समूह्यः are irregularly formed when they are names of fire.

These words are thus formed:—परि+चि+प्यत्=परि+चै+य=परि+चाय+य= परिचाय्यः 'sacrificial fire arranged in a circle' (the है being changed into आर्य by the analogy of VI. 1. 79. This peculiar sandhi before the semivowel य has been illustrated in the previous examples also). So also उपचाय्यः 'a kind of sacred fire'. सम्+वह+प्यत्=सम्+कह+य=समूह्यः 'a kind of fire'. समूह्यं चिन्तीत पङ्कजः 'let him kindle the Samuhya fire desirous of a victim'.

Why do we say 'when they are names of fire'? Observe otherwise, परिचेयम् 'to be heaped', उपचेयम् 'to be increased', संग्रह्यम् 'to be carried'.

27134

BK. III. CH. I. § 132-134.]

LYU NI AND ACH.

399

चित्याग्निचित्ये च ॥ १३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ चित्य-अग्निचित्ये, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चित्याग्नोऽग्निचित्याग्निश्च निपात्यते ॥

132. The words चित्य and अग्निचित्य are also irregularly formed.

The word चित्य: comes from the root चि 'to collect', and means fire *i. e.* that which is collected. As चित्योऽग्निः 'the funeral pile fire'. The word अग्निचित्य means, arranging the fire. The affix च has been added to denote condition, together with the augment तुक् (तृ). These words have *udātta* accent on the last vowel. The regular form is चेयम् 'to be gathered'.

ग्वुलद्वैचौ ॥ १३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ग्वुल-द्वैचौ, (धातोः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वधातुभ्यो ग्वुलद्वैचौ प्रत्ययौ भवतः ॥

133. The affixes प्वुल (अक्) and द्व (द्व) are placed after all verbal roots, expressing the agent.

The word 'root' is understood in the above aphorism. Thus कृ 'to do' + प्वुल = कार + वृ (VII. 2. 115) = कार + अक (VII. 1. 1) = कारक nom. sing. कारकः 'doer.' कृ + द्व = कर + द्व (VII. 3. 84) = कर्तृ nom. sing. कर्ताः. So also हारकः and हर्ताः.

The च् of द्व is not indicatory, but distinguishes this affix from द्वन्; the simple द्व includes both द्व and द्व, as in V. 3. 59, and VI. 4. 154.

नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः ॥ १३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ नन्दिग्रहि-पचादिभ्यः, ल्यु, णिनि, अचः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्रिभ्योगणै-यस्त्यः प्रत्यया यथासंख्यं भवन्ति, नन्द्यादिभ्यो ल्युः, ग्रहादिभ्यो णिनिः, पचादिभ्योऽचः ॥

134. After the verbs classed as नन्द 'to be happy', ग्रह 'to take' and पच 'to cook' there are the affixes ल्यु (अन) णिनि (इन्) and अच (अ) respectively.

The word *ādi* meaning *etcetra*, is to be joined with every one of the above three words. These three affixes come respectively after the verbs of the above three classes. Thus after the verbs of नन्द class, comes the affix ल्यु; after the verbs of ग्रह class, comes the affix णिनि; after the verbs of पच् class, comes the affix अच्.

The नन्दादि verbs will not be found in one place in the Dhātupātha. The list of the words formed by these affixes have, however, been collected in the Gaṇapātha. Thus नन्द + ल्यु = नन्द + यु (I 3. 8) = नन्द + अन (VI. 1. 1) = नन्दन nom. sing. नन्दनः 'son' (lit. what gladdens). So also from the following causa-

14

400

THE AFFIX KA.

BK. III. CH. I. § 135.

tive roots, nouns are formed, meaning names:—बासि—बासन: or बाशन: ; महि—महन: ; वृषि—वृषण: (or भूषण:); साधि—साधन: ; वर्धि—वर्धन: ; शीभि—शीमन: and रोचि—रोचन:.

The following derivatives are names:—सहि—सहन: ; सपि—सपन: ; इमि—इमन:

So also the following words:—जल्पन:, रमण:, इर्पण:, संकल्पन:, संकर्षण:, संहर्षण:, जनार्दन:, यवन:, पवन:, मधुसूदन:, विभाषण:, लवण: (the ण in लवण is irregular), चित्तविनाशन:, कुलदमन: and शत्रुदमन:.

The वहादि verbs are also nowhere enumerated in a group. The following are, however, those verbs:—यह—महिन् nom. याही; उत्सह—उत्साहिन् nom. उत्साही; उदस—उदासिन्; उद्वास—उद्घासिन्; स्था—स्थायिन्; मन्त्र—मन्त्रिन्; संमर्द—संमर्दिन्. So also the verbs रक्ष, भु, वस, वप and शा preceded by नि; as, निरक्षिन्, निभाविन्, निवासिन्, निवापिन्, निशायिन्. The verbs याचि, व्याह, संव्याह, ब्रज, वद and वस take णिन् when preceded by the negative particle; as, अयाचिन्, अव्याहारिन्, असंव्याहारिन्, अब्राजिन्, अवादिन् and अवासिन्. So also after verbs ending in a vowel when agents are non-conscious beings: as, अकारिन्, अहारिन्. So also, अविनायिन्, अविशायिन्, विशायिन्, विघयिन् (meaning a place) विशायिन् and विघायिन्, अभिभाविन्, अपराधिन्, उपरोधिन्, परिभाविन् and परिभाविन् ।

The following are पचादि words:—पच, वच, वप, वद, चल, तप, पत नद्द, भघट, वस गरट, प्रवट, तरट, चीरट, ग्राहट, जर, मर, झर, झम, सूदट, देवट, मोरट, सेव, मेष, क्रोध, ब्रण, वंश, वश, वम्भ, जारमर, इवपच, मेष, क्रीष, लप, मद, रज, दीघट, चरट ।

The द् in नद्द &c., shows that the feminine of these is formed by long ई (IV. I. 15). The पचादि class is an आकृतिगण: ।

अडिबिधि: सर्वधातुभ्यः पञ्चन्तं च पञ्चादयः ।

अणु बाधनार्थमेवं स्यात् सिध्यन्ति इवपचादयः ॥

In fact the affix अच् comes after all verbs, and is not exclusively confined to the verbs above enumerated. The affix अच्, therefore, debars अणु and may be taken to be the universal affix, and by its help the forms like इवपच &c. may be explained.

इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकरः कः १३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ इग्-उपध-ज्ञा-प्री-किरः,

कः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इगुपधेभ्यो जानातेः पीणातेः किरतेभ्य कप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

135. After a verb ending in a consonant but preceded by इ, उ or क (long or short), and after the verbs सा 'to know', प्री 'to please', and कु 'to scatter', comes the affix क (अ).

Thus विज्ञिप्+क=विज्ञिप् nom. sing. विज्ञिप्:. So also विज्ञिप्: 'inscription'; वृध: 'who knows'; कृश: 'lean'; सा+क=स: 'who knows' (VI. 4. 64); प्री+क=

BK. III. CH. I. § 136, 137] THE AFFIX SA.

401

प्रियः 'what pleases'; कृ+क=कि+अ (VII. I. 100)=किर+अ (I. I. 51)=किरः 'who scatters' i. e. 'a hog'.

The words देव 'God', सेव 'service' and भेव 'ram', should be read in the पचादि class of the last sūtra, being formed by the affix अच् and not by क.

आतश्चोपसर्गं १३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, च, उपसर्गं, ( कः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तेभ्यो धातुभ्यः उपसर्गं उपपर्वं क्रमस्थयो भवति ॥

136. Also after a verb ending in long आ when there is a preposition along with it, the affix क is placed.

This is an apavāda of III. I. 40, and debars the affix ण. Thus प्रस्था+क=प्रस्थ+अ=प्रस्थः (VI. 4. 64). सुग्जै+क=सुग्ज+अ=सुग्जः 'very weary' (आ substituted for है by VI. I. 45.) सुग्जै+क=सुग्ज+अ=सुग्जः 'very languid'.

The final आ is dropped before the affix क by rule VI. 4. 64. There is elision of long आ when an ārdhadhātuka affix follows beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory क or ङ.

पाघृध्ना घेट् दृशः शः ॥ १३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ पा-घृ-ध्ना-घेट्-दृशः, शः, ( उपसर्गं ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पादिन्यो धातुभ्यः उपसर्गं उपपर्वं क्रमस्थयो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ जिप्तेः संज्ञायैः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

137. The affix श (अ) is employed after the roots पा 'to dr' k', घृ 'to smell', ध्ना 'to blow', घेट् suck', and दृश 'to see' when there is a preposition along with these roots.

Thus उत्+पा+श=उत्+पिब+अ (VII. 3. 78)=उत्पिब nom. sing. उत्पिबः; so also विपिबः; उज्जिघृ: and विजिघृ:। उत्+ध्ना+श=उत्+धम्+अ= (VII. 3. 78); उज्ज:; विघ्नः; उत्+घे+श=उज्जय:; विघ्नः; so also उत्+दृश+श=उत्पन्नः; (VII. 3. 78). so also विपन्नः;

Some commentators do not read the word 'upasarga' into this sūtra. According to them the forms like पन्नः &c., can be formed also.

The affix श, of which श is indicatory, the real affix being अ, causes the root to undergo all those changes, which it undergoes in special tenses; for it is a sārvadhātuka affix there; see sūtra III. 4. 113 and VII. 3. 78.

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated of the root घृ, when the word to be formed is a name. As वि+आ+घृ+क=व्याघ्रः 'tiger' (an animal that goes about smelling). Here there is क and not the affix श.

THE AFFIX NA.

BK. III. CH. I. § 138-140.

अनुपसर्गान्निष्पविन्दधारिपारिवेद्युदेजि चेतिसातिसाहिभ्यश्च ॥
१३८॥ पदानि ॥ अनुपसर्गात्, लिप्य-विन्द-धारि-पारि-वेदि-उदेजि-चेति-
साति-साहिभ्यः, च (शः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनुपसर्गेभ्यो लिप्यादिभ्यः शपथययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ नो लिप्येति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ गवादिषु विन्दे संज्ञायाम् ॥

138. The affix श is employed after the following verbs when used without a preposition : लिप्य, विन्द and the causatives धारि, पारि, वेदि, उदेजि, चेति, साति and साहि.

Thus लिप्य: 'smearing'; विन्द: 'acquiring'; धारय: 'holding'; पारय: 'ferrying'; वेदय: 'knowing'; उदेजय: 'shaking'; चेतय: 'perceiving'; सातय: and साहय.

Why do we say 'when used without a preposition'? Observe प्रलिप्य; here the affix is क.

Vart :—The verb लिप् with the preposition नि takes the affix श. As निलिप्या 'the name of certain deities', 'a cow'.

Vart :—The affix श is employed after विन्द when compounded with the words गो &c. and when the word to be formed is a proper noun. As गोविन्द: 'Krishna' (protector of cows); अरविन्द: 'a lotus' (having petals like spokes).

ददातिदधात्योविभाषा ॥ १३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ ददाति-दधात्योः,
विभाषा, ( शः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दानो धान्यश्च विभाषा शपथययो भवति ॥

139. The affix श is optionally employed, after the root श 'to give', and धा 'to hold', when used without a preposition.

This debars श: Thus इदः 'giving'; or दायः 'inheritance'; इधः 'holding' or धायः 'having'.

When a preposition is used, the affix श is not employed; as प्रहः, प्रधः.

ज्वलितिकसन्तेभ्यो शः ॥ १४० ॥ पदानि ॥ ज्वल्-इति-कसन्तेभ्यः,

भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सनीतेऽपि उपसंख्यानम् ॥

140. After the verbs beginning with ज्वल 'to shine' and ending with कस 'to go', when used without a preposition, the affix श is optionally employed,

BK. III. CH. I. § 141, 142.] THE AFFIX NA.

The word इति in उवलिति indicates beginning. These are about 56 verbs, all belonging to the *Bhūḍā* class. See No. 804 to 860 in the Dhātupātha, Bombay Edition in the Appendix to Sidhānta Kaumudi.

This debars the affix अच्; as उवाल: or उवल: ; चाल: or चल:

The affix ण (अ) having an indicatory ण, causes the vriddhi of the penultimate अ. When the affix ण is not used, then अच् is used, and we have the other form. But compound verbs take अच्; as प्रउवल: 'luminous'.

*Vart.*—The verb तन 'to stretch' must be included in this list, and it takes the affix ण; as अवतान. The conditions 'option' and 'without preposition' do not apply in this case. The verb तन् necessarily takes this affix, though compounded with an upasarga.

इयाऽद्वयधातुसंस्तूतीशवसावहुलिहशिलपश्वसश्च ॥ १४१ ॥ पदानि ॥

इया-आदु-व्यथ-आसु-संसु-अतीश-अवसा-अवहु-लिह-शिलप-श्वसः, च, (गः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इयैह आकारान्तेभ्यश्च धातुभ्यः व्यथ आलु, संतु, अतीश अवसा अवहु लिह शिलप श्वस इत्येतेभ्यश्च णप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

141. The affix ण is employed after the following verbs also :—इये 'to go', verbs ending in long आ, व्यथ 'to pierce', आलु 'to pain', संतु 'to flow', अतीश 'to pass on', अवसा 'to complete', अवह 'to take away', लिह 'to lick', शिलप 'to embrace', and श्वस 'to breathe'.

The root इये, before affixes, becomes इया, (VI. 1. 45) and is thus included in the phrase 'verbs ending in long आ'. What is then the use of its separate enumeration? The separate enumeration is for the sake of excluding the application of every other rule which might have prohibited ण. Thus III. 1. 136 enjoins क when a compound verb ends in आ. But that rule does not apply to the verb इया.

Thus अवइयाय: 'frost', प्रतिइयाय: 'catarrh', वाय: 'inheritance', धाय: 'having', व्याध: 'pain', आलाव: 'wound', संलाव: 'flow', अत्याय: 'transgression', अवसाय: 'conclusion', अवहार: 'taken away', लेह: 'licking', इलेप: 'embracing', इवास: 'breath'. See VII. 3. 33.

दुन्मोहनुपसर्गे ॥ १४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ दु-न्योः, अनुपसर्गे, ( गः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दुनोतेनैयतेश्वानुपसर्गे णप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

142. The affix ण is employed after the verbs दु 'to burn', and नी 'to lead', when used without a preposition.
