[BK. III. CH. I. § 143-145.]

Thus बु+ण=शै+अ (VII. 2. 115) = शबः (VI. 1. 78) 'burning'. So also नी+ण=नी+अ=नायः 'leading'.

Why do we say 'when used without a preposition'? Observe प्रहः 'burning'; प्रपद्यः 'friendship'.

विभाषा ग्रहः ॥ १४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, ग्रहः, ( शः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विभाषा महेधातोर्णप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ भवतश्चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

143. The affix ण is optionally employed after the verb मह 'to seize'.

This debars the affix अच्. Thus मह+ण = मह+अ (VII. 2. 116) = माहः 'seizing', 'a crocodile'; or मह+अच् = महः 'a planet'.

The option allowed by this aphorism is a vyavasthita-vibhāshā or definite option, that is to say, the affix ण is always used when the word to be formed means a water-animal, such as a crocodile, shark &c., and in that sense the word is माह. But not so, when heavenly luminaries are meant; there the word is मह.

Vart:—This rule should be extended to the root भू 'to be' also. Thus:—भावः 'condition' and भवः 'existence'.

गेहे कः ॥ १४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ गेहे, कः, ( ग्रहः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ महेधातोः कप्रस्थयो भवति गेहे कर्तरि ॥

144. The affix क is employed after the verb मह when the agent so expressed denotes a house.

Thus मह+क (VI. 1. 16) = गृहन् 'a house'. The र is changed into ऋ by the rule of saṃprasāraṇa. The plural form गृहाः means 'wife', as she is especially the person that constitutes the house; while the plural of गृहं meaning 'house' will be गृहाणि.

शिल्पिनि खुन् ॥ १४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ शिल्पिनि, खुन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धातोः खुनप्रस्थयो भवति शिल्पिनि कर्तरि ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ नृतिखनिरखिन्यः परिगणनं कर्तव्यम् ॥

145. The affix खुन् (अक) comes after a verb; when the agent so expressed denotes an artist.

Vart:—This affix should be confined to the verbs नृत् 'to dance', खन् 'to dig' and रङ्ग 'to dye'.

Thus नृत्+खुन् = नर्त+अक (VII. 1. 1) = नर्तकः 'dancer'. The letter ब is indicatory (I. 3. 6) and by Rule IV. 1. 41, it denotes that words formed by prefixes having indicatory ब form their feminine gender by the affix ङीष्. Thus

BK. III. CH. I. § 146-148.] THE AFFIX NYUT.

405

the feminine of नर्तक is नर्तकी; so also खनक: 'miner', fem. खनकी; रजक: 'washer-man', fem. रजकी.

In the case of the root रंज the nasal is elided. According to the opinion of the author of *Mahābhāshya*, only two verbs are governed by this sūtra namely नूत and खन. According to him, the verb रञ्जु takes the affix कून्. Thus रञ्जु+कून् = रञ्जु+बु (VI. 4. 37) = रञ्जु+अक (VII. I. 1) = रजक, feminine रजिका.

गत्यकन् ॥ १४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ गः, थकन् ( शिल्पिनि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गायतेत्यकनपत्ययो भवति शिल्पिनि कर्तरि ॥

146. The affix थकन्, (थक) comes after the verb गै to 'sing', when the agent so expressed, denotes an artist.

As, गै+थकन् = गायकः (VI. I. 45) 'a singer', fem. गायिका.

गयुट् च ॥ १४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ गयुट्, च ( गः, शिल्पिनि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गायतेत्युट् पत्ययो भवति शिल्पिनि कर्तरि ॥

147. The affix ग्युट् is also employed after the verb गै 'to sing', when the agent so expressed denotes an artist.

By the word च 'also', the word गा of the last sūtra is drawn into this. Thus गै+ग्युट्=गा+अन (VII. I. 1)=गायनः fem. गायनी; the च is added by VII. 3. 33.

The separation of these rules (*yoga-vibhāga*) relating to गै is for the purpose of the sūtras that follow. Had गत्यकन् and ग्युट् च been made one aphorism, the *anuvritti* of both these affixes would have run into the subsequent sūtras. But it is intended that the *anuvritti* of ग्युट् should only run, and hence this *yoga-vibhāga* or division of one sūtra into two.

हृश्च श्रीहिकालयोः ॥ १४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ हृः, च, श्रीहि-कालयोः, ( गयुट् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जहातेर्जिहीतेश् धातोण्युट् पत्ययो भवति श्रीहो काले च कर्तरि ॥

148. After the verb हा, also the affix ग्युट् is employed when the agent so expressed denotes 'rice' and 'time'.

The verb हा denotes two verbs हाक 'to abandon' and हाह 'to go' both belonging to the Third Conjugation, forming जहाति and जिहीते as 3rd per. sing. Thus हा+ग्युट्=हायनः 'a kind of rice' (that which *jahāti* 'leaves off' all water) हायनः 'a year' (that which *jihite* 'goes through' all conditions.)

THE AFFIX VUN. [BK. III. CH. I. § 149, 150.

The accents are however different in the two. In one case the udatta is on the middle; in the other, on the last.

पु-स्वः(स्वः)ः सममिहारे वुन् ॥ १५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ मु-स्वः(स्वः)-स्वः, सममिहारे, वुन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मु-स्वः (स्वः) लु इरवेलेश्यो धातुभ्यः सममिहारे वुन् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

149. After the verbs मु 'to go', सु 'to move', लु 'to flow' and लु 'to cut', the affix वुन् is employed, when repetition is meant.

As, मु+वुन्=प्रो+अक (VII. I. I)= प्रबकः; so also, सरकः, सबकः, and लबकः.

The word *samabhikāra* in the sūtra indicates that the action done by the agent must be well performed. The affix *vun* being thus ordained for the action, when it is well performed, it follows, that it will not be employed where the action is repeatedly ill performed. The affix will be employed even when there is no repetition but the action is well performed even at the first attempt.

आशिषि च ॥ १५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ आशिषि, च, ( वुन् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आशिषि गम्यमानायां धातुमानात् वुन् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

150. The affix वुन् is employed after all verbs, when benediction is intended.

As, जीव+वुन् = जीवकः 'may he live'; ननकः 'may he be happy'.

The word आशीः means a sort of prayer; and it relates to action. The force of this affix is that of 'an agent with the addition that the action is simply the object of a prayer of some one who wishes that that may be the action of that agent'.

# अथ तृतीयाध्यायस्य द्वितीयः पादः ॥

# BOOK THIRD.

# CHAPTER II.

—:o:—

कर्मणयण् ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्मणि, अण्, ( धातोः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वत्र कर्मण्युपपत्ते धातोरण्यपत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ शीलिकामिमध्याचरिष्यो णः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्तरस्य च वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ ईशिक्षमिष्यां चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

1. The affix अण् comes after a verbal root when the object, (of whatever sort it may be), is in composition with it, (as an upapada).

The object or karma is of three sorts, namely *nivartya*, *vikārya* and *prāpya*.

The object which has a material cause, but such cause is however unexpressed in the sentence, is called *nivartya* object; as कुम्भम् करोति 'he makes a pot'; here युत 'mud' the material cause of कुम्भ is unexpressed, therefore, कुम्भ is *nivartya* object. Where the material cause itself is changed, by a modification, into something else, such an object is called *vikārya* object; as काण्डलावः 'the branch-cutter'. While the object which cannot be approached by any action, and is not affected by it, but is always constant, is called the *prāpya* object; as वेदाध्यायः 'the reading of Veda'; the Veda is always the same.

They will be illustrated by the following examples:—Of the first kind, we have कुम्भकारः 'a potter' and नगरकारः 'a city-builder'; of the second, we have काण्डलावः 'a branch-cutter' and शरलावः 'a reed-cutter'. Of the third, वेदाध्यायः 'the learning of Veda' and चर्चापाठः 'the reading of Charcha'. But compound nouns cannot be formed of such sentences as प्रातः गृहीत इति 'he goes to the village', आदित्यं पश्यति 'he sees the sun', 'हिमवंतं गुणोति' 'he hears the Himavat'. The reason is that it is against the usage of the language to form nouns out of these.

*Vart*:—The affix ण comes after the verbs शील, काम, भद्र्य and आचर and the noun in composition with it, retains its original accent. As मांसशीलः 'addicted to flesh', fem. मांसशीलाः; मांसकामः 'loving flesh', fem. मांसकामा; मांसभक्षः 'carnivorous', fem. मांसभक्षा; and कल्याणाचारः 'good-conducted', fem. कल्याणाचारा।

16

408

THE AFFIX KA.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 2-4.

Vart:—The affix ए comes after the roots ईक्ष 'to look' and क्षम 'to for-bear' under similar circumstances. As सुखप्रतीक्षः, fem. सुखप्रतीक्षा 'expecting happiness'; बहुशमः fem. बहुशमा 'much forbearing'.

हृवामश्च ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ हृ, वा, सः, च, (अण्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हृम्, वैम्, माहः, एतेभ्यः कर्मण्युपपेक्ष्यप्ययौ भवति ॥

2. The affix अण् comes after the root हृम् 'to call', वैम् 'to weave', माहः 'to measure', when the object is in composition with it.

This debars the affix क (III. 2. 3); as स्वर्ग+हृ+अण् = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ = स्वर्ग+हृ+अ

आतोऽनुपसर्गैः कः ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, अनुपसर्गैः, कः,

( कर्मणि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तेभ्यो धातुभ्योऽनुपसर्गेभ्यः कर्मण्युपपेक्ष्यप्ययौ भवति ॥

3. The affix क comes after a verbal root that ends in long आ when there is no upasarga preceding it and when the object is in composition with it.

This debars अण्; as गां+हृ+क = गां+हृ+अ = गोः 'Giver of cows', (the long आ is elided by VI. 4. 64.) = So also, कश्चन्द्रः 'who gives a blanket'; पाष्पिच्चम् 'what protects the rear'; अङ्गुच्चिनम् 'what protects the finger' (a thimble).

Why do we say 'when there is no upasarga'? Witness गोः 'who ceremoniously gives a cow', बडवांदाय 'who ceremoniously gives a mare'. Here the compound verb संदा takes the affix अण्.

सुपि स्थः ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुपि, स्थः, ( कः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सुबन्त उपपेक्ष्यप्ययौ स्थितेः कप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

4. The affix क comes after the root स्था when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix, as an upapada.

In the three previous sutras, the word in composition was always in the accusative case. This sutra declares that with regard to the verb स्था, the upapada may have any case not necessarily the accusative. As समस्थः = समे स्थितिः 'who dwells in accessible position'; and विषमस्थः 'having an inaccessible position'.

BK. III. CH. II. § 5]

THE AFFIX KA.

409

This *sūtra* should be divided into two *sūtras* (yoga-bibhāga). Thus:—
(1) सुषि ॥ The affix क comes after every root ending in long आ, when in composition with a case-inflected word; as द्वाभ्यां पिवति = द्वि+पा+क=द्विपः (VI. 4. 64) 'who drinks with two organs' *i.e.* the proboscis and the mouth, an elephant'. So also पाइपः 'a plant' (what drinks through the foot). कच्छपः 'a tortoise' (that always *protects* its *mouth* by drawing it in, at the approach of danger).
(2) सुषिच्यु ॥ The affix क comes after the root स्था when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix. Why do we make this two-fold division, when we see the second rule is included in the first as the verb स्था also ends in a long आ? The reason is that the first rule applies where the agent is indicated, while the second rule applies where condition is to be denoted. As आष्णुमुस्थानम् = आष्णुमुस्थः 'a swarm of rats'; so also शलमोस्थः 'a swarm of locusts'.

Both the words कर्मणि and सुषि are understood in the *sūtras* that follow: *vis*: the word कर्मणि in *sūtras* that relate to transitive verbs, and the word सुषि everywhere else.

तुन्दशोकयोः परिमृजापनुदोः ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तुन्द-शोकयोः, परिमृज-अपनुदोः, ( कर्मणि, कः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तुन्दशोकयोः कर्मणोरुपपदयोः परिमृजापनुदोर्धार्योः कप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ आलस्यसुखाहरणयोरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कप्रकरणे मूलविभुजादिभ्य उपसंख्यानम् ॥

5. The affix क comes after the verbs परिमृज 'to wash out' and अपनुद 'to drive away', when in composition with the words तुन्द 'navel' and शोक 'grief', as objects, respectively.

As तुन्द परिमृज आस्ते 'he lay lazy'. So also शोकापनुदः पुत्री जातः 'a son, destroyer of sorrow is born'.

*Vart.*—This affix is to be applied only then, when the meaning of the word to be formed is 'lazy' and 'giver of happiness'.

*Vart.*—The epithet तुन्द परिमृजः is applied to a lazy person; while तुन्द परिमार्जः means who clears his navel. So शोकापनुदः means giver of happiness, while शोकापनोदः means 'removal of sorrow'.

*Vart.*—The words मूलविभुजः 'a chariot' and the rest should be included in the subdivision of words formed by the affix क. The words belonging to this head can only be recognised by their form, there being no list of them to be found anywhere. Thus मूलविभुजः 'a chariot', मखमुचः 'a bow', काकगुह 'sesamums', कुमुदम् (कौ मोदते) 'a lotus'.

410

THE AFFIX TAK.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 6-8.]

प्रेदाजः ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रे, दा-जः, ( कर्मणि, कः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इदातेजानातेश्व धातोः प्रेणोपहृष्टात् कर्मण्युपपरे क्रमत्ययो भवति ॥

6. The affix क comes after the root श 'to give' and ज्ञ 'to know', when taking the preposition म and in composition with a word in the accusative case.

We applied by sutra 3 the affix क after verbs that ended in long आ and had no upasarga. Now begins the case of verbs with upasarga. This debars the affix अण्; as सर्वेषः (VI. 4. 64) 'giver of all; liberal', पथिमतः (VI. 4. 64) 'acquainted with roads'. The long आ of श and ज्ञ is elided by VI. 4. 64.

Why do we say 'when taking म'? With any other upasarga these verbs will take the general affix अण्; as गोसंशयः.

सनिश्चयः ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि सनि, स्वः, ( कर्मणि, कः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संपूर्वात् स्वया इत्येतस्मादातोः कर्मण्युपपरे क्रमत्ययो भवति ॥

7. The affix क comes after the root स्वया 'to tell', when preceded by the preposition सन्, and when the object is in composition with it.

The verb स्वया ends in long आ and by III. 2. 3 when compounded with an upasarga, it would have taken the affix अण्. This debars अण्; as गोसंख्या (VI. 4. 64) 'a cowherd' (गा संचटे).

गापोष्ठक ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ गा-पीः, टक्, ( कर्मणि, अनुपसर्गे ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गायतेः पिवतेश्व धातोः कर्मण्युपपरे अनुपसर्गे टक्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सुराशीघ्नीः पिवतेरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ बहुलं छन्दसि इति वक्तव्यम् ॥

8. The affix टक् comes after the verbs गै 'to sing' and पा 'to drink' when used without a preposition, and when the object is in composition with it.

The phrase anupasarga is to be read again into this sutra by anuvritti from sutra 3, though this anuvritti had temporarily lain dormant in sutra 6 and 7, as being unnecessary. This debars क; of this affix इ and क are indicatory the इ showing among others that the feminine is formed by the affix ङीप् (IV. 1. 14)

As, शक्रं गायति = शक्र+गा+टक्=शक्रगः (VI. 4. 64) 'who sings Sakra hymns'. सामगः 'singer of Sāma', fem. शक्रगी and सामगी ।

Vart.—The affix टक् comes after the verb पा when it means to drink and only when it is in composition with the words सुरा and शीघ्र as its object.

BK. III. CH. II. § 9.]

THE AFFIX ACH.

411

This is an important modification of the general sūtra. Thus सुरापः fem. सुरापी 'wine-bibber'; शीघुपः fem. शीघुपो 'spirit-drinker'.

Why do we say 'when in composition with surā and sidhu'? Observe श्रीरपा ब्राह्मणी 'the milk-drinking Brāhmaṇi'; formed by the affix क and the feminine, therefore, not formed by the affix ई but by आ.

Why do we say 'when पा means to drink'? When पा means 'to protect' this affix is not used; as सुरापा 'who protects wine'.

When these words are compounded with an upasarga they do not take टक् but अण्; as शक्रसंगायः, सामसंगायः।

Vart.—There is diversity in the Chhandas as to the employment of these affixes; as वा ब्राह्मणी सुरापी or सुरापा भवति नैनां देवाः पतिलोकं नयन्ति 'the gods do not carry that Brāhmaṇi to the regions of her husband who drinks wine'.

हरतेरनुद्यमनेऽच् ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ हरतेः, अनुद्यमने, अच्, ( कर्मणि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हरतेऽचिर्तुरनुद्यमने वर्त्तमानात् कर्मण्युपपदेश्युपस्थयो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ अच्युपकरणं शक्तिजागलाङ्कुशयटितोमरघटघटीधनुष्पु ग्रहैरपसंख्यानम् ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ सूत्रेण धार्यये ॥

9. The affix अच् comes after the verb हम् when it does not mean 'to raise up', when the object is in composition with it.

This debars अण्. The word उद्यमन means 'to raise a load'. Thus अंश हरति=अंशहरः 'who takes a share, or sharer'; so रिक्त्यहरः 'an heir'. (ह+अच्=हर+अ=हरः) (VII. 3. 84).

Why do we say 'when it does not mean to raise up'? For then the affix अण् will be employed; as भारहारः 'a burden-bearer, a porter'.

Vart.—This affix comes after the verb ग्रह when in composition with the words शक्ति 'spear', लाङ्कुल 'plough', अंकुश 'goad', यटि 'staff', तोमर 'an iron club', घट 'jar', घटी 'a small jar', धनुष 'a bow'; as शक्तिमहः 'a lancer', लाङ्कुलमहः 'a plough-man', अंकुशमहः 'an elephant driver', यटिमहः 'a staff-bearer', तोमरमहः 'a club-bearer', घटमहः, घटीमहः 'a jar-bearer', धनुमहः 'a bow-bearer'.

Vart.—This affix comes after the verb मह when the word सूत्र is in composition with it and the sense is that of 'holding'; as सूत्रमहः 'a thread-holder'. When it has not this meaning we have सूत्रमहः 'a thread-taker'.

वयसि च ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ वयसि, च, (हरतेः, कर्मणि, अच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वयसि गन्धमाने हरतेः कर्मण्युपपदेश्युपस्थयो भवति ॥

17

412

THE AFFIX ACH. [BK. III. CH. II. § 11, 12.

10. The affix अच् comes after the verb इन् when the object is in composition with it and when the meaning of the word to be formed is descriptive of age.

In this sūtra the verb इन् has the sense of udyamana which was specifically excluded in the last. The word वयस् means the condition of human body as dependent upon time. This rule applies to those words which indicate the attainment of appropriate age for the accomplishment of objects described by the upapada, or the reaching of that age in which the thing described by the upapada naturally takes place; as अस्थिहरः 'या 'the dog that has reached the age when it can chew bones' (lit. when it can raise it up); कवचहरः क्षणिकुमारः 'the Kshatriya boy old enough to wear (lit. 'to raise up or bear) the shield'; so that the verb here has the sense of 'raising up'.

आडि ताच्छील्ये ॥११॥ पदानि ॥ आडि, ताच्छील्ये, (कर्मणि, ह- रते:, अच् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आड पूर्वाद्भरते: कर्मण्युपपेक्ष्यप्यथो भवति ॥

11. The affix अच् comes after the verb इन् (when the object is in composition with it), the root taking the preposition अच्, and the sense of the word to be formed is inclination or accustomed occupation.

The word ताच्छील्यं means a natural inclination or habitual occupation; as पुष्पाहरः (पुष्प+आहरति=पुष्प+आहर) 'he who has a natural tendency towards fetching flowers or whose habitual occupation is to collect flowers'; so also फलाहरः ।

Why do we say 'when denoting inclination'? Otherwise the affix will be अच्; as भारताहरति=भारहारः 'who brings load'.

अहैः ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अहैः, ( कर्मणि, अच् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अहै पूजार्था, अस्माद्वातो: कर्मण्युपपेक्ष्यप्यथो भवति ॥

12. The affix अच् comes after the verb अहै 'to respect', when the object is in composition with it.

This debars अच्. The words so formed are especially of feminine gender. As पूजार्था 'deserving of respect'; so also गन्धार्था, मालार्था ।

स्तम्बकर्णयो रनिजपोः ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तम्ब-कर्णयोः, रनि- जपोः, ( सुपि, अच् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तम्बकर्ण इत्येतयोः सुबन्तयोःपपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोःपयोर्यथासंख्य रनिजपोः

वार्तिकम् ॥ हस्तिसूचक्योरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

BK. III. CH. II. § 13, 14]

THE AFFIX ACH.

413

13. The affix अच् comes after the verb रम् 'to sport' and जप् 'to whisper' when the case-inflected words स्तम्ब 'a clump of grass' and कर्ण 'ear' are in composition with them respectively.

The verb रम् is intransitive and the verb जप् can take an object under very limited circumstances; only namely when the object denotes Sabda; therefore in the case of both these verbs, the object cannot be in composition as an accusative case; therefore, the upapada here must be a general case-inflected word. Hence we have read the anuvritti of the word सुप् from sūtra 4 into this, the anuvritti of the word कर्म being inapplicable here.

Vart.—The words to be formed must have the sense of 'elephant' and a 'tale-bearer'. Thus स्तम्बेरमते=स्तम्बेरमः 'an elephant (lit. who sports in cluster of grass)' कर्ण जपति=कर्णजपः 'a slanderer (lit. who whispers in the ear)'.

The affix अच् is not employed when the words to be formed do not mean an 'elephant' and a 'traducer'. Thus स्तम्बे रन्ता 'who plays in clusters of grass'. कर्ण जपिता मशकः 'the mosquito that hums near the ear'.

शनि धातोः संज्ञायाम् ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शनि, धातोः, सं-ज्ञायाम्, ( अच् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शम्भुपपे धातुमात्रासंज्ञायां विपये ऽच्‌वस्ययो भवति ॥

14. The affix अच् is employed after the verbal roots when शम् 'well', is in composition, and the word to be formed denotes a name.

As शम्+कृ+अच्=शंकरः lit. 'who does good'. So also संमयः संवदः । All these are proper nouns.

Why have we repeated the word dhātu in this aphorism, when it was understood by anuvritti from sūtra III. 1. 91? To this the reply is, that the repetition of the word dhātu shows that there is prohibition of the affix ङ, that comes after the verb कृ in certain senses (III. 2. 20), when the word शम् is in composition. The affix अच् will be employed after the verb कृ and not the affix ङ, when शम् is an upapada, even when the sense to be indicated is that of cause, habit &c. (III. 2. 20). The result is that the feminine of शंकर will be शंकरा, and not शंकरा, which, had the affix been ङ, would have been the proper feminine (See IV. 1. 14). शंकरा means 'a female-ascetic,' 'a vulture' and 'one having the habit of doing good'.

अधिकरणे शेतेः ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अधिकरणे, शेतेः, (सुपि,अच् )॥

THE AFFIX TA.

वृत्तिः ॥ शेषं धीतोरधिकरणे सुबन्त उपपदे उष्मस्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ पार्श्वविष्णुसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ दिग्धसहपूर्वाच्च ॥

15. The affix अच् comes after the verb शौ 'to lie down' when in composition with a case-inflected word indicating location, i. e., in the locative case.

The word सुप् (III. 2. 4) a noun ending in a case-affix is understood in this aphorism. As खे शेषे = खगय: 'who lies in the sky'.

Vart.—The affix अच् comes after the verb शौ when in composition with the words पार्श्व 'ribs', &c., though not necessarily denoting location; as पार्श्वव्यो शेषे = पार्श्वव्यो: 'who reclines on his sides', उदरव्यो: 'who lies on his stomach', पृष्ठव्यो: 'who lies on his back'.

Vart.—And when the verb शौ is preceded by the word दिग्धसह; as दिग्धेन सह शेषे = दिग्धसहयाः ॥

Vart.—So also when the words उत्तान &c. are in composition with it denoting agent and in the nominative case. As उत्तान: शेषे = उत्तानव्यो: । अवमूर्द्धो शेषे = अवमूर्द्धव्यो: ।

Vart.—In the Chhandas the affix उच् comes after the verb शौ when in composition with the word गिरि in the locative. As गिरौ शेषे = गिरिदा: 'who lies on the mountain'.

The letter ब् of उच् is indicatory denoting that there is elision of the final vowel with what follows it (I. 1. 64).

चरेष्टः ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ चरेः, टः, ( अधिकरणे, सुपि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चरेधीतोरधिकरणे सुबन्त उपपदे उष्मस्ययो भवति ॥

16. The affix ट comes after the verb चर 'to go' when a case-inflected word in composition with it, denotes location.

The word adhikarana of the last sutra is understood in this. As कुरुषु चरति = कुरुचर: 'who goes among the Kurus'. मद्रचर: 'who goes among the Madras'.

Of the affix ट the real affix is अ, the letter ट being indicatory, showing that the feminine of these words is formed by the affix क्षेप्. (See. IV. 1. 14), as कुरुचरी, मद्रचरी ।

BK. III. CH. II. § 17-20.]

THE AFFIX TA.

415

भिक्षासेनादायेषु च ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ भिक्षा-सेना-आदायेषु,
च, (चरेः, टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भिक्षा सेना आशाय इश्येतेपूर्वेषु चरैर्धातोऽप्यस्यो भवति ॥

17. The affix ८ is employed after the verb चर 'to go', when the words in composition with it are भिक्षा 'alms', सेना 'army' and आशाय 'having taken'.

The *anuvritti* of the words 'in the locative case' does not extend to this aphorism, and hence the necessity of making a distinct and separate sutra.

Thus भिक्षाचरः 'a beggar' (who goes for alms); सेनाचरः 'one who goes with an army'; आशायचरः 'one who goes after having taken'.

पुरोऽप्यतोऽप्येषु सर्तेः ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुरस्-अप्रतस्-अप्रेषु, सर्तेः,
(टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुरस्-अप्रतस्-अप्रेषु इश्येतेपूर्वेषु सर्तैर्धातोऽप्यस्यो भवति ॥

18. The affix ८ comes after the verb च 'to move' when the words in composition with it, are पुरः, अमतः and अने, all meaning 'in front of or before'.

As पुरः सरति = पुरःसरः 'who goes in front, a harbinger'. So also अमतः सरः and अमसरः 'going in front, a leader'.

पूर्वे कर्तरि ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूर्वे, कर्तरि, (सर्तेः, टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वैश्च कर्तृशाचिन्युपपरे सर्तैर्धातोऽप्यस्यो भवति ॥

19. The affix ८ comes after the verb च 'to go', when पूर्व is in composition with it, denoting the agent.

Thus पूर्वः सरति = पूर्वसरः 'going in front'.

Why do we say 'denoting the agent'? Otherwise the affix अण्ण् will be employed. As पूर्वैश्च सरति = पूर्वसरः 'going to the east'.

कञ्चो हेतुताच्छील्यानुलोश्येषु ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ कञ्चः, हेतु-ता-
च्छील्य-आनुलोश्येषु, (कस्मैणि, टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मण्युपपरे करोतेर्धातोऽप्यस्यो भवति हेतो ताच्छील्ये आनुलोश्ये च गम्यमान् ॥

20. The affix ८ comes after the verb कृप 'to make' when the object is in composition with it denoting cause, habit and going with the grain (concession).

The word हेतु of this sutra means the final or conclusive cause, and is not the grammatical हेतु meaning agent. ताच्छील्य means habit, and literally, the

18

416

THE AFFIX TA.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 21.

act of being accustomed to that. आनुजोम्य comes from अनुजोम meaning 'with the hair', that is to say, regular, in natural order, successive, and hence favourable, and agreeable complaisance, acquiescence &c. Of हेतु, we have शोककरी कन्या 'the daughter that causes sorrow; यशस्करी विद्या 'honorable science'; कुजकर धन 'the family making wealth'. Of ताच्छ्रीत्य, we have आजकर: 'who performs obsequies'; अर्धकर: 'who amasses wealth'. Of आनुजोम्य, we have भैषकर: 'who promptly does what he is directed'; वचनकर: 'who regularly does what he is told'.

Why do we say 'when having these senses'? Otherwise the affix will be अणु. As कुम्भकार: 'potter', नगरकार: 'city-maker'.

दिवाविभानिशाप्रभाभास्कारान्तानन्तादिबहुनान्दीकिंलिपिलिबि-
बलिभक्तिकर्तृचित्रक्षेत्रसंख्याजङ्घावाहवहयेतद्गुरुरूपु ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥
दिवा-विभा-निशा-प्रभा-भास-कार-अन्त-अनन्त-आदि-बहु-नान्दी-किं-लिपि-
लिबि-बलि-भक्ति-कर्तृ-चित्र-क्षेत्र-संख्या-जङ्घा-बाहु-अहः-यत्-तत्-धनुस्-अ-
रूपु, (कग्मैषि, सुपि, करोते, टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिवाविषुपदेषु करोतेर्धातोऽप्यस्यो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ किं यतद्बहुषु कृमोऽन्विधानम् ॥

21. The affix c comes after the verb क 'to make when the following words are in composition with it:—
दिया 'by day', विभा 'light', निशा 'night', ममा 'splendour', भा: 'light', कार 'work', अन्त 'end', अनन्त 'endless', आदि 'beginning', बहु 'many', नान्दी 'benediction', किं 'what', लिपि 'writing', लिबि 'writing', बलि 'oblation', भक्ति 'devotion', कर्तृ 'agent', चित्र 'painting', क्षेत्र 'field', words denoting numerals, जङ्घा 'thigh', बाहु 'hand', अहः 'day', यत् 'what', तत् 'that', धनुस् 'bow' and अरुस् 'wound'.

Both the words 'karma' and 'sup' are understood in this aphorism; that is to say, sometimes these upapadas stand as accusative case and sometimes they have other cases, as the construction may require. This affix c comes when the sense is not that of cause &c., as it was in the last sutra.

Thus दिवाकर: 'the sun.' The word दिवा is an indeclinable and means 'in the day time'. There the upapada, therefore, is in the locative case. The sun is so called, because it makes creatures active in the day time.

So विभाकर: 'the sun' (light-maker); निशाकर: 'the moon' (the night-maker); प्रभाकर: 'the sun'; भास्कर: 'the sun' (the letter स is not changed into visarga, as it has been so read in the sutra); कारकर: 'agent'; अन्तकर: 'death' (end-maker); अनन्तकर: 'magnifying to any extent'; आदिकर: 'the creator'; बहकर: 'the busy'; नान्दीकर: 'the speaker of benediction'; किंकर: 'a servant'; लिपिकर: 'a

BK. III. CH. II. § 22, 23.] THE AFFIX TA.

417

scribe'; लिबिकर: 'a scribe'; बलिकर: 'offering sacrifice'; भक्तिकर: 'a devotee'; कर्तृकर: 'an agent'; चित्रकर: 'a painter'; क्षेत्रकर: 'a cultivator'; एककर: 'doing only one thing'; डिकर: 'doing two things'; विकर: 'doing three things'; जड्याकर: 'a runner, an express'; बाहुकर: 'a hero', 'a manual labourer'; अहस्कर: 'the sun'; तस्कर: 'doing that'; यस्कर: 'doing that'; धनुष्कर: 'bow-maker'; अहस्कर: 'causing or inflicting wounds'.

*Vart.*—The affix अच् comes after the verb क् when किम्, यत्, तद् and बहु are in composition with it. The speciality of ङ affix is that the feminine of words derived from it is formed by long ई; while the feminine of words derived by अच् is formed by long आ. Thus किंकरा, यस्करा, तस्करा and बहुकरा; these words might be said to belong to the अज्ञादि class (See IV. I. 31).

कर्मणि भूतौ ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्मणि, भूतौ, ( कर्मणि, करोतिः,

टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मशब्द उपपदे कर्मवाचिनि करोतेष्टप्रत्ययो भवति भूतौ गम्यमानायाम् ॥

22. The affix ङ comes after the verb क् 'to make', when the word कर्म is in composition with it, and the sense of the word to be formed is that of wages.

The word भूति means service for hire, wages. The word कर्म does not mean the grammatical object but the word-form कर्म; as कर्मकर: 'a hired labourer' (not a slave); otherwise the affix is अण्; as कर्मकार: 'an artisan'.

न शब्दश्लोककलहगाथा वैरचाटु सूत्रमंत्रपदेषु ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥

न, शब्द-श्लोक-कलह-गाथा-वैर-चाटु-सूत्र-मंत्र-पदेषु, (करोतिः, टः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शब्दादिषुपपदेषु करोतेष्टप्रत्ययो न भवति ॥

23. The affix ङ does not come after the verb क् 'to make', when the following words are in composition with it:—शब्द 'sound', श्लोक 'verse', कलह 'quarrel', गाथा 'praise', वैर 'enmity', चाटु 'flattery', सूत्र 'thread', मन्त्र 'hymns' and पद 'word'.

This prohibition relates even when the sense is that of cause, habit &c. The affix ङ being prohibited, the general affix अण् takes its place. As शब्दकार: 'sounding, sonorous'; श्लोककार: 'a verse-maker'; कलहकार: 'one who foments quarrels'; गाथाकार: 'a writer of Gāthās or prakritee verses'; वैरकार: 'an enemy'; चाटुकार: 'a flatterer'; सूत्रकार: 'an author of sūtras'; मन्त्रकार: 'a composer of Mantras'; पदकार: 'an author of Padapātha'.

418

THE AFFIX IN.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 24-26.

स्तम्बशक्तोरिन् ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तम्ब-शक्तोः, इन्, ( क-
नैषि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तम्ब शङ्कु, इरयेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योरिन्मययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ श्रीहिवल्लयोरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

24. The affix इन् comes after the verb क् when
the objects in composition with it, are the words स्तम्ब 'a
sheaf', and शङ्कु 'ordure'.

Thus स्तम्ब + क् + इन् = स्तम्बकरि nom. sing. स्तम्बकरि; so also शङ्कु करि.

*Vart.*—This rule is applicable when the sense of the words to be formed, is that of 'rice' and 'a calf' respectively. Therefore स्तम्बकरि: means 'rice', and शङ्कुकरि: 'a calf'.

When the words have not the senses of 'rice' and 'a calf', the affix अण् is employed. As स्तम्बकार: 'sheaf-maker', शङ्कुकार: 'ordure-maker'.

हरतेर्द्वृत्तिनाथयोः पशौ ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ हरतेः, द्वति-नाथयोः,

पशौ, ( कर्मणि, इन् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्वति नाथ इरयेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योः हरतेः श्लोः पशौ कर्तरि इन् पश्ययो भवति ॥

25. When the agent indicated is an animal,
the affix इन् comes after the verb इ 'to take', the object in
composition with it being the words इति 'a leather-bag'
and नाथ 'a master'.

Thus द्वतिहरि: 'a dog' (a carrier of skin); नाथहरि: 'a beast' (that carries its
master).

When the words formed do not denote an animal, the affix अण् is employed; as द्वतिहार: 'a water-carrier' (a carrier of a leather-bag for holding
water). नाथहार: 'a carrier of his master'.

फलेयहिरात्समभरिश्च ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ फलेयहिः-आत्ममभरिः,

च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ फलेयहिः आत्ममभरिः इरयेतो शब्दो निपाश्यते ॥

26. And the words फलेयहि and आत्ममभरि are irregularly formed.

The word फलेयहि: is formed by adding the affix इन् to the verb मह and
making the upapada end in the vowel ए. Thus फलानि गृह्णाति = फलेयहि: 'the
fruit-bearing *i. e.* a tree'.

BK. III. CH. II. § 27, 28.] THE AFFIX KHAS.

419

The word आत्ममम्रः is formed by adding the augment मुम् (म) to the upapada आत्म, and the affix इन् to the verb मुम्. Thus आत्मानं विमर्शि = आत्ममम्रः 'selfish' (one who feeds his own self).

The word 'and' indicates that there are other such irregularly-formed words. As कृत्तिमम्रः 'gluttonous, selfish' (earing to feed his own belly). उदरमम्रः 'gluttonous, selfish'.

छन्दसि वनसनरशिमथाम् ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, वन-सन-रशि-मथाम्, ( कर्मणि, इन् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वन सन संमन्तो, रक्ष पाञ्चने, मय विजोऽने, एतन्मः कर्तव्युपपरे छन्दसि विधये इन् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

27. In the Vedic literature, the affix इन् comes after the verbs वन् 'to honor' सन् 'to worship' रक्ष 'to protect' and मय 'to agitate', when the object is in composition.

Thus ब्रह्मवर्ति तथा क्षत्रवर्तिम् (Vaj. San. I. 17., V. 12., VI. 3); उत नो गोषभि (Rig. Ved. VI. 53. 10) ये ते इथानी पथिरन्तः (Rig. Ved. X. 14. 11) इन्द्रो यातुनामभवत् पाराशरो हविर्मधीनाम् (Rig. Ved. VII. 104. 21).

एजेः खश् ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ एजेः खश्, ( कर्मणि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एजु कम्पने इत्यस्मात् ण्यन्तारकर्मण्युपपरे खश्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ खश्प्रत्यये वातगुनीतिजशब्दे-व्यजभेद् तुषजशतीनामुपसंख्यानम् ॥

28. The affix खश् comes after the verb एजु 'to tremble' when ending in णि (III. 26.) and when the object is in composition with it.

This affix comes after the causative of एजु. Of the affix खश् the letters ख् and श् are indicatory, the real affix is अ. The ख् indicates that the augment मुम् is added to the upapada ending in a vowel (VI. 3. 67). The श् indicates that this is a Sārvadhātuka affix (III. 4. 113), and therefore the vikaraṇas like शप् &c. (III. 1. 68.) will be employed here. Thus अज्जमेजयति = अज्जमेजयः (अज्जः+एजि+शप्+खश्=अज्जम्+एजे+अ+अ) 'who awes the limbs'; जनमेजयः 'who awes mankind'.

*Vart:*—The affix खश् comes after the verbs अज् 'to go', भेद् 'to suck', तुष 'to strike', श् 'to leave' when in composition with the words वात 'wind', गुनी 'a bitch', तिल 'sesamum' and शार्द 'flatulence'. As वातमजा: शृगा: 'swift antelopes' (going with the wind); गुनीमथय: 'a bitch-sucker'; तिल-तुष: 'an oilman'; शार्द-खहा नावा: 'a kind of bean' (that causes or cures flatulence). The long ई of गुनी is shortened by VI. 3. 66.

19

420

THE AFFIX KHAS.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 29, 30.

नासिकास्तनयोः भमघेटोः ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ नासिका-स्तनयोः,

भमा-घेटोः, (कर्मणि, खश् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नासिकास्तनयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योः भमघेटोः खश् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ स्तने घेटः ॥ नासिकायान् भमघेटः ॥

29. The affix खश् comes after the verbs भा 'to blow' and घे 'to suck' when नासिका 'nose', and स्तन 'breast' are in composition with them as object.

The rule of *yathāsankhyā* as given in I. 3. 10 does not however, apply here. For स्तन is compounded with घेट; as (स्तन+घे+खश्=स्तन+मुम्+घे+शप्+खश्=स्तन+मुम्+घे+अ+अ)=स्तन+घः 'an infant' (sucking the breast).

But नासिका is compounded with both भा and घे; as नासिका+भा+खश्=नासिक+मुम्+घे+अ (VI. 3. 66 and 67; VII. 3. 78)=नासिकधः 'blowing and breathing through the nose'. So also नासिकधः 'drinking through the nose'.

That the rule of *yathāsankhyā* does not apply here, is indicated by the irregular construction of the *Dvandva* compound नासिकास्तनयोः. By rule II. 2. 84. the word स्तन containing fewer syllables ought to have stood first; one irregularity lets in another.

The feminine of स्तनधः is स्तनधः, as the verb घे has an indicatory द्।

नाडीमुण्डयोश्च ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ नाडी-मुण्डयोः, च, (कर्मणोः,

भमा-घेटोः, खश् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नाडी मुष्टि इत्येतयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योः भमघेटोः खश् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

30. And when the words नाडी 'a tube' and मुष्टि 'fist' are objects in composition with the verbs भा and घे, the affix खश् is employed.

Here also the irregularly-formed *Dvandva* compound नाडीमुष्टि shows the non-applicability of the rule of *yathāsankhyā*; for मुष्टि being a घि ought to have stood first (II. 2. 32).

Thus नाडिन्धः 'blowing through the tube'; मुष्टिन्धः 'blowing through the fist'; नाडिन्ध्यः 'sucking through the tube', an infant; मुष्टिन्ध्यः 'an infant'.

The word 'and' in the aphorism indicates that there are other words also so formed. Thus घटिन्धः, घटिन्ध्यः, खारिन्धः, खारिन्ध्यः, वातन्धः, वातन्ध्यः, 'a mountain'.

This sūtra is not Pāṇini's, but is really a Vārtika, raised to the rank of a sūtra by the author of the Kāsikā. The Vārtikakārā divides the last sūtra in this way: (1) स्तने घेटः ॥ (2) स्तो मुट्टी भमघ ॥ (3) नासिकायां भमघेटः ॥ (4) नाडी मुष्टि घटोखारिचित्ति वक्तव्यम् ॥

BK. III. CH. II. § 31-34.]

THE AFFIX KHAS.

421

उदि कूले रजिबहोः ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदि, कूले, रजि-वहोः,
( खग ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रजि भजु, वह प्रापणे, एताम्यापुण्यभ्यो कूले कर्मण्युपपे खगप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

31. The affix खग comes after the verbs रज 'to break into pieces' and वह 'to carry', when preceded by the upasarga उन्, and the word कूल 'bank' is in composition with them as the object.

Thus कूलमुद्गजति = कूलमुद्गजः 'breaking down banks' (such as a chariot, river, elephant, &c.); कूलमुद्गहः 'tearing up or carrying away the bank'.

वहासे लिहः ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ वह-अये, लिहः ॥ ( खग ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वह अब इरवेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपययोः लिहेधातोः खगप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

32. The affix खग comes after the verb लिह 'to lick' when the object in composition with it, is the word वह 'the shoulder of an ox' or अब 'a cloud'.

As वहलिहो गोः 'the shoulder-licking cow'; अब लहो वायुः 'the cloud-licking wind'.

परिमाणे पचः ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ परिमाणे, पचः, (कर्मणि, खग ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिमाणे मस्यापि, तस्मिन्कर्मण्युपपे पचेः खगप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

33. The affix खग comes after the verb पच 'to cook' when the object in composition with it denotes a measure.

Thus प्रस्थं पचति = प्रस्थंपचः 'a pot having the capacity to cook a *prastha* of food'; so also द्रोणपचः, खारिम्पचः 'a kettle'.

मितनखे च ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ मित-नखे, च, ( पचः, खग ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मित नख इरवेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपययोः पचेः खगप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

34. The affix खग is employed after the verb पच, when मित 'a measured partition' or नख 'a nail' is the word in composition with it as an object.

The aphorism has its scope when the words formed do not denote measures, which was the case in the last sutra. Thus मितम्पचा ब्राह्मणो 'the Brāhmaṇi who cooks a little *i. e. a.* niggardly Brāhmaṇi'; नखम्पचा यवागुः 'the nail-scorching barley gruel'.

विध्वरुषोस्तुदः ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ विधु-अरुषो, तुदः, ( कर्मणि,

खग ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विधु अरुष इरवेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपययोः तुदेधातोः खगप्रस्थयो भवति ॥

422

THE AFFIX KHAS.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 35-37.

35. The affix खण् comes after the verb तुव् 'to strike', when विधु 'the moon' or अरुस् 'a wound' is the word in composition with it as object.

As विधुनुवः राहुः 'the Rāhu that eclipses the moon ; अरुनुवः 'corrosive, wounding the vital parts'. For the addition of the augment मुम् after the word अरुस्, see VI. 3. 67.

असूर्यललाटयेद्रृगितपोः ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ असूर्य-ललाटयोः, दृगि-तपोः, (कर्मणि, खण्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ असूर्यजलाट इरयेतयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योः दृगितपोर्धार्योः खण्। यययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययययय

36. The affix खण् comes after the verb इष् 'to see' and तप् 'to heat' when असूर्य and जलाट are the words in composition with them respectively as objects.

Thus असूर्य+इश्+खण्=असूर्यम्पद्यः; as असूर्यम्पद्यया राजवारा 'the king's wives not even seeing the sun' (being shut up in the harem, and so having no opportunity of seeing the sun, that is, they are so well protected that even the sun cannot see them, much less any irreverent gaze).

So also जलाटन्तप्: 'heating the fore-head' (such as the sun).

The word असूर्य is an incomplete or impossible compound, as the negative अ applies to the verb इश् and not to the word सूर्य. This is in opposition to the rule of *samartha pada vidhi* (II. 1. 2).

उगम्पद्येरस्मदपाणिन्धमाश्च ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ उगम्पद्य-इरस्मद-पाणिन्धमाः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उगम्पद्य इरस्मद पाणिन्धम इरयेतो शब्बा निपात्यन्ते ॥

37. The words उगम्पद्य, इरस्मद and पाणिन्धम are irregularly formed.

Thus इष् पद्यति = उगम्पद्यः 'fierce-looking'; इरया भवति = इरस्मद: 'delighting in drinking an epithet of Agni, a flash of lightning'. So पाणिन्धमाः पध्यानः 'chilly roads'.

प्रियवशे वदः खच् ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रिय-वशे, वदः, खच् ॥

BK III. CH. II. § 38, 39.]

THE AFFIX KHACH.

423

38. The affix खच् comes after the verb वष 'to speak' when मिथ or वश is the word in composition with it as an object.

Thus मिथ वशति=मिथवष: 'who speaks kindly'; वशवष: 'who professes submission'.

Of the affix खच्, the letters ख् and च् are indicatory; ख् indicates the insertion of the augment मुम् (VI. 3. 37), and च् shows that there is shortening of the vowel in certain cases (VI. 4. 94).

In the case of मिथ and वश with वष, the affix खश् would have given the same result as the affix खच्. Making a separate affix in this sutra is for the sake of the aphorisms that follow, where this affix will produce different effects than खश्.

Vart.—The affix खच् comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when a word ending in a case-affix is in composition with it. As मितगमो हस्ती 'the slow-moving i. e. an elephant'; मितगमा हस्तिनी 'the slow-moving i. e. a she-elephant'.

Vart.—This affix comes under similar circumstances when the word in composition with गम् is विहायस्; and the letter is then replaced by the word विह. As विहायसा गच्छति=विहंगम: 'a bird (that which goes through the sky)'.

Vart.—In the Vārtikas above given, the affix खच् may optionally be considered as if it had an indicatory ङ. The force of ङ is to cause elision of the final vowel with what follows it. As विहंग: or विहंगम: 'a bird'. So also भुजंगम: or भुजंग: 'a serpent' (what goes crookedly).

Vart.—विहायस् is replaced by विह when the affix ङ (III 2. 48) comes after the verb गम्; as विहंग: 'a bird'. Thus we have three forms: विहंग, विहङ्ग, विहङ्गम।

द्विषत्परयोस्तापेः ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्विषत्-परयोः, तापे,

(खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्विषत्परयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योस्तापेर्धातोः खच्पत्ययो भवति ॥

39. The affix खच् comes after the verb ताप् 'to heat', when द्विषत् or पर is the word in composition with it as an object.

The verb तप् belongs both to Bhū and Chur classes. Both are meant in the sutra. In the case of Bhūḍdi, the verb तापि is the causative ending in णि of तप्; while in Churādi, all verbs take णि.

Thus द्विषन्तं तापयति=द्विषन्तपः (VI. 4. 94) 'one who destroys his enemies', so also परन्तपः 'one who subdues his enemies, a hero'.

This affix however, will not apply when the above upapadas are in the feminine gender. In this case the general affix अण् will be employed; as द्विपतीं लापयति = द्विपतीलापः।

वाचि यतो व्रते ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ वाचि, यमः, व्रते, (खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वाक्प्राप्ते कर्मण्युपपत्ते यमेधात्तोः खच्प्रत्ययो भवति व्रते गन्धमाने ॥

40. The affix खच् comes after the verb यम् 'to curb' when the word वाक् 'speech' is in composition with it as object, and the sense indicated is that of a vow.

The word व्रत means a vow taken according to the rules of Dharma-sāstra. Thus वाच्यं आस्तं 'he has taken the vow of rigid silence'.

Why do we say 'vow'? Otherwise the form is वाग्यामः 'restraining speech' (VI. 3. 69).

पूः सर्वयोर्दारिसहोः ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूः-सर्वयोः, दारि-सहोः,

(खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुर् सर्व इत्येतयोः कर्मणोऽपपद्योर्धयासंख्यं वारिसहोर्धात्तोः खच्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ भगे च दारिरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

41. The affix खच् comes after the verbs वारि 'to split' and सह 'to bear' when respectively in composition with the words पुर् 'a city' and सर्व 'all', as objects.

As पुर् वारयति = पुरन्दरः 'name of Indra (who splits as under cities)' (VI. 3. 69 and VI. 4. 94); सर्वसहो राजा 'the king who is all-forbearing'.

Vart.—So also when the word भग is in composition with the verb वारि; as भगन्दरः 'a fistula in the anus'.

सर्वकूलाश्रकरीषेषु कपः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्व-कूल-अश्र-करिषेषु,

कषः, (खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्व कूल अश्र करिष इत्येतेषु कर्मण्युपपत्तेषु कपेधात्तोः खच् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

42. The affix खच् comes after the verb कप 'to rub' when the words सर्व 'all', कूल 'bank', अश्र 'cloud' and करिष 'a dry cow-dung', are in composition with it as object.

As सर्वकषः खलः 'a villain, a rogue'; कूलकषा नदी 'a river'; अश्रकषो गिरिः 'a mountain'; करिषकषा वाग्या 'a strong wind'.

BK. III. CH. II. § 43-45] THE AFFIX KHACH.

मेघन्तिभयेषु कजः ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ मेघ-ऋति-भयेषु, कजः,

(खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मेघ ऋति भय इत्येतेषु कर्मसुपपत्तेषु कजः खच् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उपपदविधौ भवादिमहणं तदन्तविधि प्रयोजयति ॥

43. The affix खच् comes after the verb क् 'to make' when the words मेघ 'cloud', ऋति 'misfortune' and भय 'fear' are in composition as objects.

As मेघकरः 'producing clouds'; ऋतिकरः 'giving pain'; भयंकरः 'frightful'.

*Vart.*—The *tadanta vidhi* applies in the case of upapadas like भय. &c. This is an exception to the *vārtika* under I. I. 72. by which, in the case of affixes, *tadanta-vidhi* was prohibited. Thus we have अभयंकरः 'who causes security'.

श्वेतप्रियमद्रेण् च ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ श्वेत-प्रिय-मद्रे, अण्, च,

(खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ श्वेत प्रिय मद्र इत्येतेषु कर्मसुपपत्तेषु करोत्तेरण् प्रत्ययो चकारात् खच् ॥

44. And the affix अण् as well as खच् comes after the verb क् 'to make' when the words श्वेत 'happiness', प्रिय 'pleasant' and मद्र 'joy' are in composition as objects.

The word 'and' denotes that the affix खच् is also to be included.

Thus श्वेतकारः or श्वेतंकरः 'propitious'; प्रियकारः or प्रियंकरः 'showing kindness'; मद्रकारः or मद्रंकरः 'causing delight'.

The repetition of the affix अण्, when its *anuvritti* could have been read into this sutra by using the word वा 'optionally', indicates that these words never take the affix ङ of sutra 20 though cause, habit, &c., may be denoted; so that the feminine of those words is formed by आ and not by ई; as अल्पारम्भाः श्वेतकराः 'small beginnings lead to or cause prosperity'.

आशिते भुवः करणभावयोः ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आशिते, भुवः, करण-

भावयोः, (खच्, सुपि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आशितशब्दे सुबन्ते उपपत्ते भवतेथीतीः करणे भावे चाये खच् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

45. The affix खच् comes after the verb भू 'to be' when in composition with the case-inflected word आशित 'satisfied by eating' and the sense is that of instrument or condition.

The word 'सुपि' of sutra 4 is understood here.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 46, 47.

Thus आशिर्लभः meaning 'food', literally that by which one is satiated.
आशिती भवती अनेन. Here the word denotes instrument. And आशिर्लभः also means 'satiety', which denotes condition.

संज्ञायां भूतवृजिधारिसहितपिदमः ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ संज्ञायां, भू-तू-बृ-जि-धारि-सहि-तपि-दमः, (कर्मणि, सुषि, खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भू-तू-बृ-जि-धारि-सहि-तपि-दम इत्येतेभ्यो धातुभ्यः संज्ञायां विषये खच् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

46. The affix खच् comes after the following verbs when the words to be formed denote a name:—viz. भू 'to bear', दू 'to cross over', बृ 'to choose', जि 'to conquer', धारि 'to hold', सहि 'to bear', तपि. 'to heat' and दम 'to subdue'.

Both the words कर्मणि and सुषि of sūtra 1 and 4 are understood here and should be applied as the occasion requires. Thus विद्वन्मा 'earth' (that which supports all); रघुनाथ 'the Rathantara Sāma'; पतिवरा 'a girl' lit. (who is about to choose a husband); शत्रुजयः 'an elephant' lit. (who conquers the enemy); युगधरः 'a mountain' or 'the pole of a carriage to which the yoke is fixed'; शत्रुसहः 'Satrunsaha' (withstanding an enemy); शत्रुतपः 'Satruntapa' (destroying an enemy); अरिदमः 'Arindama' (victorious).

Why do we say 'when denoting a name'? Observe कुटुम्बभारः 'he who supports his family'.

गमश्च ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ गमः, च, (सुषि, संज्ञायां, खच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गमेधौतोः सुन्दुपपदे संज्ञायां विषये खच् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

47. And the affix खच् comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix, and when the word to be formed denotes a name.

As सुतंगमः 'Sutangama'. Though the verb गम् could well have been included in the last aphorism, the separation serves the purpose of carrying the *anuvritti* of गम् into the subsequent sūtras.

अन्तात्यन्ताश्वदूरपारसर्वानन्तेषु डः ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्त-अत्यन्त-अध्वन्-दूर-पार-सर्व-अनन्तेषु, डः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्त-अत्यन्त-अध्वन्-दूर-पार-सर्व-अनन्त इत्येतेषु कर्मसुपपत्तेषु गमेऽपश्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ इ प्रकरणे सर्ववपन्नयोऽपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उरसो ओपश्च ॥

BK. III. CH. II. § 48.] THE AFFIX DA.

427

वार्तिकम् ॥ सुहृरोरधिकरणे ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ निरोद्देशे ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उपकरणेऽन्येष्वपि दृश्यते ॥

48. The affix ङ comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when in composition with the following words as its objects :—अन्त 'end', अत्यन्त 'excessive', अचन् 'road', दूर 'far', पार 'across', सर्व 'all' and अनन्त 'endless'.

The anuvritti of the word संज्ञायाम् does not extend to this. As अन्तः 'having gone to the end, thoroughly conversant'; अचन्नः 'going too fast'; अच्नः 'a way-farer'; दूरः 'going to a distant place'; पारः 'completely familiar'; सर्वः 'going everywhere, the Supreme Being'; अनन्तः 'going to infinity, moving for ever'.

Of the affix ङ the letter ङ is indicatory, the real affix being अ. The ङ indicates that the ङ portion of the word to which this is added, must be elided (VI. 4. 143); as अन्त+गम्+ङ=अन्त+ग्+अ (the ङ portion अम् of गम् is elided). Now though the rule VI. 4. 143 says 'when that which has an indicatory ङ, follows, there is elision of the ङ of a अ'; yet in the present case, such elision takes place, although the word गम् here is not one of those called अ (I. 4. 18); because the presence of ङ as an indicatory letter must not be unmeaning.

Vart.—The ङ is also employed when the words in composition are सर्वत्र 'everywhere' and पन्न 'creeping'; as सर्वत्रः 'Supreme Spirit'; पन्नः 'snake'.

Vart.—So also when the word in composition is उरस् 'breast', and there is elision of its final. As उरस्+गम्+ङ=उरगः 'moving on breast, a snake'.

Vart.—So also with the words सु 'well' and दूर 'bad', when the resulting words denote location. As सुगः 'that in which one goes easily, easy of access'. दुर्गः 'difficult of access, a fort'.

Vart.—So also with the preposition निर्, the word to be formed meaning country; as निगः 'a country'.

Vart.—Others say, that this ङ is added when other words besides the above stand as upapadas. Thus स्थगागः (क्षी+अगार+गम्+ङ) 'who goes to the women's compartment'; मानः 'going to the village'; गुहतल्पः 'who pollutes the bed of his guru'.

आशिषि हनः ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ आशिषि, हनः, (ङः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आशिषि गम्यमानायां हन्तेऽर्थोः कर्मण्युपपदे ङ प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ दारावाहनोऽप्यन्तस्य च टः संज्ञायाम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ चारो वा ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कर्मणि सनि च ॥

21

428

THE AFFIX DA.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 49-51.]

49. The affix ङ comes after the verb हन् 'to kill', when the object is in composition with it, and when benediction is intended.

The affix ङ is understood in this sūtra. Thus तिमिं बध्यात्=तिमिहः 'may he kill the whale'; शत्रुहः 'may he kill the enemy'.

Why do we say 'when benediction is intended'? Otherwise we have शत्रुधातः 'who kills his enemy'.

Vart.—The affix अण् comes after the verb आहन् when the word बारु 'wood' is in composition with it, and the final letter of the word so formed is changed into ङ, when the word so formed denotes a name. As बारु आहन्ति=वार्वाघाटः (बारु+आहन्+अण्) 'the wood-pecker'.

Vart.—So also optionally when the word चारु 'beautiful' is in composition under the circumstances detailed in the last vārtika: as चार्वाघाटः or चार्वाघातः।

Vart.—So also, when the verb हन् is preceded by the preposition सन्, and is in composition with a word in the objective case, the affix अण् is employed; and the final is replaced by ङ; as वर्णान् संहन्ति=वर्णसंघाटः or वर्णसंघातः 'the alphabet'; पदानि संहन्ति=पदसंघाटः or पदसंघातः 'connecting the words that are separated, an annotator'.

अपे क्लेशतमसोः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ अपे, क्लेश-तमसोः, ( कर्मणि, हनः, ङः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपपूर्वाञ्चन्तेः क्लेशतमसोः कर्मणोरुपपदयोऽन्त्यथो भवति ॥

50. The affix ङ comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when it is compounded with the preposition अप्, and when the object in composition with it, is the word क्लेश 'pain' or तमस् 'darkness'.

As, क्लेशापहः पुनः 'the pain-allayer i. e. the son'; शमोपहः सूर्यः 'the darkness-destroyer i. e. the sun'.

This aphorism has its scope when the sense is not that of benediction.

कुमारशीर्षयोश्चिनिः ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ कुमार-शीर्षयोः, शिनिः, (हनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कुमार शीर्षं द्रव्येतयोरुपपदयोः हन्तीर्णनिः प्रत्यथो भवति ॥

51. The affix शिनि comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the word in composition with it is कुमार 'a child', or शीर्ष 'head'.

BK. III. CH. II. § 52, 53.] THE AFFIX TAK.

429

Thus कुमार+हन्+पिनि=कुमार+घात+हन् (VII. 3. 54 and VII. 3. 32) = कुमारघातिन् nom. sing. कुमारघाती 'child-killer'. So also शीर्षघातिन् nom. sing. शीर्ष-घाती 'head-killer'.

The word शीर्ष is an irregular form of the word शिरस्।

लक्षणे जायापत्योष्टक् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ लक्षणे, जाया-पत्योः, टक्, (हनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हन्तेजायापत्योः कर्मणोः रूपपद्योः लक्षणवतिकर्तिरि टक्पत्ययो भवति ॥

52. The affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when it is in composition with the word जाया 'wife' or पति 'husband' as object, and when the word so formed denotes the agent possessed of that attribute (or when the word so formed denotes a mark).

The word लक्षण of this sutra gives rise to the doubt whether it means लक्षण कर्तिरि or लक्षणवति कर्तिरि. In the former case the meaning will be 'when the agent is itself the mark'; as जायाचनः 'a mole' (a mark on the body indicative of the death of one's wife). In the latter case the meaning will be 'when the agent is possessed of the attribute denoted by the word'; as जायाचनः 'the murderer of his wife'; पतिवृत्ती 'the murderer of her husband'.

Of the affix टक् the letters ट् and क् are indicatory. The ट् shows that the feminine is formed by है, and क् causing elision of the penultimate अ of हन्. Thus जाया+हन्+टक्=जाया+हन्+अ (VI. 4. 98) = जायाचनः (VII. 3. 54).

अमनुष्यकर्तृके च ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ अ-मनुष्य-कर्तृके, च, (टक, हनः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अमनुष्यकर्तृके वर्तमानादन्तेद्वीतोः कर्मणोपपद्योः टक्पत्ययो भवति ॥

53. And the affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the object is in composition with it, and when the word to be formed denotes an agent other than a human being.

As जायाचनस्तिलकालकः 'the mole' (literally that which indicates the death of one's wife); पतिवृत्ती पाणिरेखा 'the line of the palm of the hand' (that which indicates the death of one's husband). These two forms were deducible also from the last aphorism. श्लेष्मघ्नं मधु 'honey' (literally that which has the property of destroying the phlegm). पिसघ्नं घृतं 'clarified butter' (lit. that which destroys the bile).

Why do we say 'when the agent is not a human being'? Observe भाखुपातः शत्रुः 'a Sūdra' (literally one who kills the mice). Here the affix is अणु.

430

THE AFFIX KHYUN. [BK. III. CH. II. § 54, 55.

Why is the affix टक् not employed in the following? चौरपातो हस्ती 'an elephant' (i. e. who kills a thief.) Here the word is formed by the affix अणु on the analogy of sutra III. 3. 113 which allows a diversity in case of *kritya* affixes, which diversity is extended in this case to a *krit* affix.

शक्ती हस्तिकपा(वा)टयोः ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शक्ती, हस्ति-कपा-(वा)टयोः, (हन्तः, टक्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शक्ती गन्धमानार्था हस्तिकपा(वा)टयोः कर्मणोरुपपद्योर्हन्तेऽकृपत्ययो भवति ॥

54. The affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the word in composition with it as its object is हस्ती 'elephant' or कपाट 'gate' and when the sense indicated is that of power.

This sutra applies where the agent is a human being. As हस्तिनं हन्तुं शक्तः=हस्तिघ्नः मनुष्यः 'a man who is strong enough to kill an elephant'; so also कपाटघ्नः 'a burglar' (who is capable of breaking open the doors).

Why do we say 'where power is indicated'? Observe विशेष्य हस्तिनं हन्ति = हस्तिपातः 'who kills the elephant by poison'. Here the affix is अणु.

पाशिघताडघौ शिल्पिनि ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ पाशिघ-ताडघौ, शिल्पिनि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पाशिघ ताडघ इत्येवौ शव्यौ निपाश्चैव शिल्पिनि कर्तरि ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ राजघ उपसंख्यानम् ॥

55. The words पाशिघ and ताडघ are irregularly formed when denoting an artificer.

These forms are thus evolved. The affix क is employed after the verb हन् in composition with पाशिघ 'hand' and ताड 'a blow' as object; then the ि portion of हन् i. e. अन् is elided, and ह is changed into घ irregularly. Thus पाशिघ+हन्+क=पाशिघ+ह+अ=पाशिघः 'a drummer' (workman or handicraftsman); ताडघः 'a smith'.

Why 'when denoting an artificer'? Observe पाशिघातः 'boxing'; ताडघातः 'hammering'.

*Vart:*—The word राजघः should be enumerated in this connection; राजघः 'a regicide'.

आढघसुभगस्थूलपलितनगनान्धप्रियेषु चव्ययैष्वच्यौ (कजः करखे स्युन् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ आढघ-सुभग-स्थूल-पलित-नगन-अन्ध-प्रियेषु, चित्र-अ-यैषु, अच्यौ, कजः, करखे, स्युन् ॥

BK. III. CH. II. § 56.]

THE AFFIX KHYUN.

431

वृत्तिः ॥ आख्याविषु कर्मसुपपवेषु च्ययथैव च्ययन्तेषु करोतेर्ज्ञातोः करणो कारके ख्युनुमस्ययो भवति ॥

56. The affix ख्युन, when the sense of the word to be formed is that of an instrumental agent, comes after the verb क् 'to make', when the following words are in composition with it as objects:—आद्य 'rich', सुगम 'fortunate', स्थूल 'big', पलित 'grey', नम 'naked', अन्य 'blind' and प्रिय 'pleasant', provided that these words have the sense of the words formed by the affix चित्र, though not actually ending in the affix चित्र.

The affix चित्र (V. 4. 50.) is added to a noun when it is in composition with the verbs भू 'to become', क् 'to make' and अस् 'to be'; its force being that a thing attains to a condition in which it previously was not. The चित्र being an optional affix, its sense is two-fold; namely, words ending in चित्र and words not ending in चित्र. Both may have the force of चित्र. In the present sutra, however, the words that actually end in चित्र have been excluded, while words which do not take the affix चित्र, but have the force of चित्र are included in the present sutra.

Thus आद्य + क् + ख्युन = आद्य + कर + अन् = आद्य करण 'that by the instrumentality of which the poor becomes rich, viz., wealth, prosperity, means of enriching'; सुगमकरणम् 'making happy'; स्थूलकरणम् 'by which one becomes big'; पलितकरणम् 'rendering grey'; नमकरणं 'making naked'; अन्यकरणम् 'making blind'; प्रियकरणम् 'showing kindness'.

Why do we say 'when the force is that of the affix चित्र'? Otherwise आद्य लैलेन कुर्वन्ति *i. e.* अन्यजयन्ति 'they anoint with oil'. Here though something is joined with what it previously was not joined, namely with oil, yet as the radical word is not prominent here, the sense is not that of चित्र and hence this counter-example.

Why do we say 'when not ending in the affix चित्र'? Observe आद्यौ कुर्वन्ति अनेन 'they make rich by this'. Here the affix ख्युन is not employed.

It might be objected: 'well if ख्युन is not used, then the affix ख्युन must be used (III. 3. 117) as there is no difference between ख्युन and ख्युन; both having the efficient portion ख्; what is then the use of prohibiting चित्र? We reply, 'because there is this prohibition, when the affix ख्युन is not employed the affix ख्युन will also be not employed. Thus by implication the affix ख्युन is also prohibited. The prohibition of चित्र in this sutra is for the sake of the aphorisms that follow'.

22

432.

THE AFFIX KVIN.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 57, 58.

Pātanjali observes this prohibition as superfluous; because there is no distinction between ल्यूद and ख्यून. For the word formed by any one of these affixes have the same form and the same accent. Nor there is any distinction in the feminines of their derivatives. For the word formed by नम्, स्नम्, ईक्, अक् and ख्यून take ई in the feminine as well as the words तरुन and तजन. Nor there is any distinction in their *samāsas*. For in both the cases it will be *nitya samāsa*. Nor is the prohibition made for the sake of the augment मुन. For it being an indeclinable, मुन cannot come after it. The prohibition therefore is of no use to this sūtra but it is inserted here for the sake of the following sūtras.

कर्तेरि भुवः खिण्णुचु खुकजौ ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तेरि, भुवः, खिण्णुचु खुकजौ, (आद्यादिषु) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आद्यादिषु सुबन्तेपुपपवेषु च्यर्थश्च च्ययन्तेषु भवतेऽर्थोः कर्तेरि कारके खिण्णुचु खुकज इत्यतो प्रत्ययो भवतः ॥

57. The affixes खिण्णुचु and खुकज, when the word to be formed denotes an agent, come after the verb मु 'to become', when it is in composition with words आद्य &c., provided that these have the sense of the words formed by the affix चि though not ending in चि.

Thus आद्यमविष्णुः 'becoming rich (who was not rich before)'; आद्यम-भावुकः 'becoming rich'; सुभगमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming happy'; स्युजमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming big'; पल्लिमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming grey'; गन्तमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming naked'; अनमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming blind'; प्रियमविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming an object of affection, amiable'.

Why do we say 'when denoting the agent'? Not so when it denotes the instrument. The affixes will apply when the sense of the upapada is that of चि, otherwise not; as आद्यो भविता 'he will be rich'.

These affixes will not apply when the upapada ends in चि; आद्यो भविता।

स्पृशोऽनुदके किन् ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्पृशः, अनुदके, किन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्पृशोऽनुदके सुबन्तेपुपपवेषि किन्त्यस्यो भवति ॥

58. The affix किन् comes after the verb स्पृश 'to touch', when it is in composition with a case-inflected word other than उदक 'water'.

By sūtra 4 of this chapter, the *anuvritti* of the word सुषि is to be read into this sūtra. It might be objected 'why do we not read the *anuvritti* of the word कर्म instead of सुषि, because the verb स्पृश is a transitive verb, and after

BK. III. CH. II. § 59.]

THE AFFIX KVIN.

433

such verbs, the anuvritti of कर्म ought to come by sūtra 4'? To this we say there is no harm in reading the anuvritti of सुषि in this case; because the word कर्तरि of the last sūtra is also, in a way understood here, and indicates the collection of all sorts of agents whether objects, instruments &c., and this can only be when the first member of the compound is a word in general.

Thus पूतं स्युराति = पूतस्यु, nom. sing. पूतस्युक् 'he who touches clarified butter'. स्पृश् + किन् + सु = स्पृश् + वि + ० (VI. 1. 68) = स्पृक् + ० (VI. 1. 67, and VIII. 2. 62). So also मन्त्रेण स्युराति = मन्त्रस्युक् 'who touches with hymns'; जज्ञेन स्युराति = जज्ञस्युक् 'who touches with water'. But उदकेन स्युराति = उदकस्पृश्; here we have the general affix अण्.

The न् of किन् is to distinguish this affix from affixes like किप् &c. For, had it been merely कि, then in sūtra VIII. 2. 62. we should have used कि प्रत्ययस्थ क्; and it would have been ambiguous, for कि might be explained as meaning both कि and किप्, as क्य means क्यप्, क्यप् &c. To remove this ambiguity, न् is added to make a distinctive affix. The न् cannot be for the sake of accent. (VI. 1. 117), the verb being monosyllabic would of itself have taken that accent.

ऋत्विग्दधृकस्रग्दिगुथिगांचुयुजिकुञ्चां च ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥

ऋत्विक्-दधृक्-स्वक्-दिक्-उणिक्-अञ्चु-युजि-कुञ्चान्, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋत्विगादयः पञ्चरान्नाः किञ्चस्ययान्ता निगलयन्ते अपरे नयो धातवो निर्दिश्यन्ते ॥

59. The words ऋत्विक् 'a domestic priest', दधृक् 'impudent', लक् 'a garland', विक् 'a direction' and उणिक् 'a quatrain' are irregularly formed by adding the affix किन्; and so also after the verbs अञ्चु 'to worship', युजि 'to join' and कुञ्च 'to approach', the affix किन् is employed.

The first five words are irregular forms. Thus ऋतु + यज् + किन् = ऋत्विक् 'he who performs sacrifice in the season (ऋतो) or to the season (ऋतुम्). This word, however is a कष्ट word in which it is fruitless to search for its etymological meaning. धृष् + किन् = दधृक्. Here there is reduplication and the final has acute accent. खज् + किन् = लक्. Here there is augment अम्. दृग् + किन् = विक्. So also उत् + सिन्ह् + किन् = उणिक्. All these are in fact crude nouns, their current meaning having little traces of their root meaning.

The affix किन् comes after the three roots युज्, अञ्चु, and कुञ्च. Being read along with the five above-mentioned irregularly-formed words, there is some irregularity in the application of किन् to these verbs. Thus the affix किन् comes after अञ्चु only when a word ending with any case-affix precedes it in composition. As प्र + अञ्चु + किन् = प्राञ्च् nom. sing. प्राह् (VI. 4. 24; VII. I. 70, VIII. 2. 23 and 62) 'east'; so also प्रस्थक् 'west'; उदक् 'north'.

434

THE AFFIX KAN.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 60.

The affix किन् comes after युजि and कुडु when these are uncombined. Thus युज्+किन्=युज्. In nominative singular, युज्+सु=युज्+सु (VII. 1. 71) = युज्+सु (VI. 1. 68) = युज् (VIII. 2. 62) 'who joins'. When the root युज् is in composition with an *upapada*, it takes the affix किन् (see sutra 61). As अभयुक् 'yoked with horses'.

So also कुडु+किन्=कुडु, nom. sing. कुडु, 'a curlew'. The non-elision of the म (VI. 4. 24) of कुडु is an irregularity, as this word has been taught in connection with other irregular words.

त्यदादिषु दृगोऽनालोचने कञ्चु ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ त्यद-आदिषु, दृगः, अनालोचने, कञ्चु, च, (किन्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्यदादिषुपवेषु दृगोऽनालोचनेऽपे वसीमानात् कञ्चुस्ययो भवति चकारात् किन्तु ॥

60. And the affix कम् comes after the verb दृगः 'to see' when it is in combination with स्वद &c. and does not signify perception.

The force of 'and' is that the किन् also comes under similar circumstances. स्वद &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see I. 1. 27. Thus स्वादृगः nom. sing. स्वादृक्, 'such-like' when it is formed by किन्; and स्वादृगः 'such-like' when the affix is कम्. So also तद्+दृश्+किन्=तादृश् (VI. 3. 91) nom. sing. तादृक् (VI. 1. 68, VIII. 2. 36 and 62, VIII. 4. 56); and तादृगः when कम् is the affix. So यादृक् or यादृगः 'what-like'.

What is the force of the letter म् of कम्? It is for the sake of accent; the *udatta* is on the first syllable of those words which are formed by an affix having an indicatory म् or न् (VI. 1. 117). But the indicatory न् would have given the same accent, there being no difference between कम् and कन् in this respect. The indicatory म् then serves only the purpose of distinguishing the affix कम् from कन् in sutra IV. 1. 15 in which कम् is taken and not कन्. Had we not formed this separate affix, then for कञ्चुकम् of that sutra, we should have read कन् कम् so that the feminine of words formed by कन् would have also taken long हैं, so that the feminine of यावकः (याव+कन् V. 4. 29) would have been यावकी instead of यावका.

Why do we say 'when not signifying perception'? See सं पश्यति = तदृशः 'who sees that'. The words स्वादृक्, तादृश् &c. are crude nouns, in which the etymological sense of the root not being visible, the act of seeing can never be denoted by these words.

*Vart.*—This rule applies also when the words समान and अन्य are in composition with दृश्. 'As सदृक् or सदृगः 'like' (समान+दृश्+किन्=स+दृश् VI. 3. 89); so also अन्यादृशः or अन्यादृक् 'of another kind'.

BK. III CH II. § 61] THE AFFIX KVIP.

435

Vart.—The affix क्स comes also after the root इश्. As तादृशः, यादृशः, अन्यादृशः and कीदृशः। तद्+दृश्+क्स=ता+दृश्+क्स (VI. 3. 91.)=तादृश्+स (VIII. 2. 36) = तादृक्+स (VIII. 2. 41) = तादृक्+ष (VIII. 3. 59) = तादृशः।

सत् सूद्धिपदृहदुहयुजविदभिदच्छिदजिनीराजासुपसर्गेऽपि किप् ॥
६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ सत्-सू-द्विष-दृह-दुह-युज-विद-भिद-छिद-जि-नी-राजान्,
उपसर्गे, अपि, किप्, ( सुषि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सदादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः सुबन्ते उपपन्ने उपसर्गेऽन्युपसर्गेऽपि किप्परथयो भवति ॥

61. The affix किप् comes after the following verbs when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix, though it may be an upasarga, viz:—सत् 'to sit', सू 'to bring forth', द्विष 'to hate', दुइ 'to bear malice', दुइ 'to milk', युज 'to join', 'to concentrate the mind', बिद 'to know', 'to become', 'to consider', भिद 'to divide', छिद 'to cut', जि 'to conquer', नो 'to lead' and राज 'to shine'.

The phrase 'the word ending with a case-affix' is understood in this sūtra. The *anuvritti* of कर्म is not to be taken in this sūtra for the same reasons as in sūtra 58 *ante*. The upasargas are also words ending in a case-affix *i. e.* they are also *subanta* words. Their special mention in this section, indicates by implication (*jñāpaka*) that wherever in the previous sūtras, the word *subanta* (a case-inflected word) is used, it does not include an upasarga (III 1. 106).

The root सू being read in conjunction with द्विष shows that अद्विष class verb is meant here, and not तद्विष class. The verb युज includes, both युजिर 'to join' and युज 'to concentrate one's mind'. The verb बिद includes the three verbs having the sense of 'to know', 'to become' and 'to consider', but does not include the verb बिद 'to gain', because that root has an indicatory लू (बिद्लू) while all these verbs have indicatory अ.

Thus, सत्—शुद्धिपत् 'dwelling in purity'; अन्तरिक्षसत् 'dwelling in the skies', 'epithets of Brahma' (Kath. 5. 2); उपसत् 'serving'. सू—अण्डसू: 'oviparous'; शतसू: 'bringing forth hundred'; प्रसू: 'parent'. द्विष—निम्बद्विद् 'treacherous'; प्रद्विद् 'hostile'. दुइ—निम्बभूक्त 'treacherous'; प्रभूक्त 'hostile' (VIII. 2. 37). दुइ—गोभूक्त 'cow-milker'; प्रभूक्त 'milker' (VIII. 2. 32. and 37). युज—अन्धयुक् 'carriage'; प्रथुक् 'impulse'. बिद—वेदवित् 'knower of Veda'; प्रथित् 'knower'; ब्रह्मवित् 'knower of Brahma'. भिद—कादमित् 'wood-cutter'; प्रथित् 'cutter'. छिद—रज्जुच्छिद् 'rope-cutter'; प्रच्छिद् 'a cutter'. जि—शजुजित् 'enemy-conqueror'; प्रजित् 'conqueror'. नी—सेनानी: 'leader of an army'; प्रणी: 'a leader'; प्राणी: 'head-borough'; अषणी: 'first'. (Why is there cerebral ण in these words? Because the word प्राणी has a cerebral ण in

23.

436

THE AFFIX NYUT. [BK. III. CH. II. § 62-65.

sūtra V. 2, 78 and that indicates that these words will have ण, as also by sūtra VIII. 4. 3). णन्—विराद् 'splendour'; समाद् 'emperor' (the letter म is added by sūtra VIII. 3. 25).

This sūtra is a continuation and expansion of sūtras 75 and 76 sup.

भजो शिवः ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ भजः, शिवः, (उपसर्ग, अपि, सुपि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भजोर्भूतोः सुबन्त उपपदे उपसर्गोऽप्यनुपसर्गोऽपि ण्विमस्ययो भवति ॥

62. The affix ण्वि comes after the verb भज् 'to share' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix whether it be an upasarga or not.

The words 'upasarga' and 'supi' are understood in this sūtra. As अर्द्ध भजते = अर्द्धभाज् nom. sing. अर्द्धभाक् 'sharing a half'. So also when in composition with a preposition; as भजाक् 'division'.

छन्दसि सहः ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, सहः, (उपसर्ग, सुपि, शिवः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये सहेर्भूतोः सुबन्त उपपदे ण्विमस्ययो भवति ॥

63. In the Chhandas, the affix ण्वि comes after the verb सह 'to bear' when it is in composition with a word ending in a case-affix.

The words 'upasarga' and 'supi' are understood here. As सुर+सह+ण्वि =सुरासाह nom. sing. सुरासाह 'name of Indra'. The dental स is changed into cerebral ष by VIII. 3. 56, and the ह into ट by VIII. 2. 31. The final अ of सुर is lengthened by VI. 3. 137. See Rig Veda. I. 175. 2, III. 48 5.

वहश्च ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ वहः, च, (छन्दसि, शिवः, सुपि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वहेर्भूतोः छन्दसि विषये सुबन्त उपपदे ण्विमस्ययो भवति ॥

64. The affix ण्वि comes after the verb वह 'to carry', in the Chhandas, when a word ending with a case-affix is in composition with it.

As प्रह्लाद् 1st sing. प्रह्लाद् 'carrying a *prashtha* measure'; so, वित्यवाद् ।

The division of this sūtra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sūtras, into which the anuvritti of वह only is carried and not of सह. See Yajur, Veda. XIV. 10, XVIII. 26.

कव्यपुरीषपुरीष्येषु ण्युट् ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कव्य-पुरीष-पुरीष्येषु, ण्युट्, (छन्दसि, सुपि, वहः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कव्य पुरीष पुरीष्य इत्येतेषु उपपदेषु छन्दसि विषये वहेर्भूतोऽर्थुदमस्ययो भवति ॥

65. In the Chhandas the affix ण्युट् comes after

BK III. CH. II. § 66, 67.]

THE AFFIX VIT.

437

the verb वह when it is in composition with the words कव्य 'oblation of food to deceased ancestors', पुरीष 'fæces' and पुरीष्य 'water'.

As कव्यवाहनः पितृपानम् (Yajur. Ved. II. 29) 'fire that carries the oblation to the pitris'; पुरीषवाहनः 'carrier of water'; पुरीष्यवाहनः (Yaj. Ved. XI. 44). The feminine of these words is formed by adding long हैं।

हव्येनन्तःपादम् ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ हव्ये, अनन्तःपादम्, (छन्दसि, वहः, ज्युत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हव्यशब्दे उपपदे छन्दसि विषये बहैर्धातोऽर्थुद्रत्ययो भवति, अनन्तःपादं चेदहि-र्वर्तते ॥

66. The affix ज्युत् comes in the Chhandas, after the verb वह 'to carry' when it is in composition with the word हव्य 'an oblation to gods', provided that the word so formed does not occur in the middle of a pāda (fourth part of a stanza).

As अग्निश्च हव्यवाहनः 'fire, the carrier of oblation to the gods'. (Rig. Ved. I. 44. 2).

When this word occurs in the middle of a pāda, or at the beginning, the form is हव्यवाह, which is derived by adding the affix णिव (sūtra 64). As हव्यवाहनः पिता नः 'the never-decaying agni or fire that carries oblation to the gods, is our father'. (Rig. Veda. III. 2. 2.)

जनसनखनक्रमगमो विद् ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ जन-सन-खन-क्रम-गमः, विद्, (छन्दसि, उपसर्गे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जनादिभ्यो धातुभ्यः सुबन्त उपपदे छन्दसि विषये विद्रत्ययो भवति ॥

67. The affix विद् (the whole of which is elided) comes in the Chhandas after the verbs जन 'to be born', सन् 'to bestow', खन् 'to dig', कन् 'to pace' and गम् 'to go', when a word ending in a case-affix is in composition, and the final nasals are changed into long आ.

The words छन्दसि, उपसर्गे and सुपि are understood in this sūtra. The verb जन् includes two verbs meaning 'to be born' and 'to happen'; so also सन् means both 'to give' and 'to worship'.

Of the affix विद् the letter द् is indicatory, and is qualifying, as in VI. 4. 41, by which rule the final nasal of जन्, सन् &c. is replaced by long आ when the affix विद् follows, and the whole affix is elided by VI. 1. 67.

438

THE AFFIX KAP. [BK. III. CH. II. § 68, 70.

As अप्+जन+विद्=अज्ञा: (Rig. Ved. VII. 34. 16) 'born in water' (VI. 4. 41); गोजा: 'born in the heaven i.e. God' (Rig. Veda IV. 40. 5). So also from सन्—गोया: 'acquiring or bestowing cows' (VIII. 3. 108); गोया इंद्रो नृपा असि 'O Indra bestower of cows! thou art lover of mankind' (Rig. Veda IX. 2. 10). From खन्—विसखा: 'digger of lotus stalk'; कृपखा: 'digger of well'. From क्रम्—इपिका: 'who gets milk' (Rig. IV. 39. 1 and 40. 5). From गम्—अर्पणा उन्नेदृणाम् 'the leader'.

अदोऽनने ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अद्:, अनने, (सुपि, विद्) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ अरोधोतोऽनने सुप्युपपरे विद्मस्ययो भवति ॥

68. The affix विद् comes after the verb अत् 'to eat,' when in composition with a case-inflected word other than अन्न 'food'.

The *anuvritti* of the word 'Chhandasi' does not extend to this sutra.

Thus आममत्ति = आमात् 'eating raw food'; शब्धात् 'granivorous'.

But with अन्न as an upapada, we have अज्ञा: 'eating food', which is formed by the general affix अण् (III 2. 1.)

क्रव्ये च ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रव्ये, च, (अद्:, विद्) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ क्रव्यशब्द उपपरे अरोधोतोऽनस्ययो भवति ॥

69. The affix विद् comes after the verb अत् 'to eat,' when the word क्रव्य is in composition with it.

As क्रव्यमत्ति = क्रव्यात् 'carnivorous'.

Why has it been made a separate sutra, when this form could have been obtained by the last sutra also? To this the vartika replies: 'This has been made a separate sutra in order to indicate that the rule of वासकूप (III. 1. 94) does not apply here. Therefore the affix अण् will not apply in the alternative. If the affix अण् does not apply, how then we get the form क्रव्याः which is evidently formed by the affix अण्? The affix अण् comes after the root when the word formed means the eater of meat which has been cut, dressed and cooked'; thus क्रव्याः means a man who eats meat cooked and prepared, i.e. a meat-eater as opposed to a vegetarian, while क्रव्याः means an animal which eats raw flesh; the word क्रव्याः in fact may be regarded as an irregular form falling under प्रचोदयादि class of sutra VI. 3. 109.

दुह्: कषधश्च ॥ ७० ॥ दुह्:, कप्-घ:, च, (सुपि) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ दुहेधोतोऽ सुप्युपपरे कप्पस्ययो भवति घकारधान्तावेशः ॥

70. The affix कप् comes after the verb दुह् 'to milk' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix and the letter च replaces its final.

BK. III. CH. II. §. 71, 72] THE AFFIX NVIN.

439

As कामदुधा घेनुः 'a milch cow, giving abundance of milk'; so also अर्धदुधा, घर्मदुधा।

मंत्रे श्वेतवहीकृपशस्पुरोडाशो पिवन् ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ मंत्रे, श्वेतवह-उकृपशस्-पुरोडाशः, पिवन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ श्वेतवह उकृपशस् पुरोडाश् हस्येतेभ्यो पिवन् प्रस्थयो भवति मन्त्रे विपथे ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ श्वेतवहादीनां उरस्वस्थेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

71. In the Mantra literature, the affix पिवन् comes after the words श्वेतवह, उकृपशस् and पुरोडाश्।

The above words contain both the verb and the upapada; the fact of their being so given indicates that there is some irregularity in the application of the affix.

Thus the affix पिवन् comes after the verb वह, preceded by the upapada श्वेत as denoting an agent, while the force of the whole word so formed denotes an object. As श्वेता एनं वहन्ति = श्वेतवाह, nom. sing. श्वेतवा: 'a name of Indra' (whom white horses carry).

The affix पिवन् is applied to the verb शंस् 'to praise' when preceded by the word उकृप as object or instrument; and then the nasal is irregularly dropped. As उकृपानि उकृपैर्वा शंसति = उकृपशास्, nom. sing. उकृपशाः (Rig. Ved. II. 39. 1.) 'a reciter of hymns, the name of the sacrificer'.

The पिवन् is applied after the verb वाश् 'to give', preceded by पुरो, and व is changed into उ, the force of the whole word denoting an object. As पुरो वाशन्ति एनं = पुरोडाश्, nom. sing. पुरोडाः (Rig. Ved. III. 28. 2) 'an offering'.

Vart:—The augment उस् is added to the words श्वेतवाह &c., when the pada affixes follow. Thus before pada terminations श्वेतवाह becomes श्वेतवह। Therefore its Instrumental dual is श्वेतवोध्यान्, pl. श्वेतवोभिः।

The augment उस् is not applied before सर्वनामस्थान and भ terminations. As श्वेतवाहो, श्वेतवाहः।

अवे यजः ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अवे, यजः, (पिवन्, मन्त्रे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवे उपपथे यजेधीतोर्विनुप्रस्थयो भवति मन्त्रे विपथे ॥

72. In the Mantra literature, the affix पिवन् comes after the verb यज् 'to sacrifice' when in composition with the word अव्.

As अवयाज्, nom. sing. अवयाः (Rig. Ved. I. 173. 12) 'name of a Vedic priest'; as स्वं यज्ञे वरुणस्थावया अस्ति 'Thou art the priest of Varuna in the sacrifice'.

The division of this aphorism from the last in which it could have been included, is for the sake of the subsequent sutras in which the *anuvritti* of यज

24

440

THE AFFIX VICH.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 73, 74.

only runs. This word is thus declined :—

[tbl-2.md](tbl-2.md)

विजुपे छन्दसि ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ विच्, उपे, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपउपपदे यजेऽछन्दसि विषये विच्प्रत्ययी भवति ॥

73. The affix विच् comes after the verb यज् when उप precedes, in the Chhandas.

As उपयज्भिक्प्रभे वहन्ति 'they carry it up with the उपयज् formulas'. उपयज् is the name of eleven formulas at a sacrifice.

The word 'Chhandas' has been repeated here though the anuvritti of the word 'mantra' was present in it, in order to include the Brāhmaṇa literature also.

The च् is indicatory and is useful in including the affix विच् in the larger group called वि (which includes किन्, किप्, ण्वि, विद्), as in the sūtra वेदपृक्तस्य (VI. 1. 67).

Why has this sūtra been made, since the affix विच् would have been valid even by aphorism 75? The sūtra has been separately made to show that it is a restrictive rule here. The form उपयज् is found in the Chhandas only, and not in the ordinary literature.

आतो मनिन्क्रनिष्वनिपश्च ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, मनिन्-
क्रनिप्-वनिपः, च, (छन्दसि, सुपि, विच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तेभ्यो धातुभ्यः सुप्युपपदे छन्दसि विषये मनिन् क्रनिप् वनिप् हरयेतं प्रत्यया भवन्ति चकाराद्विजपि ॥

74. The affixes मनिन्(मन्), क्रनिप्(वन्), वनिप्(वन्) and विच् come in the Chhandas, after verbs which end in long आ, when a case-inflected word or an upasarga is in composition.

The force of 'and' is to include विच्. Thus सुधा + मनिन् = सुधामन्, 1st. sing. सुधामा (Rig. VI. 20. 7) 'one who gives liberally'; अश्व + स्था + मनिन् = अश्वस्थामन्, 1st. sing. अश्वस्थामा 'the name of Asvatthaman'; सुधा + क्रनिप् = सुधी + वन् (VI. 4. 66) = सुधीवन्, 1st. sing. सुधी वा 'having good understanding'; सुपा + क्रनिप् = सुधीवन्, 1st. sing. सुधी वा 'a good drinker'. भूरि + वा + वनिप् = भूरिदावन्, 1st. sing. भूरिदावा (Rig. II. 27. 17) 'liberal'; घृतपावन् 1st. sing. घृतपावा (Yaj. VI. 19) 'ghee-drinker'.

The affix विच् is also included in this aphorism. As कीलाज + पा + विच् = कीलाज पा: (Rig. X. 91. 14) 'rectar-drinker'; सुध्या: (Rig. IV. 3. 6. and Pāṇini VII.

BK. III. CH. II. § 75-77.]

THE AFFIX KVIP.

441

3. 46) 'beautifully going'; रामस्योपदः 'an offering of Rāma.' (see sūtra III. 3. 106 and Yajur. Ved. XXX. 9).

अन्येभ्योपि दृश्यते ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्येभ्यः, अपि, दृश्यते, (मनिन्, क्रनिप्, वनिप्, विच्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्येभ्योपि धातुभ्योऽनाकारान्तेभ्यो मनिन्, वनिप्, वनिप् इत्येति प्रत्ययाः दृश्यन्ते, विच् ॥

75. These affixes viz. मनिन्, क्वनिप्, वनिप्, and विच् are seen after other verbs also besides those ending in long आ.

The word छन्दसि is not understood here. As सु+भू 'to injure' + मनिन् = सुगर्मन्, 1st. 'sing. सुगर्म' 'who destroys well i.e. destroys sin or ignorance'. मातर+इ 'to go' + क्वनिप् = मातर+इत्+वम् (VI. 1. 71) = मातरिस्वम्, 1st. sing. मातरिस्वा 'who goes early'. वि+जन्+वनिप्=वि+जा+वम् (VI. 4. 41) = विज्ञावम्, 1st. sing. विज्ञावा 'who brings forth'. अर्धगावा 'who goes before'. रिष्+विच्=रेष् (VII. 3. 86) 1st. sing. रेद् 'who injures'; as in रेदसि पर्णं नयेः (Yajur. Ved. VI. 18).

The word 'also' in this aphorism has the force of removing all conditions under which these affixes were employed in the previous aphorisms, that is to say, these affixes come even when there is no upapada. As पीवा, धीवा.
