The term सन् in the aphorism means Desideratives in the affix सन्, and not the verb, सन् because the verb सन् is never seen with this affix.

As, चिकीर्षुः 'desirous of doing'; जिहीर्षुः 'desirous of taking'; आशंसुः 'desirous'; भिक्षुः 'a beggar'.

The verb आशंस with the upasarga आ is the verb शसि 'to desire' and not the verb शसि 'to praise'.

विन्दुरिच्छुः ॥ १६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ विन्दुः, इच्छुः, (तच्छी०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विवेर्मुगागम इषेऽच्छ्वमुकारश्च प्रत्ययो निवारयते तच्छीलादिषु कर्तेषु ॥

169. The words विन्दु and इच्छु are irregularly formed by the addition of the affix उ, in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c'.

To the verb विधि we add the augment नुम् and then the affix उ; as, विध + नुम् + उ = विन्दुः (I. I. 47) = वेदनशीलः 'intelligent'; so of इष 'to wish', the प is replaced by छ, and we have इच्छुः = एषणशीलः 'desirous'.

क्याच्छन्दसि ॥ १७० ॥ पदानि ॥ क्यात, छन्दसि, (तच्छील०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कयप्रत्ययान्ताजातोऽच्छन्दसि विपये तच्छीलादिषु कर्तेषु उकारप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

170. The affix उ comes in the Chhandas, after the roots that have taken the Denominative affix क्य in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c'.

The term क्य includes the three affixes क्यच्, क्यङ् and क्यप् (see sūtras III. I. 8, II, 13, &c). As भिन्नयुः, संस्वेदयुः, सुधयुः (Rig. Ved. I. 3. 4).

33

476

THE AFFIXES KI AND KIN.

[BK III. CH. II. § 171.

In the modern Sanskrit वृन् will be employed. As भिन्नीयिता. By sūtra VII. 4. 33, the long ई replaces the final अ, when क्वच् follows; as पुन+क्वच्=पुनी+य=पुनीय. Why then in the case of भिन्नयु: there is not the substitution of long ई for the अ of भिन्न? Because the rule VII. 4. 33 is set aside by VII. 4. 35 which declares that in the Chhandas the long ई is not substituted for the अ।

आङ्गमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च ॥ १७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ आङ्ग-क्र-गम-हन-जनः, कि-किनौ, लिट्, च, (तच्छीलादिषु) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तेभ्य क्वच्यान्तेभ्यश्च गम हन जन इत्येतेभ्यश्चन्दसि विपये तच्छीलादिषु कर्तृप् किकिनौ प्रस्थयो भवतः, लिट्बच्यच् तो भवतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ किकिनावृत्तसर्गश्चन्दसि सदाविध्यो दर्पनात् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ भाषायां धामुकुश्चजनिगमिनमिभ्यः किकिनौ वक्तव्यो ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सहिवहिचलिपतिभ्यो यङन्तेभ्यः किकिनौ वक्तव्यो ॥

171. In the Chhandas, the affixes कि and किन् in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c' come after the verbs that end in long आ, or short or long ऋ, and after the verbs गम् 'to go', हन् 'to kill', and जन 'to be produced', and these affixes operate like लिट् causing reduplication of the root.

The वृ after आ is either for the sake of euphony, or for the sake of precision. Had it been त्, then by the rule of तपर (I. 1. 70) short ऋ would only be included and not long ऋ. But the present rule is applicable to long ऋ as well.

Thus पा+कि=पपिः 'drinking'; as पपिः सोमं 'drinking the soma-juice'; वदिगोः 'giving cows' (Rig. Ved. VI. 23. 4). मित्रावरुणौ ततुरिः (Rig. Ved. IV. 39. 2, VI. 68. 7). इरे अध्याजगुरिः (Rig. Ved. X. 108. 1). गम्+किन्=जग्निः 'being in constant motion, wind'; जग्मियुवा (Rig. Ved. II. 23. 11); हन्+किन्=जघ्निः 'killing, a weapon offensive'; जघ्निवृन्नम् (Rig. Ved. IX. 61. 2); जन+किन्=जज्निः as जज्निबीजम् (T. S. VII. 5. 20. 1).

The letter ऋ in these affixes is indicatory. It might be said 'it is superfluous to make these affixes कित्त्, because these being treated like लिट् will be कित्त् by rule I. 2. 5'. True, they would be कित्त् by the rule I. 2. 5, but then the rule VII. 4. 11. (when lit follows, guna is the substitute of the verb ऋच् and of those that end in the long ऋ) would also have applied to these affixes, and would have caused guna. It is to prevent this guna of the letter ऋ that we have annexed an indicatory क् to these affixes.

Vart:—The affixes कि and किन् are of universal application in the Chhandas, and not confined to the verbs enumerated in the sūtra, as we see them in सव् &c.; as सेविः (Yaj. Ved. XII. 105); नेमिः (Rig. Ved. II. 5. 3).

Vart:—The affixes कि and किन् come after the roots धामु, कुम्, छ, जनि,

BK. III. CH. II. § 172-175.] THE AFFIX VARACH.

477

गनि, and ननि in the secular literature also; as, इधिः, चकिः, ससिः, जजिः, जगिः, नेः ।

Vart:—The affixes कि and किन, come after the Intensive (बङ्ग) roots of सह, बह, चल, and यत. As, सासहिः, बावहिः, चाचलिः, यायतिः (VII. 4. 83).

स्वपितृपीनैजिङ् ॥ १७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्वपि-तृपाः, नजिङ्, (तच्छीलादिषु) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्वपेस्त्वेष्व तच्छीलादिषु कर्तेषु नजिङ्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ धृषेऽपि वक्तव्यम् ॥

172. The affix नजिङ् comes, in the sense of 'the agents having such a habit &c', after the verbs स्वप् 'to sleep' and तृष 'to be thirsty'.

As स्वप्+नजिङ्=स्वप्न 1st. sing. स्वप्नक् 'sleeping, drowsy'; तृष्वप्न 1st. sing. तृष्वप्नक् 'covetous, thirsty'.

Vart:—So also after the verb धृष 'to insult, be bold'; as, धृष्वप्न 1st. sing. धृष्वप्नक् 'bold, impudent'.

शुवन्दोरारः ॥ १७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ शू-वन्दोः, आरः, (तच्छी०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शू हिंसायाम् वन्दि अभिवादनस्तुत्योः एताभ्यां तच्छीलादिषु कर्तृप्यारःप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

173. The affix आर comes in the sense of 'the agents having such a habit &c' after the verbs शू 'to injure' and वन्द 'to praise', 'to salute'.

As शारः 'noxious, a mischievous animal'; वन्दारः 'praising, a bard'.

भियः कुक्कुनौ ॥ १७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ भियः, कु-क्कुनौ, (तच्छी०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भिभी भये अस्माजातोस्तच्छीलादिषु कर्तेषु कुक्कुनौ प्रत्ययो भवतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कु क्त्रपि वक्तव्यः ॥

174. The affixes कु and कुकन come in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit' after the verb भी 'to fear'.

As, भीरः 'fearful, timid'; भीरुकः 'timorous, a bear, a tiger, a jackal'.

Vart:—The affix कुकन, should also be stated; as भीरुकः ।

श्वेशभासपिसकसो वरच् ॥ १७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्था-ईश-भास-

पिस-कसः, वरच्, (तच्छीलादिषु) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्था ईश भास पिस कस एतेभ्यस्तच्छीलादिषु कर्तेषु वरच्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

175. The affix वरच् comes, in the sense of 'the agents having such a habit &c' after the verbs स्था 'to stand' ईश 'to rule', भास 'to shine', पिस 'to go' and कस 'to go'.

As स्थावरः 'immoveable'; ईश्वरः 'ruler, God'; पेस्वरः 'going, destructive'; विकस्वरः 'opening, expanding'.

यज्ञ यजः ॥ १७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ यः, च, यजः, (तच्छीलादिषु, वरच्) ॥

478

THE AFFIX KVIP.

[BK. III CH. II. § 176-178.

वृत्तिः ॥ या पापणे अस्ताच्छन्ताच्छ्लोजाविषु कर्तेषु वरच्यपस्ययो भवति ॥

176. The affix वरच् in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c' comes after the verb या when it ends with the affix यद्.

With the affix यद्, the intensives of verbs are formed; as यायावरः 'a vagrant, an ascetic'. See sutra I. 1. 58.

आजभासधुर्विद्युतोर्जिपूजुग्रावस्तुवः क्रिप् ॥ १७७ ॥ पदानि ॥

आज-भास-धुर्वि-द्युत-उर्जि-पू-जु-ग्रावस्तुवः, क्रिप्, (तच्छीलादिषु) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आजाविष्यो धातुभ्यस्तच्छीजाविषु कर्तेषु क्रिप्पस्ययो भवति ॥

177. The affix क्रिप् comes, in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c.' after the verbs आज 'to shine' भास 'to shine', धुर्व 'to injure', द्युत 'to shine', ऊर्ज 'to be strong', पू 'to fill', जु 'to move rapidly' and स्तु 'to praise', when it is preceded by the word पावन् 'a stone'.

Thus, विधाज् 1st. sing. विधाद् 'splendid'; भास् 1st. sing. भाः 'light'; धुर्व् + क्रिप् = धुर् (VI. 4. 21), 1st sing. धूः 'who injures'; विद्युत् 'lightening'; ऊर्ज 1st. sing. ऊर्ज 'strength'; पूर 1st. sing. पूः 'what fills'; जूः 'swift'. In the case of जु, a long vowel is the substitute of जु; यावस्तुत् (VI. 1. 71) 'a stone-worshipper'. Though by the universal rule III. 2. 76, the affix क्रिप् would have come after these verbs also, the repetition of the affix shows that बाऽसङ्घविधि does not apply in *táchchhilika* affixes.

अन्येभ्योपि दृश्यते ॥ १७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्येभ्यः, अपि, दृश्यते, (तच्छीलादिषु, क्रिप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्येभ्योपि धातुभ्यस्तच्छीजाविषु क्रिप्पस्ययो दृश्यते ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ किंवृवचिपच्छयायतस्तु कदपजुश्रीणां दीयोऽसम्पसारणंच ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ धृतिमनिजुहोतीनां द्वे च ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ जुहोतैर्दीर्घश्च ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ दृभय दृश्यस्य हस्वश्च द्वे च ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ ध्यायतेः सम्पसारणं च ॥

178. The affix क्रिप् is seen after other verbs also, besides those mentioned above, in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c'.

As युज्, 1st. sing. युक् 'joining'; छिन् 'piercing'; निन् 'dividing'.

By using the words 'is seen' in the aphorism, it is implied that other rules also apply concurrently with क्रिप्. Thus in some cases we find lengthening of the vowel; in some, there is reduplication of the root; in some instances there is *samprasāran* of the semivowel; and in other cases there is not.

BK. III. CH. II. § 179, 180.] THE AFFIX DU.

479

Vart:—When किप् follows, the long vowel is the substitute of बन्ध 'to speak', प्रच्छ 'to ask', आयतस्तु 'to praise long', कटप 'to move through a mat', जु 'to move rapidly', and श्री 'to serve', and there is no substitution of a vowel for the semivowel (VI. I. 16).

As, वाक् 'the voice'; प्रच्छ + किप् = प्रप् + किप् (VI. I. 10) = प्रप् + किप् (VIII. 2. 36) = प्राद् (VIII. 4. 56) 'who asks'; आयतस्तु 'who praises long'; कटप 'a worm'; जु 'swift'; श्री 'the goddess Lakshmi'.

The word जु which was mentioned in the last sūtra is redundant here.

Vart:—There is reduplication of the verbs युत् 'to shine', गम् 'to go' and दु 'to invoke', when किप् follows. As, विद्युत् 'shining'; जगत् 'going, the world'.

Vart:—There is lengthening also of the vowel of जुहु: as जुहु: 'a crescent-shaped wooden ladle used for pouring the sacrificial ghee into the fire.'

Vart:—The root दु 'to tear' is shortened also; as इहुत 'tearing'.

Vart:—The verb ध्या 'to think' has samprasāraṇa; as धी: 'thinking'.

भुवः संज्ञान्तरयोः ॥१७॥ पदानि ॥ भुवः, संज्ञा-अन्तरयोः, (किप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भवतेधीतोः संज्ञायामन्तरे च गम्यमाने किप्प्रस्थयो भवति ॥

179. The affix किप् comes after the verb भू 'to be' when the word so formed denotes a name or a surety.

As, विभूः 'a person called Vibhū'; प्रतिभूः 'a surety i. e. he who stands intermediate between the debtor and the creditor'.

विप्रसंभ्यो इवसंज्ञायाम् ॥ १८० ॥ पदानि ॥ वि-प्र-संभ्यो, दु, असंज्ञायाम्, (भुवः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वि प्र सम् इत्येवं पूर्वाञ्चवतेधीतोः दुप्रस्थयो भवति न चेत् संज्ञा गम्यते ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ दुप्रकरणं मितद्वादिभ्य उपसंख्यानम् ॥

180. The affix दु comes after the verb भू when it is preceded by the upasargas वि, प्र and सम् provided that the word to be formed does not mean an appellative.

As विभूः 'all pervading'; प्रभूः 'lord'; संभूः 'Creator'.

Why do we say 'when it is not a proper name? Observe विभूः 'a person called Vibhū'.

Vart:—The words मितद्व &c, also are formed by this affix. As मितद्व 'the sea'; संभूः 'causing happiness'.

Why have we applied दु and not किप् to this root, as the forms would have been the same in either case? We have done so for two purposes: (1) To prevent the rules relating to dhātus from applying to this. (2) To prevent the insertion of तुक् augment. Thus the 1st. dual of मितद्व is मितद्व, 1st. pl. is मितद्वः। Here there is no substitution of उकड् which the rule VI. 4. 77 required, if दु had retained its dhātu characteristic; so also the rule of accent in VI. I. 175

34

480

THE AFFIX SHTRAN.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 181-183.]

does not apply to Instrumental sing. मितद्व (2.) We have no त which rule VI. 1. 71 required. मितं ब्रवति=मितद्वः।

घः कर्मणि, छ्दन् ॥ १८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ घः, कर्मणि, छ्दन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ घयतैर्ध्यातोऽथ कर्मणि कारके द्रुमपत्ययो भवति ॥

181. The affix ऋन् comes, in denoting the object, after the verb घ 'to feed'.

The indicatory घ denotes that the feminine is formed by क्रीश (है) affix. As घानी 'a nurse whom the children suck (*dhayanti*); and 'Amalaki fruit which holds (*dadhāti*) all medicinal properties'.

दात्रीशसयुयुजस्तुतुदसिसिचनिहपतदशनहः करणे ॥ १८२ ॥ पदा-
नि॥ दाप्-नी-शस-यु-युज-स्तु-तुद्-सि-सिच्-मिह-पत्-दश्-नहः, करणे,(छ्दन्)॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दाप् नी शस यु युज स्तु तुव् सि सिच् मिह पत दश् नह एतेभ्यो धातुभ्यः करणो
कारके द्रुमपत्ययो भवति ॥

182. The affix ऋन्, with the sense of instrument, comes after the verbs दाप 'to cut', नी 'to lead', शस 'to hurt', यु 'to join', युज 'to join', स्तु 'to praise', तुव 'to inflict pain', सि 'to bind', सिच् 'to sprinkle', मिह 'to urine', पत् 'to fall', दश 'to bite' and नह 'to bind'.

As दाज, 1st. sing. neuter दाजम् 'a sickle' (lit. that with which one cuts);
नेत्र 1st. sing. नेत्रम् 'eye'; शस्त्रं (VII. 2. 9) 'a weapon'; योत्रं 'the tie that fastens the
yoke'; योक्तम् 'the tie of yoke'; स्तोत्रं 'a penegyric'; तोत्रं 'a goad', सेत्रं 'a ligament';
सेक्तं 'a sprinkling vessel'; मेइट्टम् 'the penis'; पत्तम् 'a vehicle'; शङ्खा 'a large tooth'.

The word शङ्खा belongs to the *Ajādi* class and hence forms its feminine in दाप्(आ) and not in है (IV. 1. 4).

The root शङ्खा is read in the aphorism without its nasal *i. e.* as दश्. This indicates by implication that दश् loses its nasal before some affixes such as लघुद्; thus we have दशम् 'tooth'.

And lastly नह+ऋन्=नद्भ fem. नद्भी (VIII. 2. 34 and 40), 'a thong'.

हलसूकरयोः, पुवः ॥ १८३ ॥ पदानि ॥ हल-सूकरयोः, पुवः,(छ्दन्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूष् पूष् पवने, अस्माद्वातोः करणो कारके द्रुमपत्ययो भवति तच्चेत् करणो हलसू-
करयोरयययो भवति ॥

183. The affix ऋन् is employed after the verb पू with the sense of instrument when denoting a member of the body of a plough or of a hog.

The verb पू includes both पूष् and पूष्; as पोत्रम् 'a plough-share'; पोत्रम् 'the snout of a hog'.

BK. III. CH. II. § 184-187.]

THE AFFIX KTA.

481

अतिर्लूघुसूखनसहचर इत्रः ॥ १८४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अति-लू-घू-सू-
खन-सह-चरः, इत्रः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अति लू घू सू खन सह चर एतेभ्यो धातुभ्यः करणो कारके इत्रमत्ययो भवति ॥

184. The affix इत्र comes after the verbs क् 'to go', लू 'to cut', घू 'to shake', सू 'to bring forth', खन् 'to dig', सह 'to bear', and चर 'to go' with the sense of instrument.

Thus, अरिजं 'a rudder'; अविजं 'a sickle'; पविजं 'a fan'; सविजं 'cause of production'; खनिजं 'a spade'; सहिजं 'patience'; चरिजं 'an instituted observance or a narrative'.

पुवः संज्ञायान् ॥ १८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुवः, संज्ञायान्, (इत्रः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पवनैर्धातोः करणो कारके इत्रमत्ययो भवति समुदायेन चेतसङ्गा गम्यते ॥

185. The affix इत्र comes after the verb पू 'to purify' with the sense of the agent so expressed being the instrument; when the sense of the complete word is simply appellative, and not descriptive.

The verb पू includes two verbs पूज् and पूज् both meaning 'to purify', but belonging to two different conjugations; as पविजं an instrument for cleansing or purifying, such as a sieve or a strainer; and in this sense it means 'two blades of *Kusa* grass used at sacrifices in purifying and sprinkling ghee'. It also means 'the sacred thread, the clarified butter, &c.

कर्तेरि चर्षिदेवतयोः ॥ १८६ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तेरि, च, ऋषि-देवतयोः, (इत्रः, पुवः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुवः करणो कर्तेरि च इत्रमत्ययो भवति, ऋषिदेवतयोः प्रथासंख्यं संबन्धः ॥

186. The affix इत्र comes after the verb पू 'to purify' in the sense of 'the agent or the instrument' when it is respectively employed in connection with a sage or a deity.

That is to say, when applied to a *Rishi* the force is that of an instrument, and when applied to a *Devat* the force is that of an agent. As, पविजोऽयवृषिः 'this sage is sacred' (through whose instrumentality one is sanctified) अभिः पविजं स, मा पुनातु 'the God Agni is sacred' (one that purifies), 'let him purify me'. So also, वायुः सोमः सूर्यः इन्द्रः पविजं ते मा पुनन्तु ।

शीतः कः ॥ १८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ शि-इतः, कः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शीतो धातोर्वर्तमानोऽयं क्तमत्ययो भवति ॥

187. The verbal roots, marked with an indicatory मि, take the affix क्, in denoting the present time.

482

THE AFFIX KTA.

[BK. III. CH II. § 188.

The *Nishthā* affix क्, as a general rule, is a past participial affix and denotes past time; and is so ordained by rule III 2. 102. The present *sūtra* thus makes an exception in case of those verbs which are marked with an indicatory भि in the *Dhātupātha*; as भिमिश 'to be affectionately inclined'; मिज: (मि+क=मि+त=मि+न (VIII. 2. 42) 'being affectionately inclined'. So भिचिबा—चिबा: 'sounding inarticulately'; भिच्या—घुट: 'bold'. The *anuvṛtti* of वर्तनाने 'in the sense of the present', is read into this *sūtra* from III. 2. 123.

मतिबुद्धिपूजार्थेभ्यश्च ॥ १८८ ॥ पदानि ॥ मति-बुद्धि-पूजा-अर्थेभ्यः,

च, (कः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मतिरिच्छा, बुद्धिर्ज्ञानम्, पूजा सत्कारः, एतर्थेभ्यश्च धातुभ्यो वर्तनानार्थे क्रमयथो भवति ॥

188. And after roots denoting inclination, understanding, or respect, the affix क् is employed with the force of the present.

The word मति means 'wish' or 'desire'; बुद्धि means 'knowledge'; and पूजा means 'worship', 'honor' or 'respect'. As राजा मतः,—इटः,—बुद्धः,—ज्ञातः,—पूजितः, &c. 'the king wishes, desires, thinks, knows, honors, respects &c'.

The force of the word च is to include other kinds of verbs not included in the above *sūtra*. Thus the following participles have their senses confined not to the past time only: शौजितः 'practised'; रजितः 'protected'; क्षान्तः 'forbearing'; आकुटः 'censured'; जुटः 'pleased'; रुटः 'angry'; रुपितः 'angry'; अभिव्याहतः 'uttered'; हटः 'happy'; तुटः 'satisfied'; कान्तः 'favourite'; संयतः 'restrained'; उधतः 'ready'; कष्टः 'evil, misery' (with a future signification); and अमृतः 'immortal'. So also:—सुतः 'sleeping'; शयितः 'lying down'; आशितः 'eaten'; लिङः 'smeared'; तृतः 'satisfied'; all these have a present signification.

ॐ

# अथ ततीयाध्यायस्य ततीयः पादः ॥

# BOOK THIRD.

# CHAPTER III.

—:o:—

उदादयो बहुलं ॥१॥ पदानि ॥ उषा-आदयः, बहुलम्, (वर्तमाने) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उषादयः प्रत्यया वर्तमानेऽयं संज्ञायां विपये बहुलं भवन्ति ॥

1. The affixes 'Un' and the rest, with the force of the present, and with a sense simply appellative, are attached diversely.

The phrase 'with the force of the present' (implying neither past nor future time) and 'with a sense simply appellative' (and not descriptive) must be read into this sūtra by anuvṛtti from sūtras III. 2. 123 & 185. By using the word 'diversely' it is indicated that these affixes are, of course, applied after roots about which they are ordained, but they come also after roots about which they are not ordained. Sometimes we must infer their application by seeing actual words. Some affixes, though there be no express injunction regarding them, are to be inferred to belong to this class. The maxim in regard to the *Unādi* affixes is that when, in appellatives, we find the forms of verbal roots and affixes coming after them, then we may know, from the result as presented in the word, what are the indicatory letters which the affix must be possessed of in order to produce the result.

These affixes are not given in Pāṇini's work, but they have been separately collected. The affix उषा is the first of these. The first sūtra of *Unādi* affixes is the following—

कृपापाञ्चिन्स्वविसाध्यगृथ्य उषा ॥

The affix उषा comes after the verbs कृ 'to make', वा 'to blow', पा 'to drink', नि 'to overcome', नि 'to scatter', स्वप् 'to be pleasant to the taste', साप् 'to accomplish', and भाप् 'to pervade'.

Thus कृ+उषा=कारः 'an artisan'. So also, वायुः 'the wind'; पायुः 'the organ of excretion'; आयुः 'a drug (which overcomes disease)'; मायुः 'the bile'; स्वायुः 'sweet'; साप् 'who accomplishes the object of another, hence virtuous'; and आयुः 'quickly'.

These *Unādi* affixes come after a limited number of roots, and not after every root, as the affixes taught in this grammar whose application is general; hence the word बहुल has been employed. Moreover there has been no exhaustive enumeration of the several roots after which these affixes come:

35

484

THE UNADI AFFIXES.

[BK. III CH. III. § 2, 3.

only some of them have been collected in works treating of *Unādi* affixes. Thus though the affixes *उज्ज्व* is ordained after *इष*, it comes also after *शक* as *शंकुला*. In fact there is a long discussion and it was a moot point at the time of Pāṇini whether these words said to be formed by *Unādi* affixes were really derivative, or primitive ones. Moreover *all* the operations of these affixes have not been shown, that is, their effects are not without remainder (*सशेष*). They are valid and good if found in sacred Scriptures or secular literature. The authors of *Niruktas* and grammarians of the school of Sākatāyaṇa, consider all nouns and substantives (*नाम*) as derivative words from simple roots (*धातुज्ञ*). Therefore where the derivation of a word is not apparent, one should infer the existence of proper base (*प्रकृति*) or affix (*प्रत्यय*) to form such a word.

The following slokas will be of some use to the student for ascertaining the *Unādi* affixes :

बाहुलकं प्रकृतेस्तनुदृष्टेः प्रायसमुच्चयनादपि वेषाम् ।

कार्यसरोपविधेयं तदुक्तं नैमस्कृतिभवं हि सुसाम् ॥ १ ॥

नाम च धातुजमाह निरुक्ते व्याकरणे शकस्त्य च तोकम् ।

यत्र पदार्थविधेयसमुत्पन्नं प्रत्ययतः प्रकृतेः तदुद्याम् ॥ २ ॥

संज्ञासु धातुरूपाणि प्रत्ययाश्च ततः परे ।

कार्याद्विध्यावनुवन्धमेतच्छालमुपादिषु ॥ ३ ॥

भूतेऽपि दृश्यन्ते ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ भूते, अपि, दृश्यन्ते, (उत्पादयः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भूतेकाले उत्पादयः प्रत्यया दृश्यन्ते ॥

2. The 'Unādi' affixes are seen also attached with the force of the past time.

By the last *sūtra*, it was taught that the *Unādi* affixes come with the force of the present time. The present aphorism teaches that they come with the force of the past also, not as a general rule, but in special cases. The force of the words 'are seen' being that no general rule can be laid down about it, but on *finding* that certain words have a past significance, we conclude that the affix in that particular case has the force of the past time.

Thus वृत्+मनिन्=वर्णन् 'a way, road' (that which has been established as a rule); चर्+मनिन्=चर्मन् 'skin' (that which is lived in); so also भस्मन् 'ashes' (that which has been reduced to ashes).

भविष्यति गन्यादयः ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ भविष्यति, गति-आदयः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भविष्यति काले गन्यादयः शब्दाः साधवो भवन्ति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनघतन उपसंख्यानम् ॥

3. The words 'gami', &c. are valid forms, having the sense of the future time.

The force of the future time is in the affix, and is so ordained, and not in the original word which takes the affix. Thus we see that the *Unādi*

BK. III. CH. III. § 4, 5.] THE UNADI AFFIXES.

485

affixes, in a way, do come with the force of not only present, but past and future also, though in the latter two cases its scope is very limited. As गमी ग्रामम् 'intending to go to the village'; आगमी 'that which has to come' So also मस्यायी 'departing'; मतिरोधी 'an opponent, (who is going to obstruct). मतिरोधी 'going to be awakened'. So also मतिरोधी 'an adversary'; मतिरोधी 'an enemy'; मतिरायी; आयायी; मायी, &c.

*Vart*:—The Future, for the purposes of this rule, must be *anadyatana* future *i. e.* the affix should come in the sense of what will happen but not in the course of the current day. In other words, the force must be of the first future लूद, and not of the second future लूद. As 'वो गमी ग्रामम्' he intends to go to the village tomorrow'.

यावतपुरानिपातयोलैट् ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ यावत्-पुरा-निपातयोः, लट्, (भविष्यति) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यावतपुराश्रययोर्निपातयोरुपपययोर्भविष्यति काले धातोर्जदप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

4. The affix 'Lat' comes after a root, with the force of futurity, when it has in construction with it the particles 'yāvat' and 'purā'.

The present tense has the force of the future when the *adverbs* यावत् and तावत् are used. The phrase 'futurity &c' is to be read into this sūtra from the last. Thus आलोके ते निपतति पुरा 'he will surely fall in the range of your sight'. यावदस्य पुरातनः समुन्मूलमाय शत्रुघ्नं प्रेषयामि. 'I shall send Satrughna to exterminate this wretch'.

These words पुरा and यावत् must be used as *adverbs* (nipātas), and not as relative pronouns. Therefore not here, यावद् शस्यति तावद् भोक्त्यते 'as long as he will give, so long he will eat'; पुरा ब्रजिष्यति 'he goes along the city'. Here यावत् is a relative pronoun; and पुरा is the Instrumental singular of पुर 'city'.

विभाषा कदाकष्टोः ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, कदा-कष्टोः, (भविष्यति, लट्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कदाकष्टि इष्टेतयोरुपपययोर्बिभाषा भविष्यति काले धातोर्जदप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

5. The affix 'Lat' is optionally employed after a root with the force of the futurity, when it has in construction with it, the *adverbs* 'kadā' and 'karhi'.

As कदा मुहूक्ते 'when will he eat', or कदा भोक्त्यते or भोक्ता; so also कष्टि मुहूक्ते or भोक्त्यते or भोक्ता 'when will he eat'.

किंवृते लिप्सायाम् ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ किम्-वृते, लिप्सायाम्, (भविष्यतिकाले, विभाषा, लट्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ किंवृशतपपये लिप्सायां भविष्यति काले धातोर्बिभाषा लदप्रत्ययो भवति ॥

486

THE UNADI AFFIXES. [BK. III. CH. III. § 6, 7.

6. When the word 'kim' or its derivatives are in construction with the verb, the affix 'Lat' is employed optionally after a root, in denoting future time, provided that the sentence expresses a desire of gaining on the part of the speaker.

The word 'optionally' is understood in this sūtra. By using the word बुन along with कि it is meant that the rule applies even when किम् takes the affixes उत्तर and उत्तम. The word लिप्सा means the desire of gaining or acquiring, a wish to have something or an intention of begging.

As कं मयन्तो भोजयन्ति or भोजयिताः 'whom will you feed'? It implies a request on the part of the questioner to feed him also. So also कतरो भिन्नां शस्यति, शहति, शता, or कतरो भिन्नां शस्यति &c, 'Which of the two or which of these all, will he give alms? Will he give something to me'?

When no desire of gain is implied, the future tense must be employed as कः पाटलिपुत्रं गमिष्यति 'who will go to Pāṭaliputra'.

लिप्स्यमानसिद्धौ च ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ लिप्स्यमान-सिद्धौ, च, (भविष्यतिकाले, विभाया, लट्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लिप्स्यमानसिद्धौ गम्यमानायां भविष्यतिकाले धातोर्विभाषा लट्पत्ययो भवति ॥

7. And when the success, that would accrue to another by fulfilling the desire of the speaker, is indicated in a sentence, the present tense may optionally be employed with the force of the futurity.

The word 'optionally' is also understood here. The word लिप्स्यमानसिद्धिः is equal to लिप्स्यमानात् सिद्धि, an Ablative-Tatpurusha Compound, signifying *siddhi* or success, that would be acquired by another by complying with the request of the speaker. The difference between this and the last sūtra is, that whereas the last related to interrogative sentences having किम् in construction, the present relates to sentences in general. As यो भक्तं शहति, स स्वर्गं गच्छति 'he who gives food, goes to heaven'; यो भक्तं शस्यति or शता, स स्वर्गं गमिष्यति or गन्ता.

Here the speaker encourages the giver to the act of charity by holding out the hope, that from rice which is the object desired (लिप्स्यमान) the success (सिद्धि), in the shape of *svarga*, will accrue to the giver.

In other words, 'the present is sometimes used for the future in conditional sentences, *i. e.* it is employed in connection with a sentence declaring the compensation or reward which follows from the granting of the wish'.

लोह्यैल्लक्षे च ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ लोह्य-अर्यै-लक्षे, च, (भविष्यतिकाले, विभाया, लट्) ॥

BK. III. CH. III. § 8-10]

THE AFFIXES TUMUN AND NVUL.

487

वृत्तिः ॥ लोढः वैष्णवलक्ष्यते येन स लोढयलक्ष्यैः धात्वर्थः, तत्र वर्तमानाद्वालोर्भविष्यति काले विभाषा लट्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

8. The affix 'Lat' is optionally employed with the force of the futurity, after that root, which in a conditional sentence, is the condition precedent for the action indicated by another verb having the sense of the imperative mood.

The word लोढः means 'having the sense of the affix लोढ or imperative mood'. The force of *lat* is 'to command, direct, invite &c' as given in III. 3. 162 and 163. The *sūtra*, translated literally, will mean 'the present tense may optionally be employed when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the imperative, as a sign (लक्षण) is to the thing signified (लक्ष्य)'. Thus उपाध्यायभेदागच्छति (आगमिष्यति or आगन्ता) अथ त्वं छन्दोऽधीच्च 'if the professor *comes* (i. e. will come) then *read* you prosody'. Here the coming of the professor is the *lakshana* of the direction as to reading.

लिङ् चोर्ध्वमौहूर्तिके ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ लिङ्, च, ऊर्ध्व-मौहूर्तिके, (भविष्यतिकाले, विभाषा, लट्, लोढयलक्ष्यैः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊर्ध्वमौहूर्तिके भविष्यतिकाले लोढयलक्ष्यैः वर्तमानाद्वालोर्भविष्यति लिङ्प्रत्ययो भवति, चकाराल्लट् ॥

9. The 'Lat' (present) or the 'Lin' (potential) is used under similar conditions in denoting futurity, when the future time is future by a 'muhūrta' (48 minutes).

All the conditions of the last *sūtra* apply here also, namely 'when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the imperative, as a sign is to the thing indicated'. By force of the word च we read the *anuvṛtti* of *lat* also into this aphorism. The word ऊर्ध्व-मौहूर्तिके is a secondary derivative from ऊर्ध्वमुहूर्त, meaning 'that which exists in time *above* a *muhūrta*'. This is an irregular compound; and the *vriddhi* takes place irregularly of the उ of मु and not of क as the general rule required. The whole word thus formed qualifies the word 'future'. Thus ऊर्ध्व मुहूर्तावृत्ति मुहूर्तस्य उपाध्यायभेदागच्छत् (आगच्छति, आगमिष्यति or आगन्ता), अथ त्वं छन्दोऽधीच्च 'If the teacher *comes* after an hour (of 48 minutes), you had better read the Prosody'.

तुमुनगवुली क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ तुमुन्, गवुली, क्रियायां, क्रियार्थायाम्, (भविष्यति काले) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्रियार्थायां क्रियायामुपपत्ते धातोर्भविष्यति काले तुमुनगवुली प्रत्ययो भवतः ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ क्रियार्थायां क्रियायामुपपत्ते वासरूपेण दत्तादयो न भवन्ति ॥

10. The affixes 'tumun' and 'nvul' are placed after a verbal root, with the force of the future, when the

36

488

THE AFFIXES GHAN &C.

[BK. III. CH. III. § II.]

word in construction therewith is another verb, denoting an action performed for the sake of the (future) action.

As भोग्नू ब्रजति 'he goes to eat'; भोग्नू ब्रजति 'he goes to eat'. Here the upapada or the verb in construction is ब्रजति; it denotes an action performed for the sake of the future action (क्रियायां), namely, eating.

Why do we say 'denoting an action'? The upapada must be an action and not a substantive; as भिजित्ये इति अस्य जटा: 'matted hair is for the purpose that he should beg.' Here the affixes are not employed.

Why do we say 'performed for the sake of another action'? Observe भावतस्ते पतिष्यति इण्ड: 'running, thy stick will fall'.

Now, it might be asked why ख्वज is taught a second time, when it was already taught generally by rule III. I. 133; and that being a common rule, would have applied to this subject also? If you reply that the future affix ख्वज would have prevented its application, in conditional sentences like the above, we say that the rule of 'non-uniform affixes applying simultaneously' given in III. I. 94 will step in and will conduce the application of ख्वज in spite of ख्वज.

*Vart.*—The repetition of the affix ख्वज (ordained to come after a verbal root, when the word in construction therewith is another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action,) is for the sake of prohibiting the application of the affixes like ख्वज &c. in denoting the above sense; that is to say, the rule of वाऽसरूप (III. I. 94) does not apply here and we cannot optionally employ any other affix, with this gerundial sense. Thus we cannot say कर्ता ब्रजति 'he goes to do'; but we must say कर्तुम् instead.

These affixes form the gerund of the infinitive of purpose.

भाववचनाश्च ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि ॥ भाव-वचनाः, च, (भविष्यति, काले, क्रियायां, क्रियायायाम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भावइति प्रकृत्य ये पचाययो विहितास्ते च भाववचना भविष्यतिकाले क्रियायामुपपत्ते क्रियायां भवन्ति ॥

11. And the affixes that are ordained to come after a root with the force of denoting the mere action of the verb, such as ख्वज &c. (III. I. 13.) have also the force of the future, when the word in construction therewith, is another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action.

As पाकाय ब्रजति 'he goes to cook'; मूर्तये ब्रजति 'he goes for the sake of success'; पुष्टये ब्रजति।

Now it might be asked, why make this rule at all, when those affixes have already been ordained? It has already been said that the वाऽसरूप rule

BK. III. CH. III. § 12 ] THE AFFIX AN.

489

does not apply in regard to infinitive; and hence तुम् would have prevented the application of other affixes. So the making of the present sutra.

Why the word वचन has been employed in the sutra? The meaning is that the words should be expressive or वाचक. How do the affixes become वाचक? When affixes which are ordained after certain bases, are employed after those bases only, then they are said to be वाचक, not when they are employed after other bases, or are even after those bases, but not in the mode as directed. So that, in short, those nouns only which have been especially formed by the भाववाच्य affixes, वच् &c, can be employed with the force of gerund, and not every noun. The भाववाच्य nouns correspond to the nouns of action or verbal nouns.

अण् कर्मणि च ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अण् कर्मणि, (भविष्यति, काले, क्रियायां, क्रियायोयान्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धातोरुपस्थयो भवति भविष्यतिकाले कर्मणयुपपे क्रियायां च क्रियायोयान् ॥

12. The affix 'an' comes after a root with the force of the future, when the word in construction with it is in the accusative case, and when the action is performed for the sake of another action.

The word 'future' is understood here. The force of च is merely that of a connective particle. By rule III. 2. 1. the affix अण् comes after a root when the word in composition is in the accusative case. That is a general injunction; and the rule of वाचकूप not applying, the affix ण्वुज् would have debarred it as already said; hence this repetition. This rule being an apavāda rule (an exception or a special rule with regard to those verbs which have the accusative case in composition) will thus, within its own jurisdiction, prevent the application of ण्वुज् of III. 3. 10; and by the rule of परत्व given in I. 4. 2, it will debar the affixes like क &c. Therefore this अण् comes after even those verbs also which were especially exempted from its operation by rules like III. 2. 3. Thus by rule III. 2. 3 the अण् of III. 2. 1 could not have come after simple verbs ending in long आ, such as वा 'to give' &c. But the present अण् with a gerundial force will come even after such verbs. As गोदायो ब्रजति 'he goes to give cows', and not गोदाः । So also क्म्बलदायो ब्रजति 'he goes to give blanket'; अङ्गदायो ब्रजति । वा+अण्=दायः (VII. 3. 33).

So also काण्डलायो ब्रजति 'he goes to cut wood'. In this case अण् would have been applied even by III 2. 1.

लुट् शेषे च ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुट्, शेषे, च, (भविष्यति, क्रियायां, क्रियायोयां, धातोः, लट्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शेषे गुडे भविष्यतिकाले चकारात् क्रियायां चोपपे क्रियायोयां धातोः लट्, मस्ययो भवति ॥

490

THE AFFIX LUT. [BK. III. CH. III. § 13-15.

13. The affix 'Lṛit' is employed after a verb, in the remaining cases, where futurity pure and simple is indicated; and also where there is in construction with it another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action.

This is what is well-known as the Second Future. As करिष्यामि इति ब्रजति 'he goes that I will do'; हरिष्यामि इति ब्रजति 'he goes that I will take'. So also, करिष्यति 'he will do'; हरिष्यति 'he will take'. Thus the Second Future is used both in dependent sentences as well as to denote simple Future.

लुटः सद्वा ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुटः, सद्व, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लटः स्थाने सत्संज्ञो शहशानचो वा भवतः ॥

14. The affixes called 'Sat' i. e. 'śatri' and 'śānach' are optionally the substitutes of 'Lṛit'.

The सत् has been defined in III. 2. 127. This option is a regulated option; that is to say, the affixes शह्व and शानच् replace लुद् under the conditions in which they replace लद्; thus by III. 2. 124, these affixes will replace लुद् when agreeing with what does not end with the first case-affix. In these cases सत् will invariably replace लद्. In other cases it will optionally replace लद्. In these cases they will form what is known as future participles. As करिष्यन्ते देववत्तं पश्य 'behold Devadatta about to do; करिष्यमाणां देववत्तं पश्य 'behold Devadatta being about to be done'. हे करिष्यन् or हे करिष्यमाणां. Besides simple futurity, it denotes intention or purpose, as अजेयिष्यमाणो वसति 'he dwells intending to earn his livelihood'; करिष्यमाणां सश्रं श्रासनं 'intending to furnish his bows with arrows'.

When, however, it agrees with the nominative case, it is optionally employed. As करिष्यन्, करिष्यमाणां, करिष्यति or करिष्यन्ते देववत्तः 'Devadatta will do'.

The form करिष्यन् is thus evolved. As कु+लुद्=कु+स्य+लुद् (III. 1. 33)= कर+इद+स्य+शह्व=करिष्यन् nom. sing. करिष्यन्। In other words the participial affixes अन् (अन्त) and मान, technically known as शह्व and शानच्, also come after a verb that has taken the personal ending स्य of the Future.

अनद्यतने लुट् ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनद्यतने, लुट्, (भविष्यति) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भविष्यवन्तयतने?यं वर्णमानाद्वातोजुंदयत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ परिवेवने चस्तनी भविष्यवयं वक्तव्या ॥

15. The affix 'Lut' comes after a verbal root in the sense of what will happen, but not in the course of the current day.

This debars 'Lṛit'. As 'भः कर्ता' 'he will do tomorrow'. इषो भोक्ता 'he will eat tomorrow'.

BK. III. CH. III. § 16-18.] THE AFFIX GHAN.

491

The word 'anadyatana' is a Bahuvrihi compound. Therefore in cases where there is not pure futurity beyond today, but a mixture of the two, लूट् will be employed and not लू. As अय भ्यो वा भविष्यति 'it will be today or tomorrow'. And where there is doubt, the second Future should be employed.

Vart.—The First Future (लू) is employed with the force of the Second Future (लू) when sorrow is expressed. As इयं तु कदा गन्ता, यैषं पादौ निश्चाति! 'Oh when will she go, who places her feet in such a way (who is such a slow walker)' अयं तु कदा-ध्येता, य एवमननियुक्तः 'when will he learn, who is so inattentive!'

पद्मनविश्वस्यो घञ् ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ पद-रज-विश-स्वशः,

घञ् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पदाभियो धातुभ्यो घञ्-प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

16. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'pad' (to pace), 'ruj' (to pain), 'viś' (to enter), and 'spriś' (to touch).

The anuvritti of 'future' does not extend to this sutra. The affixes hereinafter taught come in all the tenses.

As पद+घञ्=पादः 'foot'; रज+घञ्=रोगः 'disease'; so, वेशः 'entrance'.

Vart.—The verb स्वः takes घञ् when the sense is that of 'distress'; as स्वः 'disease' or 'warmth'. The word स्वः meaning 'touch' is formed by adding the affix अच्, under rule III. I. 134; as स्वः वैष्वतः। There is difference in accent between these two words.

स्विरे ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्व, स्थिरे, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सत्त्वहीतोः स्थिरे कर्तारि घञ् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकन् ॥ व्याधिनस्त्ययज्ञेष्विति वक्तव्यम् ॥

17. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'sri' (to move) when the agent is permanently fixed.

The word स्थिर means an object remaining steady throughout any period of time. That which thus remaining permanent moves through any interval of time, will apply to the agent of the verb. Thus, ख+घञ्=सारः 'an essence'; as चन्दनसारः 'the essence of sandal', खदिरसारः 'the essence of catechu'.

Why do we say 'permanently fixed'? Observe सत्ता 'moves', सारकः 'that which flows'.

Vart.—The word so formed also applies to disease, fish and strength. As अतिसारः 'dysentery'; विसारः 'a fish'; सारः 'strength'.

भावे ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ भावे, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भावे वाच्ये धातोपर्यन्त प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

18. The affix 'ghan' comes after a root when mere action is denoted.

37

492

THE AFFIX GHAN. [BK. III. CH. III. § 19.

Thus, पच्+घञ्=पाकः 'cooking' (VII. 2. 116 and VII. 3. 52); स्थानः 'abandoning'; रागः 'colouring' (VI. 4. 27). An action expresses a general state; so that all roots denote 'action' when their meaning is to be expressed. And as the meaning of the root can be expressed by the root itself, therefore, the affixes घञ् &c. come after all verbal roots, when the sense of the root is denoted as having attained to the completed state. It is not necessary that the words so formed should be always of the masculine gender, singular number. They may take any other gender or number. As पक्तिः, पचनम्, पाकी, पाकाः। These affixes form, in short, verbal nouns, or abstract nouns being names of action.

अकर्तरि च कारके संज्ञायाम् ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ अ-कर्तरि, च, कारके, संज्ञायाम्, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तवर्जिते कारके संज्ञायां विपये धातीर्थम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

19. And the affix 'ghan' comes after a root, when the sense is that of an appellative, the word being related to the verb from which its name is deduced, but not as agent.

Thus प्रासः (i. e. प्रास्थन्ति तम्) 'a dart, lit. that which men throw'; प्रसंयः (i. e. प्रसीत्यन्ति तम्) 'a sack, lit. that which men stitch together'; आहारः (i. e. आहारन्ति असाहसम्) 'food, lit. that from which men take out the juice to nourish themselves'. As मधुराहारः, नक्षत्राहारः।

Why do we say 'not related as an agent'? Observe मेषः 'a sheep, lit. that which looks helplessly'. Here the word मेष is related to the verb मिथति as agent, and the affix is consequently not घञ्.

Why do we say 'when denoting an appellative'? Observe कर्तव्यः कटः 'the mat must be made'.

The force of च in the sutra is to indicate that घञ् may be applied irregularly in cases where appellative is not meant: as को भवता दासो दत्तः 'what gift was given by you'; को भवता ज्ञानी लब्धः 'what gain was gained by you'.

The word कारक is used in the sutra for this purpose. The word अकर्तरि is a compound word formed by the negative नम्. The word means a non-agent. Now the word 'non-agent' has two-fold significance; either it means any other kāraka which is not an agent-kāraka; or it may mean any thing in general which is not an agent. That is to say, the former negative, called पश्चैदास, points out, by implication, the objects which are different from the thing prohibited; and in fact, makes the rule applicable to those objects; while the second sort of negative called प्रसन्न्य प्रतिषेध is a simple prohibition of the particular matter specified, without mentioning what is different from it. Giving the former interpretation to the word अकर्तरि, the word कारक becomes redundant, because 'non-agent' would mean any kāraka other than an agent.

BK. III. CH. III. § 20.] THE AFFIX GHAN.

493

But the very fact, that कारक is used, indicates the existence of the following rule which is nowhere expressly taught by Pāṇini:—That नम् is compounded even with the force of प्रसन्न प्रतिषेध. (VI. I. 45). अशित्, non-sit'.

Both the phrases, 'when denoting mere condition (नाव)' and 'a kāraka 'which is not an agent' are understood in the succeeding aphorisms. See II 2. 6 about नम् Compound.

परिमाणाख्यायां सर्वेभ्यः ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ परिमाण-आख्या-

याम्, सर्वेभ्यः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिमाणाख्यायां सर्वेभ्यो धातुभ्यो घञ् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ हारनारो कर्तारि पिण्डुक् च ॥

20. The affix 'ghan' comes after all roots when the word so formed is the name of a measure.

Thus, नि+चि+घञ्=निचै+अ (VII. 2. 115)=निचाय(VI. 1. 78) 'a heap'; as एकस्तण्डुलनिचाय; हीं शूर्पनिष्पत्ती। कू 'to scatter'+घञ्=कारः। हीं कारि; नयः काराः।

By using the word 'all' in the sūtra, it is indicated that the affix अप् (III. 3. 57) is also superseded when this sense is to be indicated. Otherwise the affix अच् would only be prohibited by the Paribhāṣha:—"Apavādas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavāda-operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to them, not the subsequent rules". Thus अच् being taught in III. 3. 56 would be superseded, but not so अप् taught in the subsequent aphorism III. 3. 57.

Why do we say 'when they are the names of measures'? Observe निश्चयः 'ascertaining'.

The word आख्यः has been used in the aphorism in order to indicate that the words so formed are not Primitive words (रूचि). The numerals are also there included, and not only measures like Prastha, Pala &c.

We have said above, that the force of the word सर्वेभ्यः in this sūtra is to indicate that the affix घञ् must be used after all verbs (not excluding even such verbs as require अच् or अप् by sūtras 56 and 57), when we want to express measure. This must be taken however, with certain limitations. The word सर्वेभ्यः is not after all so wide as at first sight it may appear. If we wish to form a word indicating measure, in the feminine gender, we cannot use घञ्; we must use the affix किन्तु (III. 3. 94). In other words, the feminine affixes are not superseded by घञ् when it supersedes अच् and अप्. Thus in forming a feminine noun denoting measure, we have एकातिलोच्छित्तिः, द्वे प्रसूती &c.

Vart:—The affix घञ् comes after the causative verbs वारि and जारि, and there is luk elision of the causative affix पिण्डु; when the word so formed is related to the verb as agent. Thus हारयन्ति धातून्=द्वारा: 'a wife' (lit 'who divides brothers' a wife breaking up the brotherly love); नारयन्ति=जारा: 'a paramour',

494

THE AFFIX GHAN.

[BK. III. CH. III. § 21-24.

इङ् ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ इङ्, च, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इङ् धातोर्ध्वम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अपादाने स्त्रियामुपसंख्यानम् तदन्ताच्च वा ङीप् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ शु वायुवर्णनिवृत्तेषु ॥

21. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'in' (to study).

This debars अच् (III. 3. 56). As अधि+इ+घम् = अधि+ऐ+अ = अध्याय 'a lesson or lecture'; उपाध्याय: (उपेत्याख्याधीन) 'a teacher'.

Vart.—When the word to be formed is related to the verb इङ् as an ablative, the word is feminine also and optionally takes the affix ङीप्. As उपेत्याधीनस्त्वः = उपाध्यायो or उपाध्यायी 'a female teacher'.

Vart.—The affix घम् comes after the root ङ, when the word so formed means 'wind', 'color', or 'cessation'. As द्वारः 'wind', 'green colour' &c. गौरिवाकृत-नीश्वरः प्रायेण शिशिरे कृशः ।

उपसर्गे रुवः ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गे, रुवः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गे उपपदे रौतैर्ध्वतोर्ध्वम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

22. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'rū' (to roar), when it has an upasarga in composition with it.

This debars अच् (III. 3. 57). As संरावः 'clamour', उपरावः &c.

Why do we say 'compounded with an upasarga'? Observe रवः 'sound'.

सनि युद्धुवः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, युद्धु-दुवः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सनि उपपदे युद्धु इत्येतेभ्यो धातुभ्यो घम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

23. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'yu' (to join), 'dru' (to run) and 'du' (to burn), when in composition with the preposition 'sam'.

As संरावः, संरावः, संरावः But प्रयवः where the preposition is not sam.

त्रिशीभुवोऽनुपसर्गे ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ त्रि-शी-भुवः, अनुपसर्गे, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्रि-शी भू इत्येतेभ्यो धातुभ्योऽनुपसर्गेभ्यो घम् प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

24. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'sri' (to go to) 'ni' (to lead) and 'bhū' (to be), when not in composition with an upasarga.

This debars the affix अच् (III. 3. 56). As श्रायः 'shelter', नायः 'a means', भावः 'a condition'.

But with upasargas, we have प्रश्नः 'respect', प्रणयः 'love'; प्रश्नः 'source'.

How do we explain the form प्रभाव in प्रभावी राजः 'the splendour of the king'? Here the word प्रभाव is not made from the compound root प्रभू+घम्, but by compounding प्र with भाव by the rules of samāsa, meaning 'excellent condition'.

BK. III. CH. III. § 25-29.] THE AFFIX GHAN.

495

How do you explain the form नय in नयो राजः? Here the root नो has taken the affix अच् diversely by III. 3. 113.

वौ सुबुवः ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ वौ, सु-बुवः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वावुपपे सु सु इरयेताभ्यो धातुभ्यो घञ् प्रस्थयो भवति ॥

25. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'kshu' (to sneeze), and 'śru' (to move and hear) when the preposition 'vi' is in composition.

This debars the affix अप (III. 3. 57); as, विश्रामः 'cough'; विश्रामः 'flowing forth', 'celebrated'. But when without preposition, we have श्रवः and श्रवः।

अवोदोनियः ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अव-उदोः, नियः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अव उत् इरयेतयोः पपयेयोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः

26. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'ni' (to lead) when the prepositions 'ava' and 'ut' are in composition.

As अवनायः 'throwing down'; उन्नायः 'elevation'.

How do you explain उन्नयः in उन्नयः स्वार्थानाम्? Here the affix is 'ach' by III. 3. 113.

प्रे दुस्तुसुवः ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रे, दु-स्तु-सुवः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रे-स्तु उपपे दु स्तु सु इरयेतेभ्यो धातुभ्यो घञ् प्रस्थयो भवति ॥

27. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'dru', 'stu' and 'sru', when the word in composition is 'pra'.

As प्रहावः, प्रस्तावः, प्रसादः। But not so in द्रवः, स्तवः and श्रवः।

निरभ्योः पूरवोः ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ निर-अभ्योः, पू-रवोः (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निरभिपूर्वयोः पूरवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः

28. The affix 'ghan' comes after the roots 'pū' (to purify) and 'lu' (to cut) when 'nir' and 'abhi' are respectively in composition.

The word पू refers to both पूर् and पूम्. The rule I. 3. 10. must be applied here, and thus निर comes before पू, and अभि before ज्। As निष्पावः 'win-nowing'; अभिज्ञावः 'moving'. But पवः and श्रवः, without these prepositions.

उन्न्योग्रेः ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ उत्-न्योः, ग्रः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उन्न्योग्रेपपयेयोः गु इरयेतस्माद्वातोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः येवोः

29. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'gri' when the upasargas 'ut' and 'ni' are in composition.

The verb गु here refers to both the verbs गु 'to make sound', and गु 'to swallow'. As उद्गारः समुद्रस्य 'the roaring of the sea'; निगारो देवव्रतस्य 'the swallow-

38

496

THE AFFIX GHAN. [BK III. CH. III. § 30-33.

ing of Devadatta'. But when without these prepositions, we have गरः।

कू धान्ये ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ कू, धान्ये, (घञ्, उन्न्याः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कू इत्येतस्माद्वातोरुन्न्योरुपपद्योर्ध्वं प्रत्ययो भवति धान्यविषयश्चेत्सत्ययो भवति ॥

30. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'krī', when the prepositions 'ut' and 'ni' are in composition and when the sense of the verb relates to grain.

The verb कू here means 'to scatter', and not 'to injure', because no words formed by this affix are found in Sanskrit in that sense.

As उत्कारी धान्यस्य 'the winnowing of corn'; निकारी धान्यस्य 'the winnowing of corn'. But when not referring to grain, we have भैष्योरुकरः 'a heap of alms', पुष्पनिकरः 'the essence or heap of flowers'.

यज्ञे सनि स्तुवः ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ यज्ञे, सनि, स्तुवः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यज्ञविषये प्रयोगे संपूर्णस्तोत्प्रेक्ष्य प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

31. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'stu' when it is preceded by the upasarga 'sam' and the word refers to sacrificial subjects.

As संस्तावश्छन्दोगानान् 'the Sanstāva of the Chhandogas; संस्ताव(=समेत्य स्तुवन्ति यस्मिन् देशो छंदोगाः स देशः) means 'the place which the Brāhmaṇas repeating hymns and prayers, occupy at a sacrifice'.

But when not referring to sacrifice we have संस्तावश्छन्दगोः 'the praising together of the two pupils'.

प्रे स्त्रोऽयज्ञे ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रे, स्त्रः, अयज्ञे, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्त्रम्, आच्छादने अस्माद्वातोः प्रश्रव्यउपपदे घञ्, प्रत्ययो भवति, न चेयज्ञविषयः प्रयोगो भवति ॥

32. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'strī' (to cover), when preceded by the preposition 'pra'; provided that the word so formed does not refer to sacrifice'.

As, शंखप्रस्तारः 'a bed of conch'; मणिप्रस्तारः 'strewing of gems'.

प्रयने वावशब्दे ॥३३॥ पदानि ॥ प्रयने, वो, अशब्दे, (स्त्रः, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्त्रम्, आच्छादने अस्माद्वातोर्विश्रव्यउपपदे घञ्, प्रत्ययो भवति प्रयने गन्धमाने तच्चे स्वयने श्रव्यविषयं न भवति ॥

33. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'strī' (to cover), when the preposition 'vi' is in composition with it, when the sense is that of extension, and when such spreading does not refer to words.

BK. III. CH. III. § 34-36.]

THE AFFIX GHAN.

497

The word पवन means 'extent, circuit, range'. As पत्तस्व विस्तारः 'the extension of the garment'.

Why do we say 'when meaning extent'? Observe, छण्डविस्तरः 'a collection of grass'. Why do we say 'not referring to words'? Observe विस्तरो वचसाम् 'prolixity of words'.

छन्दो नास्ति च ॥ ३४ ॥ छन्दः, नास्ति, च, (वै, स्त्रः, घ०)

वृत्तिः ॥ विपूर्वानुच्छ्रणासेऽछन्दोनास्ति घम्, प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

34. The affix 'ghan' comes after 'stri' with the upasarga 'vi', when the word so formed is the name of a metre.

The word छन्द here means prosodial metre such as Gāyatri &c; and not the Vedas; otherwise the word नाम would not have been used. Thus वि+स्त+घम्=वि+त्त+घम्(VIII. 3. 94)=विहारः 'the name of a metre called Vishṭāra-Pankti'.

The whole word विहारपंक्ति is the name of a metre, and is not a word *en ding* with the affix *ghan*; only a member of this word, *i. e.* the first part ends with *ghan*. The seventh case-affix in the word छन्दोनास्ति has the force of location *i. e.* when the word so formed occurs *in* a portion of a name of a metre; it is not the *full* name, but it is *in* the name *i. e.* forms a portion of the name.

उदि ग्रहः ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदि, ग्रहः, (घ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदुपपे महेन्द्रतोर्धम्पत्ययो भवति ॥

वास्तिकम् ॥ छन्दसि निपूर्वार्पण्यते सुगृधमननिपातनयोः ॥

35. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'grah' (to seize), when the preposition 'ut' is in composition.

This debars the affix अप्. As उद्गाहः 'lifting up'.

*Vart:*—In the Vedas this affix is applied even when the word ग्रह is preceded by नि; and the ह is changed into भ; the sense of the two words being 'to lift up' and 'throw down' respectively of the sacrificial ladle; as, उद्गानं च निपानं च ब्रह्मवेवा अवीषधम् ।

सनि मुष्टी ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, मुष्टी, (ग्रहः, घ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सम्पुपपे महेन्द्रतोर्धम्पत्ययो भवति मुष्टिविषयश्चैधात्वयो भवति ॥

36. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'grah' when in composition with the preposition 'sam' when the sense of the root refers to fist.

The word मुष्टि means 'boxing', 'fist'; as, अहो मल्लस्य संग्राहः 'O! the clenching of the fist of the athlete'; अहो मुष्टिकस्य संग्राहः 'O! the seizing of the boxer', meaning grasping firmly.

Why do we say 'referring to fist'? Observe संग्रहो धान्यस्य 'a collection of grain'.

498

THE AFFIX GHAN. [BK III. CH. III. § 37-39.

परिन्योर्नीशोद्यूताश्चेषयोः ॥३९॥ पदानि ॥ परि-न्योः, नी-इशोः,

द्यूत-अश्चेषयोः, (च०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिशब्दे निशब्दे चोपपदे यथासंभव नित्य इणश्च धातोर्ध्वभूयत्ययो भवति, अचो-पदादः, व्युताश्चेषयोः ॥

37. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the roots 'ni' (to lead), and 'i' (to go), when the prepositions 'pari' and 'ni' are respectively in composition with them, and when the words so formed respectively mean 'a game' and 'propriety or arrangement or law'.

Here again we take help of I. 3. 10 in interpreting this sutra. The verbs परि+नी and नि+इ; take चम् when respectively meaning 'gambling' and 'fitness'. As परिणामेन शारान् हन्ति 'he kills (or takes) many pieces by moving a chessman.' Here परिणाम=समन्ताजय means 'the moving of chess-pieces from every side, and so winning the game'. So also नि+इ+चम्=नि+पे+अ=नि+आय=न्यायः 'justice', 'propriety', 'logic'.

But when not having these senses, we have परिणामः 'marriage', and न्ययं 'decay'; as न्ययकृतः पापः 'the sin has been destroyed'. The word अश्चेय means पदार्थानामनपचारो यथायामकरणम् ।

परावतुपात्यय इशः ॥३८॥ पदानि ॥ परै, अनुपात्यये, इशः, (च०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिशब्द उपपदे इणो धातोर्ध्वभूयत्ययो भवति अनुपात्यये शस्यमाने ॥

38. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the root 'i' (to go) in composition with the word 'pari' when the sense is that of following in regular succession.

As पर्यायः 'turn, succession'; तव पर्यायः 'thy turn'; मम पर्यायः 'my turn'.

Why do we say 'when meaning turn'? Observe कालस्य पर्यायः 'the lapse of time'. The word अनुपात्ययः=क्रमप्राप्तस्थानतिपातः 'not breaking the series or order'.

व्युपयोः शेतेः पर्याये ॥३९॥ पदानि ॥ वि-उपयोः, शेतेः, पर्याये, (च०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वि उप इत्येतयोरुपपदयोः शेतेधातोर्ध्वभूयत्ययो भवति ॥

39. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the root 'sī' (to lie down) when the prepositions 'vi' and 'upa' are in composition with it, and when the sense of the word so formed is that of 'regular succession'.

As, तव विशायः 'thy turn of sleeping' (i. e. the rest enjoyed in rotation by the sentinels on watch); मम विशायः 'my turn of rest'; तव राजोपशायः=तव राजानमु पशयितुम्पर्यायः 'thy turn of sleeping the king'.

Why do we say 'regular succession'? Observe उपशायः 'lying by the side of or ambush'; विशायः 'doubt'.

BK. III. CH. III. § 40-42.] THE AFFIX GHAN.

499

हस्तादाने चेरस्तेये ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ हस्तादाने, चेः, अस्तेये, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हस्तादाने गम्यमाने चिनोतेर्धातोर्ध्वप्रत्ययो भवति, नचेत् स्तेयं चौर्यं भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ उच्चयश्च प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

40. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'chi' (to collect), when the sense expressed is that of taking by hand, provided it does not refer to stealing.

By saying 'taking by hand' the close proximity of the person taking to the thing accepted or taken is indicated. As पुष्पप्रचायः 'gathering flowers by hand'; फलप्रचायः 'gathering fruits by hand'.

Why do we say 'taking by hand'? Observe वृक्षापस्थानां फलानां बह्या
प्रचयं करोति 'he gathers with the stick the fruits hanging on the top of the tree'.

Why do we say 'when not meaning to steal'? Observe पुष्पप्रचयधौर्यं
'the gathering of flowers by theft'.

Vart.—Prohibition must be stated in the case of the word उच्चयः
'gathering'; as पुष्पोच्चयः 'gathering of flowers by hand'.

निवासचित्तिशरीरोपसमाधानैष्वादेष्ट कः ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ नि-
वास-चित्ति-शरीर-उपसमाधानेषु, आदेः, च, कः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निवास चित्ति शरीर उपसमाधान, एतेष्वपेषु चिनोतेर्ध्वप्रत्ययो भवति धातोरादेभ
ककार आदेशो भवति ॥

41. The affix 'ghan', comes after the root 'chi' (to gather), and 'k' is the substitute of the initial 'ch' in these senses viz.—'a dwelling', 'a fire on the funeral pile', 'the body' and 'collection'.

That in which people dwell (निवसति) is called निवासः or 'dwelling'. That which is gathered together (चौर्यते) is called चित्ति or 'funeral pile'. शरीर means the body of all living beings; and उपसमाधान means making a heap. Thus निकायः 'a dwelling'; as in काशीनिकायः 'Kāsi-dwelling'; आकाशमग्निं चिन्तित 'let him arrange the ākāya fire i. e. the funeral fire'; कायः 'body', as अनित्यः कायः 'a perishable body'; महान् गोमय निकायः 'a heap of cow-dung'.

Why do we say 'when having these senses'? Observe चयः 'gathering'. Why is not this rule applied in महान् काशीनिकायः 'a large heap of wood'? Here multiplicity is expressed and not collection or aggregation.

संघे चानौत्तराधर्म्ये ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ संघे, च, अनौत्तराधर्म्ये,
(चेः, आदेभ, कः, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संघे वाच्ये चिनोतेर्द्वातोर्ध्वप्रत्ययो भवति आदेभ कः ॥

42. The affix 'ghan' comes after the root 'chi' (to gather) and 'k' is the substitute of the initial 'ch' in

39

500

THE AFFIX NACH. [BK. III. CH. III. § 43.

the sense of 'a multitude or assembly' (of living beings possessing some common characteristics), but not merely a confused crowd of men.

The word संघ means a collection or assembly of living beings. It is of two sorts:—either by collection of persons possessing common qualifications, or a mere confused crowd of men. The collection denoting a confused crowd is here excepted and by *paryudāsa* negation the other is taken. Thus भिक्षुक-निकाय: 'the assembly of beggars'; ब्राह्मणनिकाय: 'the assembly of Brāhmaṇas'; वैयाकरणनिकाय: 'the assembly of Grammarians'.

But सूकरनिकाय: 'a herd of hogs'; because it is a mere collection. So also कृताकृतसमुच्चय: 'the collection of what is done and not done'; प्रमाणसमुच्चय: 'the collection of proofs'. Here there is no संघ in either of the two senses, it not being a collection of living animals, the affix *ghañ* is not employed.

कर्मव्यतिहारे यच् स्त्रियान् ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्म-व्यतिहारे,  
यच्, स्त्रियान् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मव्यतिहारे गम्यमाने धातोऽच् प्रत्ययो भवति स्त्रीलिङ्गे वाच्ये ॥

43. The affix 'nach' comes after a root in denoting reciprocity of action, and the word so formed is in the feminine gender.

The word कर्म means 'action' and is not the technical 'Karma' meaning the accusative case. व्यतिहार means reciprocity or interchange of action. The word so evolved is feminine in form and denotes mere 'action' (भाव) also. The anubandha च् in णच् is qualitative and is added to distinguish this affix from other affixes: thus in *sūtra* V. 4. 14 this particular affix is meant.

Thus वि+अव+क्रू+एन्+अन्+डीप्=व्यावक्रोशी (V. 4. 14, and VII. 3. 6) 'mutual abuse'. So also व्यावहासी, व्यावक्रोशी. The affix णच् forms only an imaginary stem; for this stem must take the affix अन् by V. 4. 14, which even does not form the complete word until the affix डीप् of the feminine is added.

Why do we say 'in the feminine'? Observe व्यतिपाकी वर्तते।

The making of this a separate *sūtra* by itself and not reading it in the subdivision of feminine affixes beginning with क्तिन् (III. 3. 94) is for the sake of removing the obstructing aphorisms that would otherwise have prevented the application of this rule.

For, had it been taught in connection with क्तिन् &c, then the affixes that would have debarred क्तिन् &c, would *a fortiori* have debarred this also. But by keeping it separate from that class, it is indicated that those obstructive affixes which debar क्तिन् &c, do not debar this. Thus व्यावचोरी, व्यावचर्ची। Here चूत् being a व्यस्त class root would have taken युच् (III. 3. 107) in the femi-

BK. III. CH. III. § 44, 45.]

THE AFFIX GHAN.

501

nine, as चोराण; and चर्च would have taken अह by III. 3. 104, as चर्च. The roots ईह and ईह, by III. 3. 102 & 103, take अ by debarring किन्तु। This debarring affix अ, however, is not debarred by this rule; as व्यतीसा, व्यतीसा are the proper feminine forms, and not व्यतीसी &c. The form व्यातुक्षी is, however, an apparent exception. All these exceptions, counter-exceptions &c. are examples of बहुलं taught in III. 3. 113.

अभिविधौ भाव इनुण् ॥४४॥ पदानि॥ अभिविधौ, भावे, इनुण् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभिविधौ गम्यमाने धातोर्भावे इनुणपत्ययो भवति ॥

44. The affix 'inun' comes after a root in denoting condition, when co-extensiveness is meant.

The word अभिविधि means co-extensiveness, that is to say, the complete comprehension or relation between the action and the quality. Thus सारा-विष्णुम् 'a general or tumultuous uproar'; सं+कूट+इन्+अण् (V. 4. 15. and VI 4. 164) = सांकृटिनम् 'a general confusion'; so सांकृटिणम् 'a general flow or stream'.

Why do we say 'when meaning co-extensiveness'? Observe संकोटः, संरावः, संप्रावः।

Why do we use the word भाव again in this sutra, when its anuvritti was already flowing from sutra III. 3. 18? The object is that the वाऽसरूप rule (III. 1. 94) should not apply here and hence घञ् never comes in this sense. Pātanjali says that the repetition is for the sake of indicating that in neuter gender, when co-extensiveness is expressed, the affixes क् &c. are prohibited; so that the affixes क् &c. should not come in the neuter with the force of भाव।

The separateness of this sutra is for the same purpose as the last aphorism. The affix ल्युट् is not, however, prohibited; as संकृटनम्. See rule कृत्यल्युटो बहुलं (III. 3. 113). The affix इनुण् (the operative part being इन्) forms but an imaginary stem, which does not become real and complete till it takes the affix अण् by V. 4. 15, as shown above.

आक्रोशेऽवन्योग्रहः ॥४५॥ पदानि॥ आक्रोशे, अवन्योः, ग्रहः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अव नि इत्येतयोऽपपद्योर्महेधोर्नोर्ध्वपपत्ययो भवति आक्रोशे गम्यमाने ॥

45. The affix 'ghan' comes after the verb 'grah' (to seize), in composition with 'ava', and 'ni'; when malediction is meant.

Though इनुण् is immediately, near, we take the anuvritti of घञ् (III. 3. 16), because we see that its anuvritti is possible.

The word आक्रोशे means 'cursing'. As अवमाहो हन्त ते वृषभभूयात् 'cursed be thou, O! sinner'. So also निमाहन्ते भूयात्।

Why 'when meaning cursing'? Observe अवमहः पश्यः; निमहचोरस्य।

प्रे लिप्सायान् ॥४६॥ पदानि ॥ प्रे, लिप्सायान्, (ग्रहः, घञ्) ॥

502

THE AFFIX GHAN.

[BK. III. CH. III. § 46-49.

वृत्तिः ॥ प्राज्यउपपये प्रहर्षतोऽप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्यप्य

46. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the root 'grah', when the word 'pra' is in composition, and the sense denoted is the desire of acquisition.

As पानमाहेण चरति भिक्षुः पिण्डार्थी 'the beggar walks for the sake of alms, carrying a vessel in hand'; ह्युम्माहेण चरति द्विजो वृत्तिणार्थी 'carrying a sacrificial ladle, the Brāhmaṇa walks about for his fee'. The word लिप्सा means the wish to have something'.

Why do we say 'when meaning desire of gain'? Observe पमहो देववृत्तस्थ ।

परी यश्चे ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ परी, यश्चे, (ग्रहः, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिशब्दउपपये प्रहर्षपमपययो भवति ॥

47. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the root 'grah', in composition with 'pari' when it relates to sacrificial subjects.

As उत्तरपरिमाहः 'the northern fencing of the sacrificial altar'; अधर-परिमाहः 'the southern fencing of the sacrificial altar'.

Why do we say 'when relating to sacrifices'? Observe परिमहः देववृत्तस्थ 'the fencing of Devadatta'.

नै वृ धान्ये ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ नै, वृ, धान्ये, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निशब्दउपपये वृ इत्येतस्माद्वातोर्धान्यविरोधेऽभिधेये घञ् मपययो भवति ॥

48. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the verb 'vṛi' preceded by 'ni'; when the sense is that of grain.

The वृ here means both वृक् and वृञ्. This debars the affix अप्. As नीवारा: 'rice growing wild or without cultivation'.

Why do we say 'meaning grain'? Observe निवरा कन्या 'a virgin girl'.

उदि अयतियैतिरुद्रूयः ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदि, अयति-यैति-

पृ-द्रूयः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उच्छ्वउपपये श्रयस्याविभ्यो घञ् मपययो भवति ॥

49. The affix 'ghañ' comes after the verbs 'śri', 'yu', 'pū' and 'dru', when the preposition 'ut' is in composition.

This debars the affix-ach (III. 3. 56). Thus उच्छ्वायः 'rising of a planet'; उद्वायः 'mixing'; उत्वायः 'purifying ghee'; and उद्वायः 'flight'.

How do you explain the form समुच्छ्वायः in पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्वायाः? The word विनाश 'optionally' in the next sūtra, exerts a retrospective effect on this sūtra, and the form is an optional one. This is a most unusual thing and is

BK. [III. CH. III. § 50-52.] THE AFFIX GHAN.

503

called सिंहावलोकनन्याय: 'the maxim of the lion's backward glance'. It is used when one casts a retrospective glance at what he has left behind, while at the same time he is proceeding, just as the lion, while going onward in search of prey, now and then bends his neck backwards to see if any thing be within its reach.

विभाषा ऽङि रूपलुवोः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, आङि, रूपलुवोः, (घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आङि उपपदे रौते: हवलेश् विभाषा घञ्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

50. The affix 'ghañ' is optionally employed after the verbs 'ru' (to roar) and 'plu' (to float), when the preposition 'āñ' is in composition.

As आराव: or आरव: 'noise'; आह्वाव: or आह्वन: 'bathing'.

अवे ग्रहो वर्षप्रतिबन्धे ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अवे, ग्रहः, वर्ष-प्रतिबन्धे, (विभाषा, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अव उपपदे ग्रहो वर्षप्रतिबन्धे भवति विभाषा वर्षप्रतिबन्धे निपेधे ॥

51. The affix 'ghañ' is optionally employed after the root 'grah', when the word 'ava' is in composition, the sense being withholding of rain.

The word 'optionally' is understood here. The word वर्षप्रतिबन्ध means the absence of rain, from some cause or another, when the season has arrived; as अवग्रह: or अवग्रहो देवस्य 'the draught of rain'.

Why do we say 'when meaning 'obstruction of rain'? Observe अवग्रहः पश्य ।

प्रे वशिजान् ॥ ५२ ॥ प्रे, वशिजान्, (विभाषा, ग्रहः, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्र शब्द उपपदे ग्रहो वर्षप्रतिबन्धे विभाषा घञ्प्रत्ययो भवति प्रख्ययान्तवाच्यश्चैव वशिजां सम्बन्धी भवति ॥

52. The affix 'ghañ' is optionally employed after the verb 'grah' in composition with 'pra', when the word so formed relates to commerce.

Both the words *grah* and *vibhāshā* are understood here. By 'relation to commerce' is meant here the string of the balance; and not commerce in general. That string by which a balance is held is called तुझापग्रहः or तुझापग्रहः, as तुझापग्रहेण चरति or तुझापग्रहेण चरति; and this may be said of any person whether he be a trader or not.

Why do we say 'when belonging to commerce'? Observe प्रगहो देवस्यस्य 'the whip of Devadatta'.

रश्मौ च ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ रश्मौ, च, (ग्रहः, विभाषा, प्रे, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्र शब्द उपपदे ग्रहो वर्षप्रतिबन्धे विभाषा घञ्प्रत्ययो भवति रश्मिश्चैव प्रत्ययान्तवानिधीयते ॥

40

504

THE AFFIX ACH. [BK. III. CH. III. § 53-56.

53. The affix 'ghañ' comes optionally after the verb 'grah' in composition with 'pra', when the word so formed means 'a rein'.

The word रुद्रिन means here the bridle by means of which horses &c. joined to the carriage, are held under control; as प्रमहः or प्रमाहः 'a rein'.

वृशोतेराच्छादने ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ वृशोतेः, आच्छादने, (वि-भाषा, प्रे, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्राज्जउपपदे वृशोतेभिर्तोर्विभाषा घञ् प्रस्थयो भवति प्रस्थयान्ते न चेदाच्छादनविरोध उच्यते ॥

54. The affix 'ghañ' comes optionally after the verb 'vri' (to choose), when 'pra' is in composition, and the word so formed means 'a sort of covering'.

As प्राबारः or प्रवरः 'a cloak, a veil'.

Why do we say 'when it means a covering'? Observe प्रवरागी।

परी भुवो अवज्ञाने ॥ ५५ ॥ परी, भुवः, अवज्ञाने, (विभाषा, घञ्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिराज्जउपपदे विभाषा घञ् प्रस्थयो भवति अवज्ञाने गन्धमाने ॥

55. The affix 'ghañ' is optionally employed after the verb 'bhū', the word 'pari' being in construction, and the sense of the word so formed being 'disregard'.

The word अवज्ञान means 'contempt', 'neglect', 'disregard' &c. As परिभावः or परिभवः 'insult, humiliation'.

Why do we say 'when meaning disregard'? The word परिभवः may be then construed to mean सर्वतोभवन्=परिभवः 'surrounding'.

एरच् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ एः, अच्, (अकर्तरि, संज्ञायाम्, भावे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इषणोन्ताञ्जातोर्भावे अकर्तरि च कारके संज्ञायामच्प्रस्थयो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अडिग्धो भयादिनामुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अवसवो छन्दसि वक्तव्यो ॥

56. The affix 'ach' comes after a root ending in 'i' or 'f' (when mere action is denoted, or when the sense is that of an appellative, the word being related to the verb from which its name is deduced, but not as an agent).

The words within brackets are to be supplied from sūtras 18 and 19: and these words are to be supplied in every subsequent sūtra as far as sūtra 113 of this chapter. This debars घञ्. The च् in अच् is qualitative, in sūtras like VI. 2. 144.

Thus, चयः 'collecting'; अयः 'going'; जयः 'victory'; ज्ञयः 'wasting'.

BK. III. CH. III. § 57, 58.]

THE AFFIX AP.

505

Vart.—In this connection the words भय &c. should also be enumerated. As भी+अच्=भयम् 'fear'; बधैम् 'rain'. These being neuter words, otherwise would have taken the affix क् &c. but for this Vārtika.

Vart.—The words ज्व् and सव are formed by this affix, and occur in the Vedas. As क्पेरिस्तु मे ज्वः, पंचौवनसवः। These roots जु and सु would have otherwise taken the affix अप्. The form would have been the same, but there would be difference of accent. See Rig. I. 112. 21, and Yaj. XI. 2.

कृदोरप् ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृत्-ओः, अप् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ककारान्तेभ्य उपगान्तेभ्य अप्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

57. After a root ending in long 'rī', short 'u', or long 'ū', there is the affix 'ap'.

This debars घञ्. The प् is indicatory for the sake of accent (III. 1. 3); as, कृ+अप्=करः 'scattering'; गृ-गरः 'beverage, poison'; शृ-शरः 'arrow'; यु-यवः 'barley'; लू-लवः 'reaping'; पू-पवः 'winnowing corn'.

The व् in कृप् is merely for the sake of euphony: it is not स् changed into व्; for then by the rule "that which follows व् is also called सपर" short उ only would have been taken and not long ऊ (I. 1. 70).

यहवृदुनिश्चिगमश्च ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ यह-वृ-दु-निश्चि-गमः, च्,

(अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रहाविन्यो धातुभ्यो ऽप्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ वशिरण्योरुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ घञ्यै कविधानं स्थानापाव्यधिहनियुध्यर्थम् ॥

58. The affix 'ap' comes after the verbs 'grah', 'vṛi', 'dṛi', 'niśchi' and 'gam'.

This debars घञ्; and in the case of निश्चि the affix अच् is debarred. As महः 'a planet'; वरः 'a boon'; हरः 'tearing, a cave'; निश्चयः 'certainty'; गमः 'march'.

The verb निश्चि would have taken अच्, but takes अप् which causes difference of accent.

Vart.—The roots वश् and रण् should also be included in this; as वशः 'obedient'; रणः 'battle'.

Vart.—When the sense is that of घञ्, the affix क् is directed to be employed, after the following verbs:—स्था, स्सा, पा, व्यध्, हन् and बुध्। As प्रस्थः 'a table-land' (on which they move); प्रस्तः 'a vessel for bathing' (in which they bathe); प्रपाः 'a place where water is distributed to travellers' (that out of which they drink); आविधः (VI. 1. 16) 'an awl, a drill' (that by which they pierce); विघ्नः 'an obstacle' (in which they are obstructed); आयुधः 'battle' (where they fight).

उपसर्गैऽदः ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गै, अदः, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गै उपपवेऽदेधीतोरुप्प्रत्ययो भवति ॥

506

THE AFFIX AP. [BK. III. CH. III. § 59-63.

59. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'ad' (to eat) when an upasarga is in composition.

As बिषसः (II. 4. 38) 'half-chewed morsel'; मपसः 'voracious'.

Why do we say 'when compounded with an upasarga'? Observe घासः 'grass'; अद्+घञ्=घस्+अ (II. 4. 38).

नै। ग। च ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ नै।, ग।, च, (अद्, अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निःशब्द उपपदे अवैधीतोऽप्यस्यो भवति चकारावद् च ॥

60. And the affix 'na' as well as 'ap', comes after the verb 'ad' (to eat), when the upasarga 'ni' is in composition.

As नि+अद्+घा=नि+आद्+अ=व्याकः (VII. 2. 116) 'feeding'; नि+अद्+अप्=नि+घस्+अ (II. 4. 38)=निषसः 'eating, food'.

व्यधजपोरनुपसर्गे ॥६१॥ पदानि ॥ व्यध-जपोः, अनुपसर्गे, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ व्यध जप इत्येतयोरनुपसर्गयोरप्यस्यो भवति ॥

61. The affix 'ap' comes after the verbs 'vyadh' and 'jap', when no upasarga is in composition with them.

This debars घञ्. As व्यधः 'wound'; जपः 'muttering'.

Why do we say 'when upasarga-less'? Observe आध्यायाः, उपजायाः ।

स्वनहसोवो ॥६२॥ पदानि ॥ स्वन-हसोः, वा, (अप्, अनुपसर्गे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्वनहसोरनुपसर्गयोरौ अप्यस्यो भवति ॥

62. The affix 'ap' comes optionally after the verbs 'svan' and 'has' when no upasarga is in composition with them.

Thus स्वनः or स्वानः 'sound'; हसः or हासः 'laughter'. But with upasargas, we have only one form; मस्वानः 'a loud noise'; महासः 'a loud laughter'.

यमः समुपनिविषु च ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ यमः, सम्-उप-नि-विषु,

च, (अनुपसर्गे, वा, अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सम् उप नि वि इत्येतैषुपपवेषु अनुपसर्गेऽपि यमेयो अप्यस्यो भवति ॥

63. And the affix 'ap' comes optionally after the verb 'yam', when the upasargas 'sam', 'upa', 'ni' and 'vi' are in composition; or even when it is upasarga-less.

This debars घञ्. As संयमः or संयमः 'restraint'; उपयमः or उपयमः 'marriage'; नियमः or नियमः 'restrictive rule'; विद्यमः or विद्यमः 'check, distress'; यामः or यमः ।

नै। गदनदपठस्वनः ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ नै।, गद्-नद्-पठ-स्वनः,

(अप्, वा) ॥

BK. III. CH. III. § 64-67.] THE AFFIX AP.

507

वृत्तिः ॥ निःशब्द उपपदे गह नः पद स्वन इत्येतेभ्यो धातुभ्यो वा अपयस्थ्यो भवति ॥

64. The affix 'ap' comes optionally after the verbs 'gad' (to speak), 'nad' (to sound), 'path' (to read), 'svan' (to sound), when the upasarga 'ni' is in composition with them.

This debars घम्. Thus निगहः or निगाहः 'recitation'; निनदः or निनादः 'noise'; निपदः or निपादः 'reading'; निस्तनः or निस्तनः 'a noise'.

कृशो वीशायां च ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृशः, वीशायाम्, च, (नौ, वा, अनुपसर्गे, अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृशो धीतोर्निर्वृत्ति सुपसर्गाच्च वीशायां वा अपयस्थ्यो भवति ॥

65. The affix 'ap' comes optionally after the verb 'kvan' (to jingle), when 'ni' is in composition with it, as well as when it is without any upasarga, or when 'flute' is meant.

This debars the affix घम्. Thus निकृष्टः or निक्राणः 'a musical tone'. कृशः or क्राणः 'sound'. When it refers to 'flute', it must have some upasarga not necessarily नि; as कर्तव्याप्यकृशो वीशा.

But not so here, अतिक्राणो वर्तते, where the upasarga being अति and the word not referring to 'a flute', no option is allowed. When flute is not meant the upasarga must be नि or no upasarga at all, for the optional application of the affix अप्. To sum up, कर्तव्य takes अप् optionally under three conditions:—1st when preceded by नि, or 2ndly when having no upasarga, or 3rdly when it refers to 'flute', and then it must have some upasarga.

नित्यं पशः परिमाशे ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ नित्यं, पशः, परिमाशे, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पण्ड व्यवहारे स्तुतौ च, अस्माद्वातोर्निरूपयस्थ्यो भवति परिमाणे गन्धमाने ॥

66. The affix 'ap' comes invariably after the verb 'pan' (to barter), when the sense is that of measure.

The word नित्यं 'invariably' is used in the aphorism in order to stop the anuvritti of the word optionally. Thus मूलकपण्डः 'a handful of radishes'; शाकपण्डः 'a handful of vegetable'. These words secondarily have come to mean 'a measure equal to a handful', irrespective of any thing.

When not meaning measure, we have पाण्डः 'trade'.

सदोऽनुपसर्गे ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सदः, अनुपसर्गे, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मदेधीतोर्नुपसर्गापयस्थ्यो भवति ॥

67. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'mad', when not in composition with an upasarga.

41

508

THE AFFIX AP. [BK. III. CH. III. § 68-70.

This debars घञ्. As विद्यमहः 'pride of knowledge'; घनमहः 'pride of wealth'; कुलमहः 'pride of family'. When compounded with upasargas, we have उन्मादः 'mad'; प्रमादः 'error or carelessness'.

प्रसदसमन्दी हर्षे ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रमद-समन्दी, हर्षे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रमद समद इरवेती शब्दो निपास्यते हर्षेऽनिषेधे ॥

68. The words 'pramada' and 'sammada' are irregularly formed, meaning 'joy'.

As कन्यानां प्रमदः 'the joy of girls'; कोकिलानां समदः 'the rejoicing of cuckoos'.

Why do we say 'when meaning delight'? Observe प्रमादः 'carelessness';

समादः 'frenzy'.

Instead of saying 'the verb *mad* preceded by *pra* and *sam* takes the affix *ap*' which also would have given the above forms, the full forms have been used in the *sūtra* to indicate that these words are रूढे in this sense; for the sense of the root is not visible in these words.

समुदोरजः पशुषु ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ सम-उदोः, अजः, पशुषु, (अप) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ समुदोरपरदशोरजतेर्द्वीतोः पशुविषये भास्यधःप्रस्ययो भवति ॥

69. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'aj' (to go), when the prepositions 'sam' and 'ut' are in composition, and the word so formed refers to beasts.

This debars घञ्. The root अज 'means to go, to throw'. When preceded by सम, it means 'a collection'; and preceded by उत् it means 'driving'. As समजः पशूनां 'a herd of cattle'; उदजः पशूनां 'driving forth of cattle'.

Why do we say 'when applying to cattle'? Observe समजो ब्राह्मणानां, उदजः क्षत्रियाणां ।

अज्ञेषु ग्लहः ॥ ७० ॥ पदानि ॥ अज्ञेषु, ग्लहः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ग्लह इति निपास्यते अज्ञविषयश्चेद्वात्स्वयो भवति ॥

70. The word 'glaha' is irregularly formed, when the sense of the root refers to gambling.

This word is derived from the root यह. The verb यह takes the affix अप and thus forms यह; and then irregularly र is changed into ल; as अज्ञस्य ग्लहः 'cast of the dice'.

Why do we say 'when referring to gambling'? Observe 'यहः पादस्य ।

Others say, this word is derived regularly from the root ग्लह 'to gamble', by adding the affix अप, and thus debarring घञ्. They suppose, therefore, the existence of the root ग्लह to explain the form ग्लहः । The counter-example which they would give, is ग्लाहः 'receiving', formed by adding the affix घञ् ।

BK. III. CH. III. § 71-74] THE AFFIX AP.

509

प्रजने सर्तेः ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रजने, सर्तेः, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्तेः ॥ प्रजने विषयं अप्प्रत्ययौ भवति ॥

71. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'sri' (to flow), in the sense of impregnating (the covering of cows &c).

This debars घञ्. The word प्रजने means 'the first covering of a cow by a bull'. As गवामुपसरः 'impregnation of cows'; पश्चानुपसरः 'impregnation of cattle'.

हवः संप्रसारणं च न्यम्पुपविषु ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ हवः, संप्रसारणम्, च, नि-अभि-उप-विषु, (अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नि अभि उप वि इत्येतेषु उपपवेषु हृदयतेऽर्थातोः संप्रसारणम् अप्प्रत्ययौ भवति ॥

72. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'hve' (to call), when the preposition 'ni' 'abhi' 'upa' and 'vi' are in composition with it, and its semivowel is changed into the corresponding vowel.

This debars घञ्. As नि+हवे+अप्=नि+हु+अ(VI. I. 108)=नि+हो+अ(VII. 3. 84)=निहव (VI. I. 78) 'invocation'; अभिहवः 'invocation'; उपहवः 'invitation'; विहवः 'calling'. But प्रहावः 'a summons'.

आडि युद्धे ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ आडि, युद्धे, (हवः, संप्रसारणं, अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आह्व उपपवे हृदयतेऽर्थातोः संप्रसारणम् प्रत्ययौ भवति युद्धेऽभिषये ॥

73. The affix 'ap' comes after the verb 'hve' when the word in composition is the upasarga 'ān', and the semi-vowel of the root is changed into its corresponding vowel, when the word so formed means battle.

As आह्वः 'battle' (where they challenge each other). But otherwise आह्वाः 'calling'.

निपाननाह्वाः ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ निपानम्, आह्वाः, (आडि, हवः, संप्रसारणम्, अप्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आह्वपूर्वस्य हृदयतेऽर्थातोः संप्रसारणम् प्रत्ययौ वृद्धिश्च निपान्यते निपानं चेदभिषये भवति ॥

74. The word 'āhāva' is irregularly formed when meaning a trough.
